declarations.heading: Setting and semantic cycle completion
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}
A \emph{complete atomic symmetric binary language} consists of a finite
set $\mathcal D$ of irreflexive symmetric binary relation symbols, each
with its own name, in addition to logical equality. In any finite
structure under consideration, each pair of distinct vertices has
exactly one colour $a\in\mathcal D$. A \emph{triangle table} specifies
which colour triples occur on three distinct vertices. A \emph{triangle-defined
age} contains exactly the finite complete colourings whose every
three-vertex substructure is allowed by the table.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Semantic homomorphic CCO
declarations.heading: Setting and semantic cycle completion
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Semantic homomorphic CCO]
A class $\mathcal K=\Age(M)$ has \emph{semantic homomorphic CCO} if every
finite partial diagram $P$ with the property that each of its specified
simple cycles admits a colour-preserving homomorphism into $M$ itself
admits a colour-preserving homomorphism $P\to M$.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Ordinary EPPA
declarations.heading: Setting and semantic cycle completion
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Ordinary EPPA]
A class of finite structures has the \emph{extension property for partial
automorphisms} if for every $A$ in the class there is a finite $B$ in
the class containing $A$ such that \emph{every} isomorphism between
induced substructures of $A$ extends to an automorphism of $B$.
One common $B$ must work for all such maps. No coherent choice of these
extensions is required.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: AP and semantic homomorphic CCO imply triangle fullness
declarations.heading: Stationary independence.
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[AP and semantic homomorphic CCO imply triangle fullness]
\label{lem:cco-triangle-fullness}
Let $\mathcal K$ be a hereditary class of finite complete atomic
binary-coloured structures with AP and semantic homomorphic CCO.  If
all induced substructures of a finite complete $A$ on at most three
vertices belong to $\mathcal K$, then $A\in\mathcal K$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Stationary independence.

declarations.heading: Stationary independence.
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}
The lemma does not claim that a \emph{partial} triangle-consistent
diagram completes.  It uses the actual chord colours of the
\emph{complete} input in the cycle-fan amalgams.  In our homogeneous
source AP is automatic, so triangle-definedness is a consequence of
semantic homomorphic CCO, not an extra substantive assumption.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Sparse labelled graph
declarations.heading: Sparse labelled graphs
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Sparse labelled graph]\label{lem:sparse-labelled-graph}
For all positive integers \(q,r,g\) there is a finite simple graph \(H\),
whose edges are labelled by \(1,\ldots,r\), with girth greater than \(g\),
such that every colouring
\(\kappa:V(H)\to\{1,\ldots,q\}\) has a colour \(d\) with the following
property: for every label \(i\leq r\), some edge labelled \(i\) has both
endpoints coloured \(d\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Uniform local finiteness of real algebraic closure
declarations.heading: Finite CCO structures have only binary Hasse covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Uniform local finiteness of real algebraic closure]
\label{cor:fibre-uniform-acl}
Let $d=|\mathcal D|$. For every nonempty finite real set
$A\subseteq M$ of size $n$, all finite one-point fibres over $A$
have cardinality $2^m$ for some $0\le m\le d$, and
\[
             |\operatorname{acl}_M(A)|\le n+d^n 2^d.
\]
In particular, real algebraic closure is locally finite with a
bound depending only on $n$ and the named palette. If $A$ is empty,
then $\operatorname{acl}_M(A)$ is empty for infinite $M$, while for
finite $M$ its cardinality is a power of two at most $2^d$.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Full typed exact calculus and heterogeneous ball Helly
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Full typed exact calculus and heterogeneous ball Helly]
\label{thm:full-typed-exact-balls}
The following common statement also applies when the original source
has several \emph{named}, individually transitive sorts. Let $N$ be a
countable homogeneous structure in a finite complete atomic binary
language whose same-sort
colours are symmetric and whose cross-sort colours come in typed
converse pairs. Assume semantic homomorphic CCO; SAP is \emph{not}
required. In this theorem products are the \emph{actual represented}
relations, and the palette for a loop sort includes its logical
identity atom.

For each ordered original sort pair $(i,j)$, let
$\mathcal W_{ij}$ consist of the nonempty represented atomic word
profiles, with intermediate sorts arbitrary, and let
$\mathcal H^{\rm full}_{ij}$ consist of their nonempty finite
intersections, including the full typed top as the empty intersection.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item The family $\mathcal W_{ij}$ is $2$-Helly. So is
$\mathcal H^{\rm full}_{ij}$; the latter is closed under
nonempty meets and typed converse.
\item For nonempty $D=\bigcap_\alpha P_\alpha$ and
$F=\bigcap_\beta Q_\beta$ of matching types,
\[
  D;F=\bigcap_{\alpha,\beta}(P_\alpha;Q_\beta),
\]
with a typed top treated as an empty list of restrictions. The
product is nonempty and full exact, and products distribute over
nonempty finite exact meets in either argument.
\item Fix a target original sort $u$. For actual centres
$b_1,\ldots,b_n$ in \emph{arbitrary} named sorts $t_i$ and
nonempty $D_i\in\mathcal H^{\rm full}_{u,t_i}$, put
\[
  B_{D_i}(b_i)=\{z\in N_u:(z,b_i)\in D_i\}.
\]
If these balls intersect pairwise, then all of them intersect;
repeated centres and identity-bearing menus are permitted. In
particular, their pairwise-intersection test is
\[
 B_{D_i}(b_i)\cap B_{D_j}(b_j)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (b_i,b_j)\in\bar D_i;D_j.
\]
\end{enumerate}
These are full (identity-aware) statements, \emph{not} assertions
about the strong diversity-only guarded product on distinct points.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Full typed exact saturation commutes with nonempty meets
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full typed exact saturation commutes with nonempty meets]
\label{lem:full-typed-exact-saturation}
Let $a,b$ be named transitive original sorts.
Let $E_a$ and $E_b$ be full exact invariant
equivalences on them, and let
$D_1,\ldots,D_m\subseteq L_{ab}$ be
nonempty full exact typed relations with
\[
                    D=\bigcap_{i=1}^mD_i\ne\varnothing.
\]
All products are \emph{actual represented},
including equality on same-sort endpoint types.
Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 E_a;D;E_b=\bigcap_{i=1}^m(E_a;D_i;E_b).
 \quad}\tag{ES}\label{eq:foundational-exact-saturation}
\]
In particular the right-hand side is a
nonempty full exact relation. For an
empty index family take $D=L_{ab}$;
both sides are the full typed top.

The nonempty-intersection assumption is
essential: no preservation of arbitrary
empty exact intersections is asserted.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Word-profile Helly and exact product calculus
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Word-profile Helly and exact product calculus]
\label{lem:exact-product}
For nonempty word profiles $P_1,\dots,P_m$ whose pairwise
intersections are nonempty, the total intersection is nonempty.
Consequently the nonempty exact supports enjoy the same $2$-Helly
property (flatten all their word presentations: pairwise
intersection of the exact supports implies pairwise intersection
of every selected pair of words) and are closed under product; more precisely, if
$E=\bigcap_iP_i\ne\varnothing$ and
$F=\bigcap_jQ_j\ne\varnothing$, then
\[
 E\,a=\bigcap_i(P_i a),\qquad
 EF=\bigcap_{i,j}(P_iQ_j),
\]
where $a$ is an atomic relation and the empty defining families
receive their evident $\Top$ convention.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Exact-ball Helly with different centres
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact-ball Helly with different centres]\label{lem:exact-balls}
Let $x_1,\dots,x_m\in M$ and let $R_1,\dots,R_m$ be exact relations.
If $R_i[x_i]\cap R_j[x_j]\ne\varnothing$ for every $i,j$, then
$\bigcap_iR_i[x_i]\ne\varnothing$. Moreover
\[
 R_i[x_i]\cap R_j[x_j]\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (x_i,x_j)\in R_iR_j.
\]
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Why exactness is essential for ball Helly
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Why exactness is essential for ball Helly]
\label{ex:exact-ball-sharp}
Let $V=\mathbb F_2^2$, and for every nonzero $\delta\in V$ name the
symmetric diversity colour $a_\delta(x,y)$ given by $y-x=\delta$.
The resulting four-point structure is transitive and homogeneous:
all finite partial colour isomorphisms are restrictions of
translations.  Its age is triangle-defined (the three differences
around each legal triangle sum to zero), has AP, and has semantic
homomorphic CCO: a labelled partial graph maps to $V$ precisely
when the edge differences sum to zero on every specified cycle.
Choose independent $e_1,e_2\in V$ and put
\[
 A_1=\Id\cup a_{e_1},\qquad A_2=\Id\cup a_{e_2},
 \qquad A_3=a_{e_1}\cup a_{e_2}.
\]
The three balls with common centre $0$ are respectively
$\{0,e_1\}$, $\{0,e_2\}$, and $\{e_1,e_2\}$.
They intersect pairwise but have empty total intersection.
These supports are invariant, but are \emph{not} exact: every
word profile is one difference atom (including $\Id$), so every
nonempty exact support is either one atom or $\Top$.
Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-balls} cannot be applied to arbitrary
invariant supports in place of exact ones.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Actual exact quotient sorts
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Actual exact quotient sorts]
Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite family of invariant \emph{exact}
equivalence relations, including $\Id$. The many-sorted expansion
$M_{\mathcal E}$ has one formal sort $M/J$ for each
$J\in\mathcal E$, with all actual binary orbits under
$\Aut(M)$ named on each ordered pair of sorts. The real sort is
$M/\Id$. For $J,K\in\mathcal E$ and a raw atom $a$ represented
by a pair of classes, the inverse image of that typed pair orbit
in $M^2$ is $JaK$; these saturated relations partition $M^2$.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Fine colours from finitely many exact quotients
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Fine colours from finitely many exact quotients]
\label{lem:exact-quotient-colour-meet}
In the one-original-sort setting of
\cref{thm:full-typed-exact-balls}, let $E_1,\ldots,E_m$, $m\ge1$,
be invariant full exact equivalences on $M$, and put
$K=\bigcap_i E_i$. For every original raw atomic orbital $a$,
including logical equality,
\[
             \bigcap_{i=1}^m E_i;a;E_i=K;a;K.
\]
Consequently the actual pair orbital of two $K$-classes is
determined by the pair orbitals of all their $E_i$-projections.
This includes coincident quotient coordinates; when $K=\Id$,
it recovers the original fine colour. No assertion that arbitrary
compatible tuples are realised is part of this lemma.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Representative-independent lifting of exact-sort cycles
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Representative-independent lifting of exact-sort cycles]
\label{lem:exact-cycle-lift}
Let $C$ be a specified simple cycle of a finite partial diagram in
$M_{\mathcal E}$, and suppose it has a typed homomorphism into
$M_{\mathcal E}$.  For each typed edge $uv$, choose a finite
word-profile presentation of the inverse image of its named pair
orbital and replace that edge by private raw paths spelling its
words.  Then the expanded raw diagram has a homomorphism into
$M$, even after arbitrary representatives of the images of all the
marked quotient vertices have been fixed.  The same conclusion
holds for two private paths representing the same nonempty typed
pair orbital.  Identity factors inside words are suppressed.  An empty-word
condition means logical equality of its real endpoints and is
handled by their identification; for a legal edge between distinct
typed vertices its nonempty orbital pullback cannot be contained in
$\Id$, so this case does not arise during the CCO expansion.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Mixed exact-sort orbitals factor through their join
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Mixed exact-sort orbitals factor through their join]
\label{lem:acf-mixed-exact-join}
Let \(E,H\) be TWO arbitrary invariant full exact
equivalences of the ACTUAL original one-sort
symmetric homogeneous source \(M\), possibly
incomparable, and put \(J=E\vee H\).
For any old raw atomic orbital \(a\), including
logical equality, the inverse image of the
actual mixed pair orbital on
\((M/E)\times(M/H)\) represented by \(a\)
is
\[
 \boxed{\quad
       E;a;H=J;a;J=J;a=a;J.
       \quad}
\tag{MEJ}\label{eq:acf-mixed-exact-join}
\]
Thus the mixed orbital of an \(E\)-class
and an \(H\)-class depends ONLY on the
orbital of their projected pair in the
COMMON quotient \(M/J\). In particular,
if finite partial automorphisms of sets
of \(E\)- and \(H\)-classes induce the
SAME partial automorphism on their
common \(J\)-quotient and separately
preserve the within-sort pair orbitals,
then their union preserves ALL mixed
binary orbitals of these two exact sorts.
The statement concerns a JOINT finite
partial isomorphism and does not claim
a global group-theoretic section.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Nested exact-sort mixed orbit collapse
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Nested exact-sort mixed orbit collapse]
\label{lem:nested-mixed}
Let $J\le K$ be invariant exact equivalences of the actual real
source, including the case $J=\Id$, and let $a$ be any actual raw
atom (possibly equality).  The inverse image of the mixed pair
orbital from $M/J$ to $M/K$ represented by $a$ is
\[
          JaK=KaK=aK.
\]
Consequently the mixed pair orbit of $([x]_J,d)$, with
$d\in M/K$, is determined solely by the pair orbit of
$([x]_K,d)$ in $M/K$.  More generally, let $p$ be a finite partial
isomorphism of $M/J$ and $\gamma$ a finite partial isomorphism
of $M/K$, with $[x]_K$ in the domain of $\gamma$ whenever
$[x]_J$ lies in the domain of $p$.  If
\[
             \pi_{J,K}(p([x]_J))
                 =\gamma(\pi_{J,K}([x]_J))
\]
for each such $[x]_J$, then the union of $p$ and $\gamma$ is a
partial isomorphism of the joint two-sort orbital structure.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Typed joint lifting for finitely many original exact quotients
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Typed joint lifting for finitely many original exact quotients]
\label{thm:typed-joint-exact-lifting}
Let $N$ be a countable homogeneous finite complete typed binary
structure satisfying the hypotheses of
\cref{thm:full-typed-exact-balls}.  For each original named
transitive sort $s$, choose finitely many invariant \emph{full exact}
equivalences $J$ on $N_s$, with $\Id_s$ included.
Form the many-sorted structure $N_{\mathcal J}$ whose sorts are
all the $N_s/J$ (identifying $N_s/\Id_s$ with the original real
sort $N_s$) and whose binary relations name \emph{all actual}
$\Aut(N)$-pair orbitals between the indicated sorts.
Then every finite partial isomorphism of $N_{\mathcal J}$ is
induced by an automorphism of the original $N$, acting on its
actual quotient classes.  No functorial choice of such lifts or
group-theoretic section is asserted.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts

declarations.title: Equivariant unary enrichment preserves joint exact lifting
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Equivariant unary enrichment preserves joint exact lifting]
\label{cor:typed-joint-exact-equivariant-unary}
In the setting of
\cref{thm:typed-joint-exact-lifting}, add any
finite family of ACTUAL $\Aut(N)$-equivariant
unary functions between the already named
original real or exact quotient sorts.
The resulting many-sorted structure is
ultrahomogeneous: EVERY finite partial
isomorphism of its finite functionally
closed induced substructures extends to
an automorphism INDUCED BY ONE original
$g\in\Aut(N)$.

This applies to actually defined
old-real quotient projections, upward
maps of represented quotient classes,
and mixed-original-sort named quotient
transports whenever their two actual
quotient sorts occur in the chosen list.
It does NOT imply SAP for the resulting
hereditary unary-closed age, nor permit
naming arbitrary NONEXACT quotient sorts.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Triangle fullness, AP and CCO of exact sorts
declarations.heading: Represented exact relations and exact quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Triangle fullness, AP and CCO of exact sorts]
\label{thm:exact-sorts-source}
The many-sorted age $\Age(M_{\mathcal E})$ is described by its legal
typed binary triangles, has AP, and satisfies semantic homomorphic
CCO. In particular every individual actual exact quotient, in its
named binary orbital language, inherits the standing source
properties (with any relevant transitivity checked in that sort).
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Finite-set orbit avoidance
declarations.heading: Finite avoidance for group actions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite-set orbit avoidance]
\label{lem:finite-action-avoidance}
Let $G$ be a group acting on a (possibly disjointly sorted)
set $X$.  Suppose every point of a finite set $A\subseteq X$
has an infinite $G$-orbit, and let $Z\subseteq X$ be any
finite forbidden set.  Then there exists ONE $g\in G$ with
\[
                         g(A)\cap Z=\varnothing.
\]
The assertion includes $A=\varnothing$ or $Z=\varnothing$;
no topology, model theory, or faithfulness of the action is
required.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite avoidance for group actions

declarations.title: Point-generated SAP iff no off-closure coordinate algebraicity
declarations.heading: Point-generated bases in a canonical coordinate expansion
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Point-generated SAP iff no off-closure coordinate algebraicity]
\label{lem:typed-point-generated-sap-criterion}
Let $M$ be a homogeneous complete structure on its original
named real sorts.  Let $\widehat M$ be an ACTUAL canonical
equivariant interpreted expansion by named unary coordinate
maps and their finite compositions, with every hidden vertex
some real-source unary-term value.  Assume every finite real
$D$ has finite FULL point-generated unary closure
$\widehat D$, and all hidden relations are interpreted
canonically from $M$.  There are no extra zero-ary generators.

The category of finite COMPLETE INDUCED point-generated hidden
structures $\widehat P$ has SAP over its full point-generated
common bases (including the empty base) if and only if
\[
 \text{for every finite real }D\subseteq M
 \text{ and }u\in\widehat M\setminus\widehat D,\quad
             |\Aut(M/D)\cdot u|=\infty.
 \tag{PGO}\label{eq:typed-point-generated-sap-criterion}
\]
This criterion does NOT assert SAP over an arbitrary
NON-point-generated hereditary hidden base with orphan vertices.
It uses no CCO, symmetry or exact multiplication.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Point-generated bases in a canonical coordinate expansion

declarations.title: Hereditary SAP iff no algebraicity outside unary closure
declarations.heading: The hereditary age of a homogeneous unary structure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Hereditary SAP iff no algebraicity outside unary closure]
\label{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}
Let $H$ be a countable HOMOGENEOUS many-sorted
structure whose only named functions are UNARY
(total on their specified source sorts), with no
additional nullary generators.  Assume that
the closure $\cl_H(T)$ of EVERY finite set
under all named unary functions is finite.
Then its age of finite induced functionally
closed substructures has strong amalgamation
if and only if, for EVERY finite $T\subseteq H$,
\[
             \operatorname{acl}_H(T)=\cl_H(T),
 \tag{UA}\label{eq:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}
\]
where algebraicity is defined by finite
orbits of the pointwise automorphism stabiliser.
In that event also
$\operatorname{dcl}_H(T)=\cl_H(T)$.
This criterion applies to a HEREDITARY unary
age; it is not restricted to point-generated
objects or to purely relational reducts.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: The hereditary age of a homogeneous unary structure

declarations.title: Fresh frames and closed-base orbit infinitude
declarations.heading: Transferring orbit infinitude through real frames
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Fresh frames and closed-base orbit infinitude]
\label{lem:foundational-real-frame-orbits}
Let $H$ be a many-sorted structure whose named functions are unary,
total on their specified source sorts, with no nullary generators.
Assume every finite set has finite unary closure. Let $G\le\Aut(H)$,
and let $R$ be a $G$-invariant union of real sorts generating all of $H$
under unary terms. Suppose that for every finite $D\subseteq R$ and
$u\notin\cl_H(D)$, the orbit $G_D\cdot u$ is infinite, where $G_D$
is the pointwise stabiliser. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every finite unary-closed $A\subseteq B\subseteq H$ there is
  a finite $D\subseteq R$ with
  $A\subseteq\cl_H(D)$ and $\cl_H(D)\cap B=A$.
\item For every finite unary-closed $A\subseteq H$ and $u\notin A$,
  the orbit $G_A\cdot u$ is infinite.
\end{enumerate}
For an arbitrary finite hidden $T$, condition (ii) also says that the
points with finite $G_T$-orbit are exactly $\cl_H(T)$; every point of
that closure is fixed by $G_T$. No homogeneity or SAP is assumed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Transferring orbit infinitude through real frames

declarations.title: Fresh real frames and hereditary hidden SAP
declarations.heading: Transferring orbit infinitude through real frames
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Fresh real frames and hereditary hidden SAP]
\label{rem:typed-fresh-frame-iff-sap}
Suppose $H$ satisfies the structural hypotheses of
\cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}, is generated by a union $R$
of named real sorts, and satisfies
$\operatorname{acl}_H(D)=\cl_H(D)$ for every finite real $D$.
Then the following are equivalent: fresh-frame separation as in
\cref{lem:foundational-real-frame-orbits}(i);
$\operatorname{acl}_H(T)=\cl_H(T)$ for every finite hidden $T$;
and SAP of the entire hereditary unary-closed age.
Indeed apply the preceding lemma with $G=\Aut(H)$, followed by
\cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}. No CCO, quotient-lattice
geometry or functorial choice of representatives is required. For a
proper subgroup $G$, the preceding lemma retains the stronger statement
about its actual stabiliser orbits; SAP alone is not asserted to imply
that subgroup statement.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Quotient-fibre avoidance with named forced values
declarations.heading: Finite avoidance within an actual quotient fibre
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Quotient-fibre avoidance with named forced values]
\label{lem:foundational-quotient-fibre-avoidance}
Let $H$ have unary functions, total on their specified source sorts,
no nullary generators, and finite singleton unary closures. Let
$G\le\Aut(H)$ act transitively on a named real sort $M$, and let
$p_J:M\to Q$ be a named surjective equivariant quotient projection
with actual kernel $J>\Id_M$. For every well-sorted real-source unary
term $\tau:M\to H_s$, let $K_\tau$ be its actual kernel. Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $J\le K_\tau$, then $\tau=\sigma\circ p_J$ for an actual
  named unary term $\sigma:Q\to H_s$.
\item If $J\nleq K_\tau$, then $[J:J\cap K_\tau]=\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
For every $b\in Q$ and every finite forbidden set $Z\subseteq H$,
there is one $x\in p_J^{-1}(b)$ such that every unforced term
($J\nleq K_\tau$) satisfies $\tau(x)\notin Z$. Every forced value
is the prescribed $\sigma(b)\in\cl_H(\{b\})$. In particular
\[
             \cl_H(\{x\})\cap Z=\cl_H(\{b\})\cap Z,
             \qquad x\notin Z.
\]
The choices can be made successively for any finite list of such
quotient vertices, possibly on different transitive real sorts: at each
step the forbidden set may include any extra finite hidden set, all
earlier representatives and all earlier unforced term values. Thus the
real representatives can be pairwise distinct while all forced values
are retained.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite avoidance within an actual quotient fibre

declarations.title: Relative-kernel criterion for fresh frames and hereditary SAP
declarations.heading: The relative-kernel criterion and its converse
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Relative-kernel criterion for fresh frames and hereditary SAP]
\label{thm:typed-abstract-fresh-frame-sap}
Let $G$ act transitively on each of finitely many named original real
sorts $M_a$. Let $H$ be a countable homogeneous oligomorphic many-sorted
structure in a finite named language, with arbitrary relations and only
unary functions total on their specified source sorts, no nullary
generators, and finite unary closures of finite sets. Assume
$G\le\Aut(H)$ preserves all named sorts, predicates and functions.
The singleton closures on the finitely many transitive real sorts are
then uniformly bounded; no uniform bound independent of the number
of generators is required. We use orbit-theoretic $\acl_H$ as in
\cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}.

Every nonreal hidden vertex is assumed to have a representation
$p_J(x)=[x]_J$ for some named surjective equivariant quotient projection
$p_J:M_a\to Q_{a,J}$, where $J>\Id_a$ is an actual $G$-invariant
equivalence. For every such $J$ and every named real-source unary
term $\tau:M_a\to H_s$ with kernel $K_\tau$, assume the exact dichotomy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $J\le K_\tau$, then $\tau=\sigma\circ p_J$ for an actual
  named unary term $\sigma:Q_{a,J}\to H_s$.
\item If $J\nleq K_\tau$, then $[J:J\cap K_\tau]=\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Finally assume that for every finite original real $D$ and every
$u\notin\cl_H(D)$, the orbit $\Aut(H/D)\cdot u$ is infinite.

Then for every finite induced unary-closed $A\subseteq B\subseteq H$
there is a finite original real $D$ such that
\[
       A\subseteq\cl_H(D),\qquad \cl_H(D)\cap B=A.
\tag{AFF}\label{eq:typed-abstract-fresh-frame}
\]
Consequently $\acl_H(T)=\operatorname{dcl}_H(T)=\cl_H(T)$ for every
finite hidden $T$, and the entire hereditary age of finite unary-closed
substructures of $H$ has SAP.

This criterion assumes no original CCO, triangle geometry, lattice
distributivity or old SAP. In the terminal application those conditions
supply the named quotient signature, kernel dichotomy and real-base
orbit condition separately. Kernel inclusion alone cannot replace the
literal named factorisation in (i).
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: The relative-kernel criterion and its converse

declarations.title: Exact abstract relative-kernel characterisation of unary hereditary SAP
declarations.heading: The relative-kernel criterion and its converse
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Exact abstract relative-kernel characterisation of unary hereditary SAP]
\label{cor:typed-abstract-relative-kernel-sap-iff}
Keep the structural hypotheses on $G$, the original transitive real
sorts, $H$, its finite unary closures and named surjective quotient
representations from \cref{thm:typed-abstract-fresh-frame-sap}, without
assuming its kernel dichotomy or real-base orbit property. Then the
following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The entire hereditary age of finite induced unary-closed
  substructures of $H$ has SAP.
\item For every finite original real $D$, $\acl_H(D)=\cl_H(D)$;
  and for every named quotient $p_J:M_a\to Q_{a,J}$ and every actual
  named real-source unary term $\tau:M_a\to H_s$ with kernel $K_\tau$,
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 J\le K_\tau:
  &\exists\text{ named unary term }\sigma:
        \tau=\sigma\circ p_J,\\[2pt]
 J\nleq K_\tau:
  &[J:J\cap K_\tau]=\infty.
\end{array}
\tag{RK}\label{eq:typed-abstract-kernel-iff}
\]
\end{enumerate}
The forward direction needs no separate original CCO, SAP, exact-lattice
or real-base orbit input. The two failure mechanisms are local to one
quotient fibre: a missing named factorisation for an existing forced
real-source term gives a definable off-closure value, while a finite
proper relative index for an existing term kernel gives an algebraic
off-closure value. The quantification over actual named terms is essential.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: The relative-kernel criterion and its converse

declarations.title: Collision unfolding
declarations.heading: Collision unfolding under strong amalgamation
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Collision unfolding]\label{lem:collision-unfolding}
Let $A$ be a finite PARTIAL relational structure, and let
$h:A\to U$ be a homomorphism-embedding into a countable homogeneous
relational structure $U$ whose age has SAP. Suppose $h$ is
injective on every member of a fixed finite family of
distinguished COMPLETE induced substructures of $A$.
Then $h$ can be replaced by an INJECTIVE homomorphism-embedding
$h':A\to U$ preserving the complete induced isomorphism type
of the image of EACH distinguished substructure.

No unary-functional closure, CCO, exactness or original
binary-language assumption is used; the statement concerns
the full displayed relational supports of the partial source.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Collision unfolding under strong amalgamation

declarations.title: Finite elementary-$2$ translate Helly is affine
declarations.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite elementary-$2$ translate Helly is affine]
\label{lem:foundational-affine-translate-helly}
Let $V$ be a finite elementary abelian $2$-group and
$\varnothing\ne A\subseteq V$. Suppose every finite family
of pairwise-intersecting translates $A+v$ has nonempty
total intersection. Then $A$ is an affine coset of a
subgroup of $V$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems

declarations.title: Exact binary finite-fibre kernel and compact projection
declarations.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact binary finite-fibre kernel and compact projection]
\label{thm:finite-fibre-kernel-csp}
The full pointwise-owner kernel is
\[
 \boxed{\quad N=
   \{(h_C)_{C\in\mathcal C}\in\prod_CH_C:
             (h_C,h_D)\in H_{CD}\ \forall C\ne D\}.
   \quad}\tag{FC1}\label{eq:finite-kernel-binary}
\]
For every finite $S\subseteq\mathcal C$ and tuple
$g\in\prod_{C\in S}H_C$,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 g\in\operatorname{pr}_S(N)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \text{for every finite }T\supseteq S
 \text{ there is }h\in\operatorname{Sol}(T)
 \text{ with }h|_S=g.
 \quad}\tag{FC2}\label{eq:finite-kernel-projection}
\]
In particular the actual binding groups
$B_C=\operatorname{pr}_C(N)$ and actual pair images
$P_{CD}=\operatorname{pr}_{C,D}(N)\le B_C\times B_D$
satisfy
\[
 N=\{(b_C)\in\prod_CB_C:
                (b_C,b_D)\in P_{CD}\ \forall C\ne D\}.
 \tag{FC3}\label{eq:finite-kernel-actual-pairs}
\]
Every $P_{CD}$ is subdirect over $B_C,B_D$, but
$B_C$ may be strictly smaller than $H_C$, and
\emph{finite} projections $\operatorname{pr}_S(N)$
need not equal the solution set of just the pairs
within $S$.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems

declarations.title: Relative homogeneity removes hidden projections
declarations.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Relative homogeneity removes hidden projections]
\label{cor:finite-kernel-relative-homogeneity}
Let $X^{\mathrm{own}}$ expand $X$ by naming
\emph{every} finite $F$-class $C$ with its own
unary predicate. If $X^{\mathrm{own}}$ is
homogeneous, then for every finite $S$,
\[
             \operatorname{pr}_S(N)
                         =\operatorname{Sol}(S).
 \tag{FC4}\label{eq:finite-kernel-strong-projection}
\]
Consequently $B_C=H_C$ and $P_{CD}=H_{CD}$.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems

declarations.title: Linear dual invariant for elementary abelian kernels
declarations.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Linear dual invariant for elementary abelian kernels]
\label{thm:finite-kernel-linear-width-two}
Assume every intrinsic finite fibre motion group
$H_C$ is elementary abelian, written as a finite
$\mathbb F_2$-vector space $V_C$. Let
\[
 D=\bigoplus_{C\in\mathcal C}V_C^*
\]
be the space of finitely supported linear tests,
and let $R\le D$ be the span of all linear
equations defining the actual local pair
subgroups $H_{CD}$ (unary equations are
allowed as tests supported on one coordinate).
Then
\[
 N=R^\perp\subseteq\prod_CV_C,\qquad
 \operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{pr}_S N)=
                       R\cap D_S
 \tag{FC5}\label{eq:finite-kernel-dual}
\]
for every finite $S$, where
$D_S=\bigoplus_{C\in S}V_C^*$. In particular
\[
 \operatorname{pr}_S(N)
 =\{x\in\prod_{C\in S}B_C:
     (x_C,x_D)\in P_{CD}\quad(C\ne D)\}
\]
holds precisely when
\[
 R\cap D_S=
 \operatorname{span}\{
        R\cap D_T:T\subseteq S,\ |T|\le2\}.
 \tag{FC6}\label{eq:finite-kernel-width-two}
\]
The condition on the right concerns
\emph{projected finite motions}, not the
global pair-CSP representation, which always
holds.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems

declarations.title: The hidden-parity obstruction and exact-owner firewall
declarations.heading: Finite packet kernels as binary constraint systems
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The hidden-parity obstruction and exact-owner firewall]
\label{rem:finite-kernel-hidden-parity}
The finite group in four named phase sets
$A=B=C=\mathbb F_2$, $D=\mathbb F_2^2$
defined by shifts $(u,v,u+v,(u,v))$ has
unrestricted two-coordinate marginals on
$A,B,C$, but its three-coordinate
projection satisfies $a+b+c=0$. Hence the
width-two criterion \eqref{eq:finite-kernel-width-two}
fails on $S=\{A,B,C\}$: elimination of $D$
creates a genuinely width-three parity check.
Its complete canonical binary orbital structure
is \emph{not homogeneous}, since the
nonextendible triple of flips is a finite
partial binary isomorphism. This is a sharp
general countercontrol, not an exact CCO
counterexample.

The stronger finite projection
\eqref{eq:finite-kernel-strong-projection}
holds automatically for a union of \emph{entire
finite named sorts} in a homogeneous binary
structure, as in
\cref{lem:typed-finite-entire-axis-projection}.
It does \emph{not} follow merely by naming
moving owner classes in an already homogeneous
source. Even homogeneous SAP+CCO multi-original-sort
full-exact covers may have strictly smaller
pointwise owner binding groups than the intrinsic
fibre groups under asymmetric cuts. Nor does the
full quotient binary group necessarily equal the
image of the old finer real automorphism group.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Typed quotient transport
declarations.heading: Invariant typed quotient transport (foundational).
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed quotient transport]\label{lem:typed-quotient-transport}
Let \(R\) be a nonempty invariant binary relation from a named original transitive sort \(a\) to a named original transitive sort \(b\), and let \(E\) be an invariant equivalence on sort \(a\). Suppose
\[
 RR^{\smile}\subseteq E.
\tag{QT1}\label{eq:typed-transport-kernel}
\]
For \(y\in b\), let \(\lambda_{R,E}(y)\) be the \(E\)-class of any
\(x\) with \(xRy\), and put
\[
 E^R=R^{\smile}ER.
\]
Then \(\lambda_{R,E}\) is well defined, \(E^R\) is a definable equivalence,
and \(R\) induces a bijection
\[
 q_{R,E}:a/E\longrightarrow b/E^R.
\]
Transport by this bijection is a lattice isomorphism
\[
 [E,1_a]\longrightarrow [E^R,1_b],
 \qquad H\longmapsto H^R=R^{\smile}HR.
\tag{QT2}\label{eq:typed-transport-lattice}
\]
It respects composition of composable relations for actual composable nonempty invariant typed relations whenever the displayed kernel hypotheses hold. In particular,
meet-irreducibility is preserved by transport.
An ADDITIONAL noncollapse conclusion under visible SAP
may hold in appropriate terminal sources, but is NOT part
of this general invariant quotient-transport assertion.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Invariant typed quotient transport (foundational).

declarations.title: Canonical invariant typed return and identity holonomy
declarations.heading: Invariant typed quotient transport (foundational).
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical invariant typed return and identity holonomy]\label{lem:foundational-typed-return-holonomy}
Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) be a nonempty finite composable sequence
of nonempty invariant represented relations between named transitive
original sorts, from \(a_0\) back to \(a_0\), and suppose
\[
 P_1\cdots P_n\subseteq E_0
\]
for a definable equivalence \(E_0\) on \(a_0\).  Put
\(R_i=P_1\cdots P_i\).  Then every prefix transports \(E_0\) to a definable
equivalence \(E_i\) on the intermediate sort, every factor is
quotient-functional between consecutive transported quotients, and the whole
loop has identity holonomy on \(a_0/E_0\).  The same conclusion holds
simultaneously for EVERY invariant equivalence \(J\supseteq E_0\).
No representation of the transported \(J_i\) by named FULL RAW exact
quotient sorts is asserted.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Invariant typed quotient transport (foundational).

declarations.title: Prescribed-action point lifting
declarations.heading: Prescribed quotient actions on points.
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Prescribed-action point lifting]
\label{lem:prescribed-action-point-lifting}
Let $K$ act on a nonempty set $Y$, let $\Gamma$ act on $B$, and
let $\rho:K\to\Gamma$ be a homomorphism. Suppose $\pi:Y\to B$
is a surjection with $\pi(ky)=\rho(k)\pi(y)$. The following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\rho$ is onto and $\ker\rho$ is transitive on each fibre
      of $\pi$;
\item for every $x,y\in Y$ and every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ with
      $\gamma\pi(x)=\pi(y)$, some $k\in K$ satisfies
      $\rho(k)=\gamma$ and $kx=y$.
\end{enumerate}
Neither action is required to be faithful, and no group section is
assumed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Prescribed quotient actions on points.

declarations.title: Orbital pullbacks through equivariant quotient maps
declarations.heading: Orbital pullbacks and the real diagonal.
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Orbital pullbacks through equivariant quotient maps]
\label{lem:foundational-orbital-pullback}
Let $G$ act transitively on nonempty named root sorts $A,B$, which
are either the same sort or disjoint. Let $\tau:A\to Q$ and
$\sigma:B\to R$ be equivariant surjections to $G$-sets, with kernels
$J=\ker\tau$ and $K=\ker\sigma$. For a nonempty $G$-orbital
$\Theta\subseteq Q\times R$, put
\[
 P_\Theta=\{(x,y)\in A\times B:(\tau(x),\sigma(y))\in\Theta\},
 \qquad D_{A,B}=\{(x,y)\in A\times B:x\ne y\}.
\]
For any $(x_0,y_0)\in P_\Theta$, let $O=G\cdot(x_0,y_0)$.
Then, with actual equality-inclusive relational composition,
\[
                  P_\Theta=J;O;K.
\]
Thus whenever a distinct-root witness is available, the diversity
pullback is exactly $(J;O;K)\cap D_{A,B}$ for its root orbital $O$.
The nonempty diversity pullbacks partition $D_{A,B}$ and induce a
partition of the set of its root $G$-orbitals.

The diversity pullback is empty if and only if $A=B$,
$J=K=\Id_A$, and
\[
                \Theta=\{(\tau(x),\sigma(x)):x\in A\}.
\]
Hence at most one output orbital has empty diversity pullback. In
this case both maps are equivariant bijections and the missing
diversity comes from the same original root, even if $Q,R$ are
different output sorts. No homogeneity, SAP, CCO or word-realisation
assumption is needed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Orbital pullbacks and the real diagonal.

declarations.title: Full exact orbital blocks and compositions
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full exact orbital blocks and compositions]
\label{lem:typed-simultaneous-blocks}
For every original atom $a:s\to t$, including logical equality
when $s=t$, put
\[
 \langle a\rangle_{st}=E_s;\{a\};E_t.
 \tag{TQ1}\label{eq:typed-exact-block}
\]
These nonempty full exact blocks partition the original typed
atom palettes and are precisely the inverse images of the actual
named pair orbitals on $Q_s\times Q_t$.  The inverse image of
$\Id_{Q_s}$ is exactly $E_s$; every quotient diversity orbital
on $Q_s^2$ pulls back to a block disjoint from $E_s$.

For composable unions of quotient atomic orbitals $R:s\to t$
and $T:t\to u$, write $\widetilde R,\widetilde T$ for their
inverse images on original real points. Then
\[
 \widetilde{R;_Q T}
 =\widetilde R;E_t;\widetilde T
 =\widetilde R;\widetilde T.
 \tag{TQ2}\label{eq:typed-exact-quotient-product}
\]
Typed converse and intersections commute with inverse image.
Every nonempty full exact quotient menu pulls back to an original
full exact menu, and every quotient atomic word profile has an
original full exact inverse image.  The quotient full atomic
word-profile families are $2$-Helly.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts

declarations.title: Exact descent in the symmetric one-original-sort case
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact descent in the symmetric one-original-sort case]
\label{lem:one-original-sort-exact-descent}
Suppose the initial source has exactly \emph{one
original transitive sort}, with all old binary
orbitals symmetric. Let $E$ be an invariant
full exact equivalence and let $D$ be a
nonempty old full exact invariant relation
which is \emph{$E$-bisaturated}:
\[
                         E;D;E=D.
\]
Then its image $D/E$ in the actual quotient
$M/E$ is a nonempty full exact relation
of the quotient represented algebra.
In particular, if $E\le K$ are original
full exact equivalences, $K/E$ is a full
exact quotient equivalence.

This converse-to-pullback assertion uses
\emph{one original symmetric sort}.
It is not asserted for an arbitrary full
exact cross-sort relation under mutually
independent quotients of multiple original
sorts.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts

declarations.title: Why independent mixed-sort word descent needs care
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Why independent mixed-sort word descent needs care]
\label{rem:mixed-word-projection-failure}
The proof of
\cref{lem:one-original-sort-exact-descent}
cannot be repeated with independent kernels on
different original sorts simply by projecting
every factor of an old word. This failure occurs
even in a homogeneous symmetric SAP+CCO example.

Take three named sorts $A,B,C$, each consisting of
two infinite pure clone fibres indexed by
$p\in\mathbb F_2$. For any two distinct old
vertices, name their original ordered sort pair
and the bit $p_x+p_y$ (with typed converse).
This source is homogeneous, SAP and homomorphic
CCO: finite partial constraints are XOR
equations whose inconsistency is witnessed by
a nonzero labelled simple cycle; infinite clone
fibres make every consistent system injectively
realizable.

The old mixed word $w=(0:A\to B,\ 0:B\to C)$
has endpoint profile
\[
 P_w=\{(a,c):p_a+p_c=0\}.
\]
Now quotient the \emph{entire} original sort $B$
by its top equivalence, keeping equality on
$A$ and $C$. Each projected edge relation
$0:A\to B/\Top$ and
$0:B/\Top\to C$ is total, so their
quotient word product is the \emph{full}
$A\times C$ relation, strictly larger than
the image of $P_w$. The intervening
$E_B$-movement is the difference.

In this particular example $P_w$ still
descends as a named \emph{atomic} $A$--$C$
quotient relation. Thus this is a
counterexample to \emph{factorwise word
descent}, not a claimed counterexample
to every conceivable multi-sort exact
descent statement. The safe general
direction remains quotient exact $\Rightarrow$
original exact pullback.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Private word-path cycle decomposition
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Private word-path cycle decomposition]
\label{lem:typed-private-path-cycle}
Let \(G\) be a finite simple partially coloured
typed graph, with diversity atoms on its specified
unordered edges. Replace each specified edge
\(uv\) by finitely many formal typed paths between
its marked endpoints, all internal vertices private
to their chosen paths, deleting genuine equality
factors by contracting them within each path.
Assume that no resulting path has length zero,
and that coincident length-one paths between
one marked pair have the same old atomic colour
and are merged.

Then every specified simple cycle of the
resulting raw graph either uses two different
private paths above ONE edge of \(G\), or its
successive marked vertices form a simple
specified cycle of \(G\) and it traverses one
private path above each edge of that cycle.
A single length-one path is counted as one
old edge, not as a parallel edge or a 2-cycle.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts

declarations.title: Simultaneous full exact quotients preserve AP and CCO
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous full exact quotients preserve AP and CCO]
\label{thm:typed-simultaneous-exact-quotients}
Let $M$ be a countable homogeneous complete finite typed binary
structure with a finite family of nonempty original transitive
named sorts, symmetric same-sort orbitals, typed converse-paired
cross-sort orbitals, and semantic \emph{homomorphic} simple-cycle
CCO.  No SAP hypothesis is imposed.  For \emph{arbitrary and
independent} full exact invariant equivalences $E_s$ on the
original named sorts, the actual simultaneous quotient $Q$ above
is homogeneous, has a triangle-defined age with AP and JEP,
and satisfies semantic homomorphic simple-cycle CCO.

Neither global lifting $\Aut(Q)\to\Aut(M)$ nor SAP of $Q$ is a
conclusion; this theorem is not a formalisation of a coherent
choice of fine representatives.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts

declarations.title: Typed full-exact quotient towers
declarations.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Typed full-exact quotient towers]
\label{cor:typed-exact-quotient-towers}
Suppose a finite sequence of homogeneous typed sources is
obtained by simultaneously quotienting each current original
named sort by arbitrary full exact invariant equivalences of
its \emph{current} equality-inclusive represented algebra.
If the initial source satisfies the hypotheses of
\cref{thm:typed-simultaneous-exact-quotients}, so does every
stage.  Furthermore, the composite of any finite number of
these quotient stages is canonically isomorphic as a complete
atomic binary structure to a single simultaneous quotient of
the initial source by full exact invariant equivalences
containing the earlier chosen kernels.  If a stage quotients
some original sort by an equivalence properly above logical
identity, the total number of typed diversity atomic orbitals
(counting converse pairs consistently) strictly decreases.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Simultaneous exact quotients of original named sorts

declarations.title: Strong finite projection of entire named sorts
declarations.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Strong finite projection of entire named sorts]
\label{lem:typed-finite-entire-axis-projection}
Let $X$ be a homogeneous relational structure of arity at most
two, with a collection of pairwise disjoint \emph{named} finite
sorts $(P_i)_{i\in I}$. Other named sorts may be infinite.
Put $\Gamma=\Aut(X)$,
$R_i=\Aut(X\restriction P_i)$, and for $i\ne j$ let
\[
 P_{ij}=\operatorname{im}\bigl(
   \Gamma\longrightarrow R_i\times R_j\bigr).
\]
Then for every finite $S\subseteq I$,
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \operatorname{im}\!\left(
 \Gamma\longrightarrow\prod_{i\in S}R_i\right)
 =\bigl\{(g_i)_{i\in S}:
               (g_i,g_j)\in P_{ij}\quad(i\ne j)\bigr\}.
 \quad}\tag{TQ3}\label{eq:typed-finite-strong-projection}
\]
In particular $\Gamma\to R_i$ is surjective and each
$P_{ij}\le R_i\times R_j$ is a \emph{subdirect} subgroup.
This is a statement about the \emph{full automorphism group of
$X$}, not about the image of an earlier finer source action.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts

declarations.title: Finite linear Goursat code and flat transport
declarations.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Finite linear Goursat code and flat transport]
\label{cor:typed-finite-linear-goursat}
In \cref{lem:typed-finite-entire-axis-projection}, suppose
each $R_i$ is, as an abstract group, an elementary
abelian $2$-group $V_i=\mathbb F_2^{d_i}$.
For each $i<j$ there exist finite vector spaces
$W_{ij}$ and surjective linear maps
$\pi_{ij}:V_i\to W_{ij}$ and
$\rho_{ij}:V_j\to W_{ij}$ such that
\[
 P_{ij}=\{(x,y):\pi_{ij}(x)=\rho_{ij}(y)\}.
\]
On any finite $S$ form the linear parity-check map
\[
 \Phi_S:\bigoplus_{i\in S}V_i
 \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{\{i,j\}\in[S]^2}W_{ij},
 \quad
 (\Phi_S(x))_{ij}=\pi_{ij}(x_i)+\rho_{ij}(x_j).
\]
The image of the actual full group $\Gamma$ on these
entire sorts equals $\ker\Phi_S$; its cardinality is
\[
 2^{\,\sum_{i\in S}d_i-\operatorname{rank}(\Phi_S)}.
 \tag{TQ4}\label{eq:typed-finite-goursat-rank}
\]
More generally, if on three distinct entire finite
named sorts the pair groups are graphs of isomorphisms
$\theta_{ij}:R_i\to R_j$, these satisfy
$\theta_{ik}=\theta_{jk}\circ\theta_{ij}$.
\end{corollary}

declarations.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Finite entire axes after full exact quotient]
\label{cor:typed-exact-finite-axis-goursat}
In \cref{thm:typed-simultaneous-exact-quotients}, take
any selection of ORIGINAL named sorts whose entire
quotient sets $Q_s=M_s/E_s$ are finite. Their full
canonical binary automorphism group $\Aut(Q)$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:typed-finite-strong-projection}, and whenever
its coordinate actions are elementary abelian it
satisfies \eqref{eq:typed-finite-goursat-rank}.
No original SAP is required.

declarations.title: Sharp kernel and lifting firewall
declarations.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Sharp kernel and lifting firewall]
\label{rem:typed-finite-goursat-kernel-scope}
The three preceding statements concern \emph{entire finite
named quotient sorts}. They cannot be applied to the
\emph{pointwise owner kernel} acting on finite fibres above
\emph{unnamed, moving} quotient owners. Naming all those
owners as new constants can destroy homogeneity, so
\cref{lem:typed-finite-entire-axis-projection} need not
hold in the expanded language. The narrower one-original-sort
finite-exact-fibre extension theorem is a genuine
additional structural input, not a formal consequence here.

A small two-original-sort phase control already disproves
the naive stronger intrinsic-binding assertion even with SAP
and CCO. Let two original sorts $U,V$ carry two $\mathbb F_2$
phase classes with infinite pure clones, and name their
cross XOR-difference. Their fine two-point phase quotient
has full automorphism group the \emph{diagonal} $C_2$
translation. Coarsen the $U$ quotient to a singleton but
keep the $V$ phase quotient. The pointwise kernel of the
map of these two fine/coarse quotient automorphism groups
is trivial, although the intrinsic within-$U$ fibre
automorphism group is $C_2$. Both the fine and coarse cuts
are full exact. This does \emph{not} contradict strong
projection for entire named sorts: the latter describes
the \emph{full fine automorphism group} by its actual
cross-sort pair orbitals, not its pointwise kernel.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Scope: joint quotients versus global lifting
declarations.heading: Goursat constraints on entire finite named quotient sorts
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope: joint quotients versus global lifting]
\label{rem:typed-simultaneous-exact-scope}
The common theorem
\cref{thm:typed-joint-exact-lifting} now supplies
individual finite partial-isomorphism lifting for several
exact quotients of each of several ORIGINAL named sorts.
The historical one-original-sort \cref{thm:joint-exact}
is its immediate special case.  The present theorem additionally
proves full triangle-defined AP and \emph{homomorphic CCO} of
the PURE quotient reduct, which does not follow merely from
mixed joint lifting.  Neither theorem constructs a section
of automorphism groups or a functorial choice of fine
representatives.  Cross-sort orbitals are not assumed
commutative and the original real source need not have SAP.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Full exact bridge
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Full exact bridge]
\label{def:foundational-exact-bridge}
Given a full exact invariant equivalence $K_a$ on sort $a$,
a \emph{bridge} to sort $b$ is a nonempty full exact relation
$R:a\to b$ satisfying
\[
 K_aR=R,\qquad RR^\smile=K_a.
 \tag{FB}\label{eq:exact-bridge}
\]
Its target kernel is $K_b=R^\smile R$.
The identity of the quotient object $(a,K_a)$ is $K_a$,
not necessarily original real equality.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Full exact rigid-bridge groupoid
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Transport of a dominant full exact involution
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Transport of a dominant full exact involution]
\label{lem:foundational-rigid-gate-transport}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a rigid bridge groupoid as in
\cref{thm:foundational-rigid-groupoid}, with distinguished object
$(a_*,K_*)$ and a nonidentity isotropy arrow
$t_*\in\mathcal H(a_*,a_*)$. Assume that every \emph{original}
full exact invariant equivalence $Z_*>K_*$ on sort $a_*$
contains $t_*$. For every reached object $(b,K_b)$ and every
bridge $R:a_*\to b$ define
\[
                         t_b=R^\smile;t_*;R.
\]
Conjugation $Z_b\mapsto R;Z_b;R^\smile$ is an order
isomorphism from the poset of original full exact invariant
equivalences containing $K_b$ to the corresponding poset
above $K_*$, with inverse $Z_*\mapsto R^\smile;Z_*;R$.
Moreover $t_b$ is independent of $R$, is a nonidentity full exact
isotropy arrow with $t_b;t_b=K_b$, and is contained in every
\emph{original} full exact invariant equivalence $Z_b>K_b$.
Consequently its quotient graph $\bar t_b$ is contained in every
nonidentity \emph{full exact} equivalence on $M_b/K_b$.
No assumption of SAP or descent of arbitrary old exact domains
into quotient word-exact domains is needed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Exact bridges descend and lift across exact kernels
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact bridges descend and lift across exact kernels]
\label{lem:foundational-rigid-quotient-bridge}
Let $E_a\le K_a$ and $E_b\le K_b$ be
full exact invariant equivalences on two
original named transitive sorts. Form their
actual simultaneous full exact quotient
$Q$ by $E_a,E_b$ (and any specified exact
kernels on the remaining original sorts).
Assume moreover that the projected
relations
\[
 \bar K_a=K_a/E_a,\qquad \bar K_b=K_b/E_b
\]
are \emph{full exact equivalences in the
quotient represented algebra}.
Then the map $R\mapsto\bar R$ taking
$E_a,E_b$-bisaturated original relations
to their quotient relations is a bijection
between the exact functional bridges
$R:(a,K_a)\to(b,K_b)$ and the exact
functional bridges
$\bar R:(Q_a,\bar K_a)\to(Q_b,\bar K_b)$.
It preserves converse and composition.
In particular no extra rigid bridge appears
in the quotient, and none disappears.

The full-exactness of the \emph{projected
gates} $\bar K_a,\bar K_b$ is an explicit
hypothesis: the general typed quotient
word-pullback theorem alone only proves
exactness in the reverse direction.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Affine exact rigid slices
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Affine exact rigid slices]
\label{lem:foundational-rigid-affine}
Let $D:a\to b$ be nonempty full exact and
$K_a,K_b$-bisaturated, supported entirely on the union
of the rigid arrows in a nonempty hom-set above.
Then $D$ is a union of \emph{whole} rigid arrows; for
some rigid arrow $d:a\to b$ and an exact subgroup
$S\le\mathcal H(b,b)$ it has the form $D=dS$.
Here $dS$ means the union of represented graphs of
the composite arrows, not an individual original atom.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Rigid-product factorisation
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Rigid-product factorisation]
\label{lem:foundational-rigid-factor}
Suppose nonempty full exact $A:a\to b$ and $B:b\to c$
satisfy $AB\subseteq R$ for one full exact bridge
$R:a\to c$ from $(a,K_a)$. Then there are bridges
$R_1:a\to b$, $R_2:b\to c$ with
\[
 A\subseteq R_1,\quad B\subseteq R_2,\quad R_1R_2=R.
\]
This uses represented seriality, not SAP.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Binary groupoid characters and phase marking
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Binary groupoid characters and phase marking]
\label{thm:foundational-rigid-character}
Assume the groupoid of
\cref{thm:foundational-rigid-groupoid}
has a distinguished nonidentity isotropy arrow
$t_*\in\mathcal H(a_*,a_*)$.
There exists a functor
$\chi:\mathcal H\to\mathbb F_2$
with $\chi(t_*)=1$. Every object $b$ has a
path-independent transported involution
$t_b=R^\smile t_*R\ne K_b$, with $\chi(t_b)=1$.
There is a global bit function on all reached quotient
points satisfying
\[
       \lambda(Rq)=\lambda(q)+\chi(R).
\]
Rigid quotient pair orbitals have one forced phase
difference; every nonrigid quotient pair orbital admits
both phase differences by appropriate global choices.
Thus the finite unary phase marking is reduct-surjective.
This alone does \emph{not} imply AP, SAP or CCO of the
marked age.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Finite phase constraints extend by groupoid seeds
declarations.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite phase constraints extend by groupoid seeds]
\label{lem:foundational-finite-phase-extension}
Use a free action on quotient points of a finite connected
rigid groupoid with a fixed character
$\chi:\mathcal H\to\mathbb F_2$ as above. Let $F$ be any
finite set of quotient points and let
$\epsilon:F\to\mathbb F_2$ be prescribed bits.
Then there is a \emph{global} phase marking $\lambda$
satisfying
\[
 \lambda(Rq)=\lambda(q)+\chi(R)
 \quad\text{for all rigid arrows $R$},
 \qquad \lambda|_F=\epsilon ,
\]
if and only if, whenever $q,r\in F$ belong to the
same rigid-groupoid orbit and $Rq=r$, one has
\[
             \epsilon(r)=\epsilon(q)+\chi(R).
 \tag{FS}\label{eq:foundational-phase-seed-test}
\]
It suffices to check the prescribed bits pairwise; no
additional higher-arity character holonomy condition is
needed. This does \emph{not} imply a finite projection
theorem for moving-owner pointwise kernels from
\cref{thm:finite-fibre-kernel-csp}.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full exact functional correspondences and rigid groupoids

declarations.title: Finite-relative orbital parity without SAP
declarations.heading: Finite relative indices and separation of exact equivalences
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite-relative orbital parity without SAP]
\label{lem:ep-ap-orbital-parity}
Let $E<F$ be arbitrary invariant equivalences on $M$ with finite
relative index $n=[F:E]$. For every old diversity atom
$c\subseteq F\setminus E$, its graph is bipartite. Its even- and
odd-walk relations $Y_c,O_c$ are represented by stabilized positive
atomic-word profiles; $Y_c$ is a full exact equivalence, and
\[
 Y_c<X_c=Y_c\cup O_c\le F,
 \qquad [X_c:Y_c]=2.
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Finite relative indices and separation of exact equivalences
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Separation at the old logical identity]
\label{cor:foundations-identity-separation}
For full exact symmetric $A,B$ containing $\Id$ and with
$A\cap B=\Id$, their exact equivalence closures intersect in
$\Id$. This is the case $K=\Id$ of
\cref{lem:ep-relative-K-closure}.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Maximal exact parity gate and its source involution
declarations.heading: Finite relative indices and separation of exact equivalences
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Maximal exact parity gate and its source involution]
\label{thm:foundational-maximal-parity-gate}
Let $Y<X$ be actual invariant same-sort equivalences in the
original homogeneous symmetric AP+homomorphic-CCO source,
with $[X:Y]=2$. Assume $Y$ and the \emph{odd relation}
$O=X\setminus Y$ are full exact. The equivalence $X$
itself need \emph{not} be full exact. Choose an
inclusion-maximal full exact equivalence $K$ satisfying
\[
             Y\le K,\qquad K\cap X=Y.
\]
Then, writing $F=K\vee X$ and $t=K;O;K$,
\[
             [F:K]=2,\qquad
             F=K\mathbin{\dot\cup}t,\qquad
             t;t=K.
\]
The relation $t$ is nonempty, full exact and $K$-bisaturated;
its image $\bar t=t/K$ is the graph of an equivariant
fixed-point-free involution of $M/K$.
More strongly, \emph{every original full exact
equivalence} $Z>K$ contains the entire
old relation $t$. In particular every full
exact quotient equivalence
$\bar Z>\Id_{M/K}$ contains $\bar t$.
The first assertion does not require any
converse exact-descent theorem.
Thus the original source object with kernel $K$ has the
distinguished nonidentity exact isotropy arrow required by
\cref{thm:foundational-rigid-character}.
No SAP is required.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: SAP-free fork totality and phase-primality
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[SAP-free fork totality and phase-primality]
\label{lem:ep-ap-TP}
For the \emph{maximal} exact-character
groupoid phase masks \eqref{eq:ep-ap-mask},
the following hold without old SAP:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textup{\alph*}),leftmargin=*]
\item[(T)] Given two allowed old atomic
pair types with compatible middle phase,
some old represented output is allowed
at the prescribed endpoint phases.
\item[(P)] If old reachable typed word
endpoint profiles \(W_1,\ldots,W_r\)
have nonempty intersection and each
meets the requested endpoint phase mask,
their intersection also meets the mask.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Exact algebraic endpoint support of a marked path
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact algebraic endpoint support of a marked path]
\label{lem:ep-ap-path}
Let $w=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be a nonempty
old \emph{typed diversity} path on formal
vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_n$, with each
specified edge $a_j$ locally allowed for
the prescribed endpoint phase bits
$\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_n$.
Write
\[
 P_r=\{a_1\};\cdots;\{a_r\},\qquad
 \delta_r=\epsilon_0+\epsilon_r,
\]
and calculate the \emph{formal lifted
endpoint supports} recursively by
\[
 L_1=\{a_1\},\qquad
 L_{r+1}=(L_r;\{a_{r+1}\})\cap
       A_{s_0s_{r+1}}^{\epsilon_0,\epsilon_{r+1}},
\]
where the last mask is the \emph{actual two-endpoint-bit}
mask from \eqref{eq:ep-ap-mask}; no extra independent
bit is introduced when an endpoint sort is inactive.
Then for every $r=1,\ldots,n$,
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 L_r=P_r\cap A_{s_0s_r}^{\epsilon_0,\epsilon_r}
                      \ne\varnothing .\qquad}
 \tag{S4}\label{eq:ep-ap-path-normal-form}
\]
The equality uses \emph{actual represented}
equality-inclusive old products: a literal
old identity may occur in $L_r$ as a
possible \emph{endpoint output}, never
as a specified diversity edge.
The supports $L_r$ are a formal
algebraic reduction of phase-constrained
paths; their equality alone does not
assume or assert that the entire marked
age has already been proved to have AP.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Identity folding preserves individual old cycles
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Identity folding preserves individual old cycles]
\label{lem:ep-ap-identity-fold}
Let \(G\) be a finite simple, typed old diversity partial network
such that every specified simple cycle has a homomorphism into \(M\).
Let \(x\ne y\) be nonadjacent vertices of the same original sort.
Suppose \(\Id\) belongs to the represented endpoint profile of
\emph{every} simple \(x\)--\(y\) path in \(G\)
(the condition is vacuous when there is no such path).
Then one may identify \(x=y\), deduplicate incident edges,
and obtain another simple typed old diversity partial network
whose every specified simple cycle admits a homomorphism into \(M\).
If \(x,y\) have the same phase bit, their prescribed bits
also descend to this quotient. No SAP or already constructed
marked Fra\"iss\'e limit is assumed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting

declarations.title: Real marked completion and AP-only safe splitting
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Real marked completion and AP-only safe splitting]
\label{thm:ep-ap-marked-completion}
A finite locally \(\chi\)-legal phase-marked
old diversity partial network \(P\)
has a homomorphic marked completion
provided each specified old simple
cycle is homomorphically completable in
the original \(M\).
Consequently the marked finite age
is reasonable, reduct-surjective,
precompact, has AP/JEP and homomorphic
semantic CCO, and its Fra\"iss\'e
limit is homogeneous.
Its complete diagrams are precisely
the locally pair-admissible old
complete diagrams.
These conclusions do \emph{not}
require original SAP or triangle-definedness.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Strict rank drop under a genuine binary character split
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Strict rank drop under a genuine binary character split]
\label{lem:exact-character-rank-drop}
Let $\mathcal C$ be any homogeneous finite complete
binary age with finitely many named transitive current
sorts. Suppose a \emph{genuine} finite unary character
split replaces a nonempty family $S$ of active sorts
$a$ by two \emph{nonempty} child sorts
$a^0,a^1$, with all original binary atom names
unchanged. Assume on each active parent $a$
there is a realised old same-sort diversity atom
$c_a$ which always has phase difference one,
so that no $c_a$-pair can lie inside
$a^0$ or inside $a^1$.
For a current sort $a$, let $k_a$ count its realised
\emph{nonidentity same-sort pair orbitals}.
Then
\[
 k_{a^\epsilon}\le k_a-1\quad(\epsilon=0,1),
 \qquad
 \Phi(\mathcal C)=\sum_{\text{current sorts }a}3^{k_a}
\]
strictly decreases at this split:
\[
 \Phi(\mathcal C^{\rm new})
 \le \Phi(\mathcal C)
       -\sum_{a\in S}3^{k_a}
       +\sum_{a\in S}2\cdot3^{k_a-1}
 <\Phi(\mathcal C).
 \tag{ACR}\label{eq:exact-character-rank-drop}
\]
No SAP is needed for this counting lemma.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting

declarations.title: Finite AP-only exact character terminalisation
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite AP-only exact character terminalisation]
\label{thm:ap-finite-character-elimination}
Starting from any homogeneous finite complete
named-sorted symmetric binary AP+semantic
homomorphic-CCO source in the class considered
above, successive \emph{maximal full exact}
character splits of
\cref{lem:ep-ap-TP,thm:ep-ap-marked-completion}
terminate after finitely many stages.
The resulting finite unary expansion remains
reasonable, reduct-surjective, precompact,
homogeneous, has AP/JEP and homomorphic
CCO, and on every terminal named sort
there are no distinct invariant equivalences
of \emph{finite relative index}.
Neither the initial nor the terminal age
is asserted to have SAP.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting

declarations.title: AP-only source for the exact-quotient core induction
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[AP-only source for the exact-quotient core induction]
\label{cor:ep-ap-safe-splitting}
Every available finite-relative-index invariant
equivalence interval in a homogeneous symmetric
AP+homomorphic-CCO source admits a reachable
maximal exact character split whose actual
expanded age has AP/JEP and homomorphic CCO
with unchanged old reduct. Moreover finitely
many such steps eliminate \emph{all} finite
relative-index intervals on the resulting
named sorts, without introducing any SAP
hypothesis on the original or a quotient.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Scope and retained source dependencies
declarations.heading: AP-only safe exact character splitting
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope and retained source dependencies]
\label{rem:ep-ap-source-boundary}
The old parity and maximal gate, full exact
word 2-Helly/convolution, rigid groupoid,
rigid-product factorisation, affine coset
and relative-\(K\) closure-separation
results all occur earlier in Part~I.
The substantial new content here is the
SAP-free actual finite marked AP/CCO
completion, including real equality
contractions. Finite termination of the
\emph{entire} AP-only character tower is
proved IN THIS Part-I module by the
standalone potential-decrease lemma
\cref{lem:exact-character-rank-drop};
it does NOT invoke the later SAP-only V27
terminal Ramsey construction.
The underlying old parity, exact and
rigid-groupoid inputs remain substantial
source-relative premises, not human/Lean
certified. In particular the proof
does not infer SAP of a marked age
when the old age lacks it.
\end{remark}
