declarations.title: Distributivity of the actual exact lattice
declarations.heading: Distributive exact geometry and the quotient CRT
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Distributivity of the actual exact lattice]
\label{lem:acf-exact-distributive}
The finite lattice $\mathcal E_{\rm ex}(M)$ of invariant exact
equivalences of a standing symmetric CCO source is distributive.
It admits Birkhoff's representation $\mathcal E_{\rm ex}(M)
\cong\operatorname{Down}(P)$, and every finite family of actual
exact quotients satisfies the set-level full compatibility CRT.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Distributive exact geometry and the quotient CRT

declarations.title: Cofinality of selected meet-irreducible coordinates
declarations.heading: Distributive exact geometry and the quotient CRT
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Cofinality of selected meet-irreducible coordinates]
\label{lem:foundational-MI-coordinate-cofinal}
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite distributive lattice, let
$J_1,\ldots,J_r\in\Lambda$ with $r\ge1$, and put
$K=\bigwedge_{i=1}^rJ_i$. If $L$ is meet-irreducible
and $K\le L$, then
\[
                        J_i\le L
 \quad\text{for some }i\le r.
 \tag{MI-C}\label{eq:foundational-MI-cofinal}
\]
Consequently, if $K$ is represented by a finite
tuple of its chosen $J_i$ quotient coordinates,
every represented proper meet-irreducible
$L\ge K$ is an \emph{upward quotient image}
of at least one of these coordinates.
No SAP, CCO or Ramsey hypothesis is part
of this finite lattice lemma.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Distributive exact geometry and the quotient CRT

declarations.title: Three separate interfaces
declarations.heading: Distributive exact geometry and the quotient CRT
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Three separate interfaces]
The abstract CRT gives a \emph{set} of compatible tuples.
Recovery of the original \emph{fine pair colours} from actual
quotient colours, and simultaneous extension of finite real/owner
partial isomorphisms, are different consequences of the represented
A32 exact-sort geometry.  We never replace those conclusions by a
bare assertion that the lattice is distributive.  Nor is the
\emph{full} invariant-equivalence lattice claimed distributive:
nonexact finite packet intervals need not lie in
$\mathcal E_{\rm ex}(M)$.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: CCO-free RAW word presentations for all original invariant equivalences
declarations.heading: Terminal original invariant equivalences: RAW words and CRT
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[CCO-free RAW word presentations for all original invariant equivalences]
\label{lem:typed-all-invariant-equivalences-raw-word}
Let $M$ be a homogeneous finite-complete binary
structure with a finite old atomic pair palette
and individually transitive named original sorts;
assume SAME-SORT old atomic orbitals are symmetric.
Fix one original real sort $a$. Suppose the FULL
original invariant-equivalence lattice on $a$
has NO relative-index-two interval. Then EVERY
original $\Aut(M)$-invariant equivalence $E$
on $M_a$ is the ACTUAL equality-inclusive RAW
relation of ONE old atomic word on sort $a$.
Thus EVERY invariant equivalence is FULL RAW
exact (already as one word profile). Neither
visible SAP nor semantic CCO, exact-ball Helly
or distributivity is assumed. In particular
this lemma does NOT claim that the FULL invariant
lattice is distributive without CCO.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Terminal original invariant equivalences: RAW words and CRT

declarations.title: Terminal typed invariant equivalences are RAW exact
declarations.heading: Terminal original invariant equivalences: RAW words and CRT
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Terminal typed invariant equivalences are RAW exact]
\label{lem:typed-terminal-all-equivalences-exact}
Fix an original named transitive sort $a$ of a finite
complete homogeneous typed symmetric SAP+semantic-CCO
source which has no proper finite relative-index interval
of invariant equivalences on $a$. Then EVERY
$\Aut(M)$-invariant equivalence $E$ on $M_a$
is an actual RAW equality-inclusive represented
atomic word profile. In particular, the FULL finite
sortwise invariant-equivalence lattice is distributive.
This does not assert commutativity of mixed-sort arrows.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Terminal original invariant equivalences: RAW words and CRT

declarations.title: Exactness descends through exact quotients
declarations.heading: Actual exact fibre products and quotient descent
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exactness descends through exact quotients]
\label{lem:exact-descent}
Suppose $J$ is an invariant exact equivalence and $Q\ge J$ is
an invariant $J$-saturated exact relation (in particular an exact
equivalence). Then its induced relation $Q/J$ on $M/J$ is exact in
the actual quotient orbital language. Conversely the pullback of
every quotient word profile is a represented exact relation on $M$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Actual exact fibre products and quotient descent

declarations.title: Typed exact descent under intertwining kernels
declarations.heading: Actual exact fibre products and quotient descent
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed exact descent under intertwining kernels]
\label{lem:typed-intertwining-exact-descent}
Let $N$ be a typed original source as in
\cref{thm:full-typed-exact-balls}, and choose for every
original named sort $s$ a full RAW exact invariant
equivalence $E_s$.  Let $D:s\to t$ be a nonempty FULL
exact original relation such that $E_s;D;E_t=D$.
Suppose $D$ has a finite word presentation
$D=\bigcap_{\alpha=1}^m P_{w_\alpha}$, allowing $m=0$
(the typed top), and that every original atomic factor
$a:u\to v$ occurring in these words satisfies
\[
                       E_u;a=a;E_v.
 \tag{TI}\label{eq:typed-intertwining}
\]
Then the induced relation $D/(E_s,E_t)$ on the actual
quotient sorts $N_s/E_s$, $N_t/E_t$ is FULL exact in
their complete binary orbital language.  Conversely,
the old inverse image of every quotient FULL exact
relation is original FULL exact without assuming (TI).
This is a sufficient typed descent criterion, not an
assertion of unrestricted factorwise mixed-sort descent.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Actual exact fibre products and quotient descent

declarations.title: Finite-index closure and packet core
declarations.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Finite-index closure and packet core]\label{def:packetcore}
For $J\in\Lambda$, let $\Sigma(J)$ be the greatest equivalence $K\ge J$
for which $[K:J]$ is finite.  Let $F=\Sigma(\Id)$.  An atomic diversity
colour $a$ is \emph{looped} if $(a,a,a)$ is an allowed triangle.  Write
$\Gamma(a)$ for the least invariant equivalence containing $a$, and put
\[
\kappa(J)=\bigvee\{\Gamma(a): a\subseteq J,\ (a,a,a)
                  \text{ is allowed}\},
\]
where an empty join is $\Id$.  Here and below $a\subseteq J$ means
that the entire actual $a$-orbital belongs to the raw support of $J$.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Loop criterion
declarations.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Loop criterion]\label{lem:loopcrit}
For invariant equivalences $J\le K$,
\[
 [K:J]<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{no looped diversity atom lies in }K\setminus J.
\]
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut

declarations.title: Canonical packet interval and exact core
declarations.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical packet interval and exact core]
\label{lem:packetinterval}
For every $J\in\Lambda$,
\[
 [J:\kappa(J)]<\infty,
 \qquad \Sigma(\kappa(J))=\Sigma(J).
\]
The equivalences with finite-index closure $\Sigma(J)$ form precisely
the interval $[\kappa(J),\Sigma(J)]$; in particular $\kappa(J)$ is its
unique least element.  If $\kappa(J)>\Id$, then $\kappa(J)$ is an
actual positive word profile, and hence an exact equivalence.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut

declarations.title: Geometry below a minimal infinite cut
declarations.heading: Finite-index packets and the first exact cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Geometry below a minimal infinite cut]
\label{prop:minimalcut}
Let $E$ be an inclusion-minimal infinite invariant equivalence and
$H=E\cap F$.  Then $E=\kappa(E)$ is exact, and every proper
invariant equivalence $J<E$ has finite classes and lies in $H$.
In particular
\[
 [\Id,E]=[\Id,H]\cup\{E\},
\]
and $E$ admits no proper finite-index refinement.  If
$J<K\le E$ has finite index and $J<K$, then $K\le H$.
The actual quotient $M/E$ is a homogeneous triangle-defined AP and
semantic-homomorphic-CCO source in its binary orbital language.
\end{proposition}

declarations.title: Finite exact regularization
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite exact regularization]\label{lem:finite-regularization}
Let $F=\Sigma(\Id)$, the greatest invariant equivalence with
finite real classes.  There is an exact equivalence $H_0\le F$,
with finite classes, such that all atomic relations lying below
the induced equivalence $F/H_0$ on $M/H_0$ are thin.
We may take $H_0=\Id$ if all atoms within $F$ are thin.
If an atom within $F$ is nonthin, we may take $H_0>\Id$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom

declarations.title: Geometric finite-exact-kernel normalisation
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Geometric finite-exact-kernel normalisation]
\label{lem:finite-exact-normalization-geometric}
Let $M$ be the standing homogeneous symmetric triangle-defined
AP+CCO source in its finite binary orbital language.  There is a
finite chain of actual exact quotients
\[
              M=M_0\longrightarrow M_1\longrightarrow\cdots
                 \longrightarrow M_m
\]
(where $m$ may be zero) such that each nontrivial step is the
quotient of $M_i$ by a nonidentity invariant exact equivalence
$K_i$ with finite real classes.  Each $M_i$ is again a homogeneous
symmetric triangle-defined AP+CCO source.  The terminal source
$M_m$ has no invariant finite-class exact equivalence strictly
above $\Id$, and all its atomic orbitals contained in its
greatest finite-class equivalence $F_m=\Sigma_{M_m}(\Id)$ are thin.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom

declarations.title: A thin finite bottom with a nontrivial exact kernel
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A thin finite bottom with a nontrivial exact kernel]
\label{ex:thin-not-exact-free}
The stronger geometric reduction in Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-exact-normalization-geometric} is really
necessary, even for a homogeneous triangle-defined AP+CCO source.
Let $I,J$ be countably infinite, and consider
$M=I\times J\times\{0,1\}$.  Name four diversity colours:
\begin{itemize}
\item $t$ between the two distinct points of one cell $(i,j)$;
\item $r$ if the $I$-coordinates agree but the $J$-coordinates differ;
\item $c$ if the $J$-coordinates agree but the $I$-coordinates differ;
\item $b$ if both coordinates differ.
\end{itemize}
The final two-point coordinate is immaterial for $r,c,b$.
The two equivalences given by equality of the $I$-coordinate and
of the $J$-coordinate are determined by the unions
$\Id\cup t\cup r$ and $\Id\cup t\cup c$ respectively.  Their
intersection is $F=\Id\cup t$, with classes of size two, and all
its atoms are thin.  The equivalences are exact: indeed $r^2$
and $c^2$ are precisely these two equivalences, so
$F=r^2\cap c^2$ is exact and nontrivial.

For completeness, the structure is homogeneous.  A finite partial
isomorphism induces partial bijections of the $I$- and $J$-index
sets, extendible to permutations of the respective countable sets;
within each occupied cell it induces a partial permutation of the
two-element fibre, independently extendible to a full permutation.
The age is triangle-defined: triangle constraints force the two
coordinate equality relations to be equivalences, while the forbidden
$t,t,t$ triangle enforces the bound of two points per cell.  Once
these conditions hold, distinct coordinate names and a two-point
labelling in each cell realise the complete finite diagram.  AP
follows from homogeneity.

The structure also has semantic homomorphic CCO.  For a partial
edge-coloured diagram, each specified edge requires equality or
inequality of the $I$-coordinates, and independently of the
$J$-coordinates, according to its colour.  Such a system of
constraints for either infinite coordinate fails precisely when a
specified inequality edge is joined by a path of specified equality
edges; a shortest such path plus the edge is a labelled simple cycle.
After these coordinate constraints are satisfied, the specified
$t$-edges are exactly the remaining requirements of different
$\{0,1\}$-labels inside one cell.  They can be satisfied precisely
when the $t$-edge graph is bipartite; an obstruction is an odd
monochromatic $t$-cycle.  Thus any failure of a homomorphic
completion is witnessed by a specified simple cycle, proving CCO.

Fix the infinite exact equivalence $E$ of equality of the
$I$-coordinate.  Between two distinct $E$-owners, the raw colour
$c$ has conditional valency $2$, because it chooses one $J$-coordinate
and either point of the target cell.  In particular
\[
                     E\cap c^2=F>\Id.
\]
This example refutes the shortcut ``$F$ thin, therefore there are no
nonidentity finite exact kernels'', but is not a counterexample to
EPPA.  The geometric reduction of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-exact-normalization-geometric}
permits the first quotient by the exact kernel $F$ in this example;
the conditional-bijection argument then applies to the quotient.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Elementary abelian translation group
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Elementary abelian translation group]
\label{lem:thin-bottom}
Assume every atom in $F$ is thin.  The atoms contained in $F$,
including equality, form a group $G\cong (\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^d$
under represented relational composition.  For each $g\in G$
let $q_g$ be its atom and $t_g(x)$ the unique point with
$x\mathrel{q_g} t_g(x)$.  The $t_g$ are automorphisms of $M$,
commute with $\Aut(M)$ and act regularly on each $F$-class.
Moreover, for any original atomic colour $a$ the product $q_ga$
is a single atom, denoted $g\cdot a$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:thin-transport}
 \col(t_gx,t_hy)=(g+h)\cdot\col(x,y)
 \qquad(g,h\in G;\ x,y\in M),
\end{equation}
where equality is included among the possible colours.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom

declarations.title: Lower interval after thin regularization
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Lower interval after thin regularization]
\label{cor:lower-subgroups}
In the reduced source in which $F$ is thin, let $E$ be an
inclusion-minimal infinite invariant equivalence and let
$H=E\cap F$.  Identifying the thin atoms in $F$ with the group
$G$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:thin-bottom}, the interval below $E$ is
\[
 [\Id,E]=\operatorname{Sub}(H)\cup\{E\}.
\]
Here $H$ is identified with a subgroup of $G$.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom

declarations.title: Scope of the finite bottom
declarations.heading: Finite exact regularization and the thin bottom
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope of the finite bottom]
\label{rem:finite-bottom-scope}
The regular action in Lemma~\ref{lem:thin-bottom} is a statement
about $F$-fibres in the \emph{actual} reduced homogeneous source.
A quotient by an arbitrary nonexact equivalence or a freely
selected system of packet origins need not inherit this action
in a compatible mixed-sort language.  The conditional groupoid
and the choice of all actual owners must be handled separately.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Closed owner walks and saturated word products
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Closed owner walks and saturated word products]
\label{lem:anchored-closed-walk}
Let $E$ be an invariant equivalence on the transitive real source
$M$.  Let $W=w_1\cdots w_m$ be a represented product whose factors
are raw atomic relations or the full relation $E$, and suppose at
least one factor is $E$.  Suppose there are actual $E$-classes
$X_0,\ldots,X_m=X_0$ such that for every atomic factor $w_i=a$
there is an $a$-edge from $X_{i-1}$ to $X_i$, while for every
factor $w_i=E$ one has $X_{i-1}=X_i$.  Then
$\Id\subseteq W$.  If every $E$-factor is expanded as a
positive word of raw atoms representing $E$, the expanded closed
raw word admits a colour-preserving homomorphism to $M$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: Anchored relative completion
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Anchored relative completion]
\label{thm:anchored-relative}
Suppose $E$ is reachable.  Let $P$ be a finite raw partial diagram
admitting a colour-preserving homomorphism to $M$, and let
$\lambda:V(P)\to Q$ be edge-compatible.  Then there is a
colour-preserving homomorphism $f:P\to M$ with
$\pi f=\lambda$.

More precisely, if $A\subseteq V(P)$ induces a \emph{complete}
raw substructure and $j:A\hookrightarrow M$ is an embedding with
$\pi j=\lambda|_A$, then $f$ can be chosen to extend $j$.
If moreover $\Age(M)$ has SAP and every $E$-class is infinite,
$f$ can be chosen injective.  No SAP is assumed for the first two
assertions.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: Exact caps of completion spectra
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Exact caps of completion spectra]
\label{cor:relative-cap}
Let $D_{xy}$ be the set of possible raw colours on a currently
unspecified pair $x,y$ in completions of a finite raw partial
diagram $P$ in $M$, where the completions are allowed to be
homomorphic (and equality is treated by identification).  Let
$C_{xy}$ be the raw pullback of the unique actual quotient orbital
from $\lambda(x)$ to $\lambda(y)$.  If $P$ has a raw completion
and $\lambda$ is edge-compatible, then the colours possible on
$x,y$ \emph{with the prescribed owner assignment} are exactly
\[
                         D_{xy}\cap C_{xy}.
\]
Moreover all quotient owner caps have a common completion.  Under
SAP and infinite fibres the same holds for injective completions,
with the diversity-colour interpretation.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: Joint exact owner caps are governed by the raw cycles
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Joint exact owner caps are governed by the raw cycles]
\label{prop:joint-owner-caps}
Assume $E$ is reachable and retain an edge-compatible quotient
assignment $\lambda$ for a finite raw partial diagram $P$.
Let $S$ be any collection of its presently unspecified unordered
pairs, and prescribe a diversity colour $a_{xy}$ on each pair
$xy\in S$.  Write $P_S$ for the diagram with all these colours
added simultaneously.  If a complete induced subdiagram
$A\subseteq P$ is already embedded by $j:A\hookrightarrow M$
with $\pi j=\lambda|_A$, retain that anchor (and otherwise take
$A=\varnothing$).
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a colour-preserving homomorphism
$f:P_S\to M$ extending $j$ and satisfying $\pi f=\lambda$.
\item Every newly prescribed $a_{xy}$ is compatible with the
actual owner pair $(\lambda(x),\lambda(y))$, and every
specified simple cycle of the \emph{whole augmented diagram}
$P_S$ admits a raw colour-preserving homomorphism to $M$.
\end{enumerate}
Under the additional SAP and infinite-$E$-class hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:anchored-relative}, ``homomorphism'' in (1)
may be strengthened to ``embedding'' (for diversity constraints).
Thus a product of the \emph{individual} capped edge spectra is
in general only an upper bound on the joint completion spectrum;
the remaining compatibility constraints are exactly those of raw
semantic CCO, not an independent choice on each edge.
\end{proposition}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: A four-cycle blocks independently admissible caps
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A four-cycle blocks independently admissible caps]
\label{ex:joint-cap-four-cycle}
In the Cartesian phase model of Example~\ref{ex:two-coordinate},
take $E$ to be equality of the row and phase coordinates;
it is reachable, since the square of the colour
$(\text{same row},\text{different column},\text{same phase})$
is exactly $E$.  Let $x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3$ be formal vertices with
four pairwise distinct prescribed row owners and the same
phase.  Between two different row owners at the same phase,
both the same-column colour $b$ and the different-column
colour $d$ are individually possible.  Nevertheless the four prescriptions
\[
 x_0x_1=b,\qquad x_1x_2=b,\qquad
 x_2x_3=b,\qquad x_3x_0=d
\]
have no common completion: the first three force all four
column coordinates to agree, contradicting the last.  Every
proper subfamily of these four constraints is realizable with
the specified owners.  There is no specified triangle;
the obstructing cycle has length four.  Thus owner-wise
edge compatibility, nonempty individual capped spectra and
checks confined to triangles cannot replace the cyclic
condition in Proposition~\ref{prop:joint-owner-caps}.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Actual finite-owner typed source
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Actual finite-owner typed source]
\label{prop:anchored-typed-source}
For a finite actual induced quotient substructure $B\subseteq Q$,
let $N_B$ be the raw induced structure on $\pi^{-1}(B)$ with one
named unary owner predicate for each $b\in B$.  Then $N_B$ is
homogeneous, and its finite complete structures are exactly the
raw triangle-legal diagrams with owner assignments in $B$ that
are edge-compatible with all prescribed raw colours.  Its age has
AP and semantic typed homomorphic CCO.  If the original raw age
has SAP and the $E$-classes are infinite, the typed age has SAP.

Further, writing $\Gamma_B=\Aut(B)$, every finite raw partial
isomorphism $p$ of $M$ whose domain and range lie in
$\pi^{-1}(B)$ and for which a prescribed $\gamma\in\Gamma_B$
satisfies $\pi\circ p=\gamma\circ\pi$ on its domain extends
to an ambient automorphism of $M$ inducing $\gamma$ on the
entire finite set of owners $B$.
\end{proposition}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: Prescribed finite-language-action EPPA
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Prescribed finite-language-action EPPA]
\label{def:gamma-eppa}
For $\Gamma_B=\Aut(B)$, each $\gamma\in\Gamma_B$ acts on the
language of $N_B$ by sending the owner predicate $P_b$ to
$P_{\gamma b}$ and fixing every original named binary raw colour.
A \emph{$\Gamma_B$-partial automorphism} of a finite typed $A$
is a pair $(p,\gamma)$ where $p$ is a partial bijection that
preserves all raw colours and sends each typed vertex in $P_b$
to a vertex in $P_{\gamma b}$.  A \emph{$\Gamma_B$-EPPA witness}
for $A$ is a single finite typed extension $W$ in the same age
such that every such pair extends to an automorphism of the
\emph{language-action structure}: there is a bijection $\widehat p$
of $W$ extending $p$, preserving raw colours and satisfying
$\widehat p(P_b^W)=P_{\gamma b}^W$ for all $b$.  The choices
for different pairs need not be coherent.  The typed age is closed
under the indicated finite language action, since the
actual quotient orbital caps are preserved by $\gamma$.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Conditional transfer of ordinary EPPA across $E$
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional transfer of ordinary EPPA across $E$]
\label{thm:relative-transfer}
Suppose the exact quotient age $\Age(Q)$ has ordinary EPPA.
Suppose, for every finite actual $B\subseteq Q$, the typed age
$\Age(N_B)$ has $\Gamma_B$-EPPA for the finite language action
which permutes its unary owner names by $\Gamma_B=\Aut(B)$
and fixes \emph{each} original raw colour name.  Then
$\Age(M)$ has ordinary EPPA.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners

declarations.title: Scope
declarations.heading: Anchored relative completion over actual exact owners
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope]
\label{rem:relative-scope}
Theorem~\ref{thm:anchored-relative} uses only raw semantic
homomorphic CCO, exact quotient geometry and triangle-definedness
up to its final injectivity clause.  The stronger raw SAP assumption
there is \emph{not} part of the standing main EPPA theorem; it is
used only later for an actual \emph{closed} transversal which has
independently been proved to admit strong amalgamation.  Likewise
Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-transfer} is a conditional reduction, not
a theorem asserting $\Gamma_B$-EPPA for arbitrary typed sources.
The latter is constructed subsequently by the HKN/selector
argument, with all mixed fine colours present.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Rectangle criterion and orbit folding
declarations.heading: Atomic supports and relative separator calculus
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Rectangle criterion and orbit folding]\label{lem:rh-fold}
For distinct diversity $u,v$ and any diversity $p$,
\[
 H(p,u)\cap H(p,v)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 A_p\cap H(u,v)\ne\varnothing.
\]
If $u\sim_R v$ and $t\in H(u,v)\setminus R$, there is
$t'\in A_u\setminus R$ such that $t'\sim_R t$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Atomic supports and relative separator calculus

declarations.title: Mixed orbit, self-side collapse, and square avoidance
declarations.heading: Atomic supports and relative separator calculus
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Mixed orbit, self-side collapse, and square avoidance]
\label{lem:rh-collapse}
Let $R$ be an equivalence support and $p$ an $R$-fixed diversity colour.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $a\ne p$ and $A_a\cap A_p\subseteq R$, then $ap$ is precisely
one diversity $R$-orbit.
\item If $c\in A_p$ and $A_c\cap A_p\subseteq R$, then
$p c=\{p\}$ and $A_c\subseteq R$.
\item Suppose $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_h\}$ is an inclusion-minimal finite
family with $\bigcap_jA_{b_j}\subseteq R$. If $b_i=p$ is $R$-fixed,
then, writing $S_i=(\bigcap_{j\ne i}A_{b_j})\setminus R$, one has
$A_a\cap S_i=\varnothing$ for every $a\in A_p$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Spoke-square localisation from the original relative separator
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Spoke-square localisation from the original relative separator]
\label{lem:rh-spoke-square-localisation}
Let $R\subseteq\mathcal D$ be an ORIGINAL global
invariant equivalence diversity support and
let $P\subseteq\mathcal D$ be a nonempty
finite set of $R$-fixed diversity colours.
Put $T=\bigcap_{p\in P}A_p$.
If $c\in T$ and $A_c\cap T\subseteq R$, then
\[
              A_c\subseteq R,
              \qquad pc=\{p\}\quad(p\in P).
\]
No globalisation of a finite one-point fibre is
assumed here. The product is the original
equality-inclusive represented RAW product.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Canonical spoke-fixer and direct finite-fibre globalisation
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical spoke-fixer and direct finite-fibre globalisation]
\label{lem:rh-direct-spoke-fixer}
Let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\subseteq M$ be
nonempty and COMPLETE, and let
$q(x/A)$ be an ACTUAL realised
one-point type with $x\notin A$.
Write $p_i=\col(x,a_i)$,
$P=\{p_i:1\le i\le n\}$, and
$Z=X_q$, with its actual
diversity palette
$T=\bigcap_{p\in P}A_p$.
Define the ORIGINAL spoke-fixer
diversity support
\[
 R_P=\{d\in\mathcal D:
                      pd=\{p\}\text{ for EVERY }p\in P\}.
\]
Then $R_P$ is a global invariant
equivalence support, and EVERY
$R_P$-class meeting $Z$ lies
wholly in $Z$; in particular
$R_P\subseteq T$.
Moreover $R_P$ is the LARGEST
global invariant equivalence
support fixing all spoke colours
in $P$.

If the realised one-point fibre
$Z$ is FINITE, then
\[
                        R_P=T,
             \qquad Z=[x]_{E_{R_P}}
                       \quad(x\in Z).
\]
The existence proof uses only ONE
internal index-two Hasse cover,
not a sequence of intermediate
globalised equivalences.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Globalisation of finite real fibres
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Globalisation of finite real fibres]\label{thm:rh-globalise}
Every finite realised one-point fibre $Z=X_q$ is exactly one class of
a parameter-free invariant finite-class equivalence. More precisely,
$T=\bigcap_i A_{p_i}$ is a global equivalence support. Every internal
saturated chain from equality to the universal equivalence of $Z$
globalises, with each successive global cover of index two.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Spoke-set criterion and uniform sizes of realised one-point fibres
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Spoke-set criterion and uniform sizes of realised one-point fibres]
\label{cor:rh-fibre-spoke-set-uniformity}
Let $P\subseteq\mathcal D$ be
a nonempty finite set of
old diversity colours realised
as the SET of spokes of
some one-point type over
a finite nonempty COMPLETE
original real base.
Put
\[
       T_P=\bigcap_{p\in P}A_p,
       \qquad
       R_P=\{d\in\mathcal D:
                            pd=\{p\}\ (p\in P)\}.
\]
For EVERY realised old
one-point type $q(x/A)$
with this same SET $P$ of
distinct spoke colours,
its real fibre $Z=X_q$
satisfies
\[
 Z=[x]_{E_{R_P}}
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                     T_P=R_P.
\]
Consequently
\[
 |Z|<\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_P=R_P\ \text{and}\ 
              [E_{R_P}:\Id]<\infty.
\]
If ONE such realised type has
finite fibre, EVERY realised
one-point type with the same
set $P$ has the SAME finite
fibre cardinality
$[E_{R_P}:\Id]$, which is a
power of two. In fact these
finite fibres are pairwise
CONJUGATE under
$\Aut(M)$, since they are
classes of the SAME invariant
equivalence in a transitive
original structure. The
statement does NOT say that
every arbitrarily prescribed
list of spokes is realisable
or that the chosen
automorphism must transport
the anchor parameters.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: A nontrivial two-point spoke-fixer fibre
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A nontrivial two-point spoke-fixer fibre]
\label{ex:rh-direct-spoke-fixer-two-point}
Let $I$ be countably infinite and let
\[
                    M=I\times\mathbb F_2\times\mathbb F_2 .
\]
Name the ORIGINAL symmetric diversity
atom $q$ for points with the same
$I$-block and first bit but opposite
second bit; name $r$ when the
$I$-block agrees but the FIRST bit
differs, regardless of the second bit;
name $b$ between different $I$-blocks.
This original one-sort complete binary
structure is homogeneous and has AP
and semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO.

For CCO, in any finite partial diagram
the specified non-$b$ edges force
common $I$-blocks. An incompatible
specified $b$ edge inside such a
connected component gives a
noncompletable SIMPLE cycle consisting
of that $b$ edge and a non-$b$ path.
Within one non-$b$ component, the
first-bit constraints are
$q$-edges of parity zero and
$r$-edges of parity one; an
inconsistent parity system gives a
specified simple cycle with odd
total parity. The second-bit
constraints occur only on $q$-edges
and require opposite bits; an
inconsistent system gives an odd
$q$-only simple cycle. Conversely,
if every specified simple cycle
homomorphically completes, none
of these inconsistencies occurs.
Solve the two parity systems
and assign distinct fresh
$I$-blocks to distinct non-$b$
connected components. This produces
one simultaneous colour-preserving
homomorphism into $M$, proving
semantic CCO. Homogeneity follows
by permutations of the $I$-blocks,
swapping the two first-bit parts
and independently swapping the
two second-bit values in each part.

Here the ORIGINAL RAW products are
\[
                  rr=\{1,q\},
                       \qquad rq=\{r\}.
\]
Fix any anchor $a=(i,0,0)$ and
the realised one-point type
$q_0(x/\{a\})$ requiring
$\col(x,a)=r$.
Its fibre is exactly
\[
        Z=\{(i,1,0),(i,1,1)\},
\]
whose original diversity palette
is $T=A_r=\{q\}$. The canonical
spoke-fixer for $P=\{r\}$ is
$R_P=\{q\}$, since $rq=\{r\}$
but $rr\ne\{r\}$ and $rb=\{b\}$.
Thus the direct theorem gives the
ACTUAL global $q$-matching class
$Z=[(i,1,0)]_{E_{R_P}}$, with
$|Z|=2$. This checks a NONSINGLETON
finite real fibre, with no choice
of an internal Hasse chain or
an artificial RAW/STRONG identity.
\end{example}

declarations.title: CCO inheritance by invariant equivalence classes
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[CCO inheritance by invariant equivalence classes]
\label{lem:rh-class-inherits}
Let $R\subseteq\mathcal D$ be a global equivalence support and $C$
any class of $E_R$. In its induced language with diversity palette
$R$, the structure on $C$ is transitive, homogeneous, triangle-defined,
and satisfies semantic homomorphic CCO (whether $C$ is finite or
infinite).
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Invariant equivalences below a class are exactly its internal equivalences
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Invariant equivalences below a class are exactly its internal equivalences]
\label{lem:rh-invariant-class-interval}
Let $E=E_R$ be ANY original
$\Aut(M)$-invariant equivalence
and let $C$ be ONE actual
$E$-class. Restriction to $C$
gives a lattice isomorphism
\[
 \{H:H\text{ an original
 invariant equivalence on }M,\
                 \Id\le H\le E\}
 \ \xrightarrow[\ \cong\ ]{\ H\mapsto H|_C\ }\
 \{\text{invariant equivalences
                    of the induced }C\}.
 \tag{CEI}\label{eq:rh-class-interval}
\]
Here the right side means
invariance under the FULL
$\Aut(C)$, not merely under a
preselected subgroup of
$\Aut(M)$.
This statement needs original
ONE-SORT homogeneous COMPLETE
BINARY atomicity and
transitivity, but neither CCO
nor SAP nor finiteness of $C$.

In particular, any internal
invariant equivalence on a
FINITE real one-point fibre $Z$
has a UNIQUE original global
invariant extension EXACT for
$Z$, once the finite-fibre
globalisation theorem has shown
that $Z$ is ONE class of its
global $E_T$. Thus the choice
of a saturated internal Hasse
chain in that theorem does not
affect the final extension.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: Relative index two throughout finite original invariant intervals
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Relative index two throughout finite original invariant intervals]
\label{cor:rh-finite-invariant-interval-index-two}
Let $E$ be an original
invariant equivalence
whose classes are FINITE.
Then EVERY Hasse cover
$H<K$ in the interval
$[\Id,E]$ of ORIGINAL
invariant equivalences
has relative index
\[
                          [K:H]=2 .
\]
Consequently every
$E$-class has size a
power of two, and the
interval $[\Id,E]$
need NOT be
distributive.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets

declarations.title: A nondistributive finite invariant interval in a genuine CCO source
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A nondistributive finite invariant interval in a genuine CCO source]
\label{ex:rh-finite-invariant-M3}
Take the one-sort original
homogeneous structure
\[
          M=I\times\mathbb F_2^2,
\]
where $I$ is countably
infinite. For distinct
$(i,u),(j,v)$ name one
symmetric old atom $b$
when $i\ne j$, and
when $i=j$ name the
three distinct atoms
$a_w$ for
$w=u+v\in\mathbb F_2^2
                  \setminus\{0\}$.
Its automorphism group
permutes the $I$-blocks
freely and independently
translates each
$\mathbb F_2^2$-block.
The finite induced age
has AP and semantic
homomorphic CCO:
the subgraph of specified
$a_w$ edges is a
group-labelled gain graph.
Its colour requirements
are soluble within each
connected component iff
the sum of labels around
every specified simple
cycle is zero.
A specified $b$-edge
between vertices in the
SAME such component
would form a forbidden
simple cycle together with
an $a_w$-path between
its endpoints.
Otherwise send different
$a_w$-components to
different $I$-blocks.
This gives one simultaneous
homomorphic completion.

Let $E$ be the original
invariant SAME-$I$-block
equivalence. Its classes
have four points and
the interval $[\Id,E]$
has exactly the THREE
different subequivalences
\[
        \Id\cup a_w
           \qquad
       (0\ne w\in\mathbb F_2^2)
\]
between $\Id$ and $E$.
They are pairwise
incomparable and meet
in $\Id$, while any two
join to $E$. Hence
$[\Id,E]$ is the
nondistributive
five-element diamond
$M_3$, although EVERY
Hasse cover has relative
index two. This is an
interval in the FULL
ORIGINAL invariant
equivalence lattice,
not an assertion that
all these relations
belong to the much
smaller FULL RAW exact
equivalence lattice.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Two-power size of finite invariant classes
declarations.heading: Internal index-two covers become global packets
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Two-power size of finite invariant classes]
\label{cor:rh-class-2power}
If $C$ is a finite class of an invariant equivalence $E_R$, then
\[
             |C|=2^m\quad\text{for some }0\le m\le |R|.
\]
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Fixed-family relative pseudocomplement
declarations.heading: Relative pseudocomplements and looped descent
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Fixed-family relative pseudocomplement]
\label{lem:rh-pseudo}
Let $R$ be a global equivalence support and let $P\subseteq\mathcal D$
be a finite nonempty set of $R$-fixed colours. Put
\[
 S_P=\bigcap_{p\in P}A_p,
 \qquad W_R(P)=\{a\in\mathcal D:A_a\cap S_P\subseteq R\}.
\]
Then $W_R(P)$ is a global equivalence support.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Relative pseudocomplements and looped descent

declarations.title: Carrier insertion
declarations.heading: Relative pseudocomplements and looped descent
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Carrier insertion]\label{lem:rh-carrier}
Suppose $P\subseteq\mathcal D$ is a finite nonempty family of spoke
colours and $b$ is an additional spoke colour; they can be jointly
realised around one new point by AP. Put
\[
 S=\bigcap_{p\in P}A_p,\qquad C=S\cap A_b.
\]
If $r\in L\cap S\cap\langle A_b\rangle$, then
$L\cap C\ne\varnothing$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Relative pseudocomplements and looped descent

declarations.title: Looped diagonal Helly
declarations.heading: Relative pseudocomplements and looped descent
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Looped diagonal Helly]\label{lem:rh-loophelly}
For every finite family of diversity colours $p_1,\dots,p_n$,
\[
 L\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^n\langle A_{p_i}\rangle\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 L\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^n A_{p_i}\ne\varnothing.
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Even-walk classes
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Canonical algebraic hull for real points
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Canonical algebraic hull for real points]
\label{thm:rh-hull}
Let $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_n\}\subseteq M$ be finite and
$x\in\operatorname{acl}_M(A)\setminus A$. Put
$p_i=\col(x,a_i)$, $k=\max\{1,|\mathcal D|\}$ and let
$R_k(3)$ be the multicolour Ramsey number for a monochromatic
triangle in a complete graph with $k$ edge colours. Then
\[
 \left|\bigcap_{i=1}^n[a_i]_{E_{\Gamma(p_i)}}\right|<R_k(3).
\]
In particular, the intersection is finite. The bound is uniform
in $A$ and $x$. This statement uses no BBGTV or CFSG, only the
standing hypotheses and the stated Erd\H{o}s and standard Ramsey
theorems.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: A two-power bound on canonical real hulls
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[A two-power bound on canonical real hulls]
\label{cor:rh-hull-2power}
In the nontrivial case of Theorem~\ref{thm:rh-hull}, put
$J=\bigcap_{a\in A}\Gamma(\col(x,a))$.  The canonical real hull
$C=\bigcap_{a\in A}[a]_{E_{\Gamma(\col(x,a))}}$ satisfies
\[
       |C|=2^m\le 2^{|J|}\le 2^{|\mathcal D|}
       \qquad\text{for some integer }m\ge0.
\]
The same assertion holds for $A=\varnothing$ and finite $M$, with
$J=\mathcal D$ and $C=M$. This supplies an additional explicit bound
and a two-power restriction for an already finite canonical hull;
it does not replace the preceding proof of its finiteness.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Exponential palette cost of minimal infinite directions
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exponential palette cost of minimal infinite directions]
\label{lem:rh-direction-palette-bound}
Let $F=\Sigma(\Id)$ be the greatest finite-class ORIGINAL invariant
equivalence and let $E_1,\ldots,E_r$ list all minimal infinite
ORIGINAL invariant equivalences (with $r=0$ if $M$ is finite).
Here and in the next two corollaries we abbreviate
$\mathcal D\setminus F=\{a\in\mathcal D:a\not\subseteq F\}$
and
$\mathcal D\cap F=\{a\in\mathcal D:a\subseteq F\}$
as SETS OF ATOM NAMES, not literal set operations between
binary relations and names.
Then
\[
   2^r-1\le|\mathcal D\setminus F|,
   \qquad
   r\le\left\lfloor
       \log_2\bigl(|\mathcal D\setminus F|+1\bigr)
                         \right\rfloor.
\]
All the counted colours are distinct ACTUAL original diversity
orbitals outside $F$; $F$ is NOT assumed exact.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Bounded character of real algebraic closure
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Bounded character of real algebraic closure]
\label{cor:rh-acl-bounded-character}
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_r$ list all inclusion-minimal ORIGINAL invariant
equivalences with infinite real classes.  Then
$r\le\lfloor\log_2(|\mathcal D\setminus F|+1)\rfloor\le|\mathcal D|$
by \cref{lem:rh-direction-palette-bound}, and
for every finite real $A\subseteq M$,
\[
   \operatorname{acl}_M(A)=
   \bigcup_{\substack{B\subseteq A\\|B|\le r}}
                 \operatorname{acl}_M(B).
\]
For $x\notin A$, this follows from the exact colour criterion
\[
 x\in\operatorname{acl}_M(A)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{for every }i\le r\text{ some }a\in A
 \text{ satisfies }E_i\nsubseteq
       E_{\Gamma(\col(x,a))}.
\]
Here $\Gamma(p)=\langle\{p\}\rangle$ is the ORIGINAL generated
equivalence support, not an exact quotient kernel.  If $M$ is
finite then $r=0$ and $\operatorname{acl}_M(\varnothing)=M$.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Polynomial growth and finite-packet bound for real algebraic closure
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Polynomial growth and finite-packet bound for real algebraic closure]
\label{cor:rh-acl-polynomial-growth}
Assume $M$ is infinite and let $F=\Sigma(\Id)$.
Write $f=|\mathcal D\cap F|$,
$d_\infty=|\mathcal D\setminus F|$ and
$c=|[x]_{E_F}|$, the constant finite size of any
original $F$-class.  Then $c\le 2^f$, and for
every finite real $A$ of size $n$,
\[
 |\operatorname{acl}_M(A)|
 \le c\left(n+
      \sum_{j=1}^{\min\{r,n\}}
           \binom{n}{j}d_\infty^j\right),
 \qquad
 r\le\left\lfloor\log_2(d_\infty+1)\right\rfloor.
\]
In particular $|\operatorname{acl}_M(A)|=O_M(n^r)$.
Moreover $\operatorname{acl}_M(A)$ is a union of COMPLETE
original $F$-classes, and the number of those classes is at most
$n+\sum_{j=1}^{\min\{r,n\}}\binom{n}{j}d_\infty^j$.
If $F=\Id$, then
$\operatorname{acl}_M(A)=\operatorname{dcl}_M(A)$
for every finite REAL $A$, although this closure may
strictly contain $A$.
No analogous assertion for arbitrary imaginary sorts is made.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Sharp closure exponent in coordinate sources
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Sharp closure exponent in coordinate sources]
\label{ex:rh-acl-polynomial-sharp}
For each $r\ge2$ let $M_r=\mathbb N^r$ and name the symmetric
diversity atom of distinct $x,y$ by the nonempty difference
support $\{i:x_i\ne y_i\}\subseteq[r]$.  Its automorphism group
is $\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)$: named atoms
preserve each coordinate equality, while independent coordinate
permutations preserve all atoms.  Thus it is homogeneous.
Every triangle-legal complete diagram induces one equivalence
relation of coordinate equality for each $i$; these can be
realised independently on $\mathbb N$, and their meet is real
identity because every specified diversity support is nonempty.
Hence the age is triangle-defined and has AP.

It also has semantic homomorphic CCO: an inconsistent
coordinate equality/disequality specification has a specified
inequality edge whose endpoints are connected by a path
of equality edges in that coordinate.  A shortest such path
together with the inequality edge is a specified simple
cycle without a homomorphism.  If no such obstruction exists
in any coordinate, assign different values to the finitely many
equality components independently, giving a homomorphism of
the entire partial diagram.

Its invariant equivalences are exactly those allowing changes
within a fixed set of coordinates: if an equivalence contains
an atom with difference support $S$, a two-step path of that
same atom (using a fresh third value in coordinate $i$)
forces each singleton difference support $\{i\}$ for $i\in S$;
single-coordinate steps then generate the whole corresponding
coordinate-change equivalence.  Thus there are precisely $r$
minimal infinite equivalences.  For
$A_n=\{(k,\ldots,k):1\le k\le n\}$, the pointwise stabiliser fixes
every tuple in $[n]^r$ and has infinite orbit on any tuple
with a coordinate outside $[n]$.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{acl}_{M_r}(A_n)
 =\operatorname{dcl}_{M_r}(A_n)=[n]^r,\qquad
 |\operatorname{acl}_{M_r}(A_n)|=n^r.
\]
The polynomial exponent $r$ is therefore optimal even
for definable closure.
\end{example}

declarations.title: SAP forces a common infinite invariant monolith
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[SAP forces a common infinite invariant monolith]
\label{lem:rh-sap-invariant-monolith}
Let $M$ be an INFINITE transitive homogeneous structure
with SAP, in a finite COMPLETE BINARY original language.
No symmetry, CCO, distributivity or triangle constraints
are needed. For any TWO nonidentity original invariant
equivalences $E,F>\Id$, their actual intersection
$E\cap F$ has INFINITE classes.

Consequently the finite FULL invariant-equivalence lattice
has a UNIQUE least nonidentity element $L>\Id$, whose
classes are infinite. The greatest finite-class original
equivalence is $F_{\mathrm{fin}}=\Id$; in the notation of
\cref{cor:rh-acl-bounded-character} there is exactly
ONE minimal infinite direction ($r=1$), including
$L=\Top$ when the source is primitive.
Moreover $\operatorname{acl}_M(A)=A$ for EVERY finite
ORIGINAL REAL $A$. These SAP conclusions do NOT
hold for AP-only sources such as $M_r=\mathbb N^r$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Infinite joint real fibre of all proper MI quotient coordinates
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Infinite joint real fibre of all proper MI quotient coordinates]
\label{cor:rh-sap-mi-joint-real-fibre}
Let $M$ be an INFINITE transitive homogeneous
finite COMPLETE BINARY original structure
with SAP, with no symmetry or CCO assumption.
Let $L>\Id$ be its unique least nonidentity
ORIGINAL invariant equivalence from
\cref{lem:rh-sap-invariant-monolith}.
Let $\mathcal I^\times$ be the set of
ALL proper NONIDENTITY meet-irreducible
equivalences in the FULL original invariant
lattice. (The original REAL identity is
EXCLUDED, even if it is meet-irreducible.)
With the empty meet interpreted as $\Top$,
\[
           \boxed{\quad
                L=\bigcap_{J\in\mathcal I^\times}J.
                 \quad}
 \tag{MK}\label{eq:rh-sap-mi-meet}
\]
Thus the ACTUAL map on original real points
\[
          \Phi(x)=([x]_J)_{J\in\mathcal I^\times}
\]
has infinite real fibres:
\[
        \Phi^{-1}(\Phi(x))=[x]_L,\qquad
        \left|\Aut(M/\Phi(x))\cdot x\right|
                    =|[x]_L|=\infty.
\]
If $\mathcal I^\times=\varnothing$
(the primitive case), then $L=\Top$,
the empty tuple is fixed, and the sole
fibre is all of $M$.  The statement
concerns an ACTUALLY REALISED full tuple
of MI quotient values, not an arbitrary
tuple of classes. It does not assert
SAP for a hidden language naming
additional non-MI exact quotients.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Infinite Helly intersections of proper original exact classes under SAP
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Infinite Helly intersections of proper original exact classes under SAP]
\label{cor:rh-sap-infinite-exact-helly}
Let $M$ be an infinite transitive homogeneous
finite complete SYMMETRIC BINARY original
structure with SAP and semantic
HOMOMORPHIC CCO. Let
$E_1,\ldots,E_m>\Id$ be any nonidentity
FULL RAW exact original invariant
equivalences on the SAME original
real sort, and choose actual
classes $C_i=[x_i]_{E_i}$.
If all $C_i$ meet pairwise, then
\[
    \boxed{\quad\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i
                  \ \text{is INFINITE}.\quad}
\]
More precisely, with
$L=\bigcap_{i=1}^m E_i$,
the intersection is ONE entire
$L$-class; $L>\Id$ and every
$L$-class is infinite.
If in addition the source is TERMINAL
(full invariant-equivalence NR2), the
result holds for ALL nonidentity
original invariant equivalences:
no separate exactness assumption is
needed by
\cref{lem:typed-terminal-all-equivalences-exact}.
For $m=0$ the intersection is the
whole infinite original sort.
For an identity kernel the infinite-size
conclusion is NOT asserted.

In particular, in the terminal setting,
a FULL tuple of proper nonidentity
meet-irreducible original quotient
classes is realised by an original
REAL point if and only if the classes
are PAIRWISE compatible. Whenever
realised, their entire common
real fibre is precisely one
INFINITE class of the unique original
SAP monolith $L$ by
\cref{cor:rh-sap-mi-joint-real-fibre}.
This is an original real-incidence
statement and does NOT imply SAP
after naming arbitrary NON-MI
exact meet quotient sorts.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull

declarations.title: Two-coordinate real algebraic corners
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Two-coordinate real algebraic corners]\label{ex:two-coordinate}
The absolute real algebraic closure in the hull theorem need not be
$F[A]$, even when the finite-class packet bottom $F$ is regular and
thin.  Let $G=\mathbb F_2$ and take
$M_*=\mathbb N\times\mathbb N\times G$.  For two distinct triples
$(r,c,g)$ and $(r',c',g')$, name the fine colour by the three data
$(\mathbf 1_{r=r'},\mathbf 1_{c=c'},g+g')$.  The only missing triple
$(1,1,0)$ denotes equality, so the diversity palette has seven
colours.  Every named colour is symmetric.

This is a transitive homogeneous, triangle-defined AP source with
semantic homomorphic CCO.  Indeed finite partial isomorphisms extend
by independently permuting the two infinite coordinates and by a
single translation of $G$.  In a complete diagram, legality of all
triangles makes each coordinate-equality relation transitive and makes
the prescribed $G$-differences a coboundary; the absent equality colour
prevents two distinct vertices from receiving the same triple.  For a
partial diagram, each specified edge imposes equality or inequality in
each infinite coordinate and one $G$-difference.  Inconsistency of
an equality/inequality system has an inequality edge joined by a path
of equality edges; inconsistency of the $G$-differences has a cycle
with nonzero total difference.  Each obstruction contains a specified
simple cycle without a homomorphism.  Conversely, in the absence of
such obstructions the equality components can be assigned distinct
coordinate values and the $G$-differences integrated.  This proves
semantic homomorphic CCO, not merely ordinary AP.

Here $F$ consists of the two-point packets
$\{(r,c,0),(r,c,1)\}$.  For
$a=(0,1,0)$, $b=(1,0,0)$ and $x=(0,0,0)$, the two colours
$\col(x,a)=(1,0,0)$ and $\col(x,b)=(0,1,0)$ determine $x$
uniquely.  Hence
\[
 x\in\operatorname{dcl}_M(\{a,b\})\setminus F[\{a,b\}].
\]
The two infinite exact equivalences generated by these colours are,
respectively, equality of the first coordinate and $G$-coordinate,
and equality of the second coordinate and $G$-coordinate.  Their
intersection is equality; the finite intersection in the hull theorem
is exactly $\{x\}$.  Thus the full canonical-hull argument is genuinely
stronger than closure under finite packets.  This example does not
contradict the \emph{relative} owner-closure theorem below, where
additional owner imaginaries are named.
\end{example}

declarations.title: The thin phase packet need not be exact
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The thin phase packet need not be exact]
\label{rem:phase-thin-not-exact}
In the same Cartesian phase model, the two-element packet
$F[(r,c,g)]=\{(r,c,0),(r,c,1)\}$ is a raw invariant
finite-class equivalence but is \emph{not} exact.  Indeed each
raw atom specifies a fixed phase difference in $\mathbb F_2$.
Consequently every nonempty atomic word profile has a single
fixed endpoint phase difference, equal to the sum of the
letters' phase differences.  An intersection of word profiles
has the same property whenever it is nonempty.  The only exact
support obtained from the empty defining family is $\Top$.
Since the proper equivalence $F$ contains both equality
(phase difference $0$) and the thin flip orbital (phase
difference $1$), it is not exact.  The same parity argument
excludes the invariant equivalences ``same row irrespective of
phase'' and ``same column irrespective of phase'' from the
proper exact supports.  This is a concrete reason for retaining
\emph{exactness} in the quotient theorems; arbitrary raw invariant
quotients are not interchangeable with exact quotients.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Scope of the CCO substitution
declarations.heading: Even walks and the canonical finite algebraic hull
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope of the CCO substitution]
The proof applies to the \emph{actual real} structure $M$ and its realised
one-point fibres over finite real sets. It does not prove the stronger
AP-only version of the hull theorem or assert CCO inheritance to arbitrary
nonexact imaginary sorts. Corollary~\ref{cor:hasse}, rather than the
finite-group classification used in the original AP-only proof, is the
entire finite-cover input here.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Harmless owners contain all minimal directions
declarations.heading: Harmless quotient owners in the full invariant lattice
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Harmless owners contain all minimal directions]
\label{lem:acf-harmless-owners}
In any standing infinite source, naming finitely many quotient
classes of an invariant equivalence $H$ does not increase
\emph{real} algebraic closure if and only if $H$ contains
all inclusion-minimal infinite equivalences.  The same holds
simultaneously for finitely many such sorts.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Correspondence equivalence and gluing dichotomy
declarations.heading: The global correspondence cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Correspondence equivalence and gluing dichotomy]
\label{lem:global-correspondence}
Assume $M$ has no invariant finite-class exact equivalence
strictly above $\Id$, and let $E$ be a nonidentity exact
invariant equivalence of $M$.  The support $R_E$ is an invariant equivalence containing $F$,
and $E\cap R_E=H=E\cap F$.  If $R_E\ne F$, then there is a
nonidentity infinite exact invariant equivalence $C$ such that
$E\cap C=\Id$.  Both actual exact quotients $M/E$ and
$M/C$ have strictly fewer original diversity orbitals.
No EPPA hypothesis is used in this structural dichotomy.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Direct unary real closure and harmless actual owners
declarations.heading: The global correspondence cut
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Direct unary real closure and harmless actual owners]
\label{lem:consolidated-unary-closure}
Suppose $M$ is infinite, with unique minimal infinite invariant
equivalence $E$, and let $F=\Sigma(\Id)$ be its greatest finite-class
equivalence.  Then for every finite real $A$,
\[
                  \operatorname{acl}_M(A)=F[A].
\]
Naming finitely many actual $E$-owner classes does not enlarge
real algebraic closure.  Hence in an owner-named union $N_B$
over any finite $G$-invariant owner set $B$ of a fully normalised
source, real closure is precisely $F[-]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Strong amalgamation of full packets]
\label{cor:relative-closed-sap}
The finite induced owner-typed structures in $N_B$ that
are closed under $F$ strongly amalgamate over their

declarations.title: The all-owner primitive transversal
declarations.heading: The residual full-owner primitive transversal, directly
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[The all-owner primitive transversal]
\label{thm:joint-transversal}
\label{lem:full-owner-transversal}
Let $\mathcal U_B$ comprise finite owner-typed diagrams
realised in $N_B$ on vertices from pairwise distinct
full $F$-packets.  Its pair palettes are
\[
          P_{st}=L_{st}\setminus F\qquad(s,t\in B),
\]
with only diversity colours between distinct formal points,
even for repeated owner names.  Then $\mathcal U_B$ is
triangle-defined, has JEP and SAP, and satisfies semantic
homomorphic CCO with injective packet-separated completions.
Every individual owner sort is primitive.  The Fra\"isse
limit $U_B$ recovers $N_B$ under full $G$-packet inflation:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-owner-inflation}
 \operatorname{own}(x,g)=g\operatorname{own}(x),\qquad
 \col((x,g),(y,h))=(g+h)\col(x,y)\quad(x\ne y).
\end{equation}
The group $\Gamma=\Aut(B)$ permutes only the owner tags
and fixes the literal raw fine-colour names.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Absorption by a full typed palette
declarations.heading: A finite bad-cycle bound on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Absorption by a full typed palette]
\label{lem:locality-absorb}
For every triple of owner sorts $s,t,u$, and every nonempty
atomic subsets $A\subseteq P_{st}$, $B\subseteq P_{tu}$,
not necessarily original exact menus, one has
\[
 A*P_{tu}=P_{su},\qquad P_{st}*B=P_{su}.
\]
In particular $A*P_{tt}=P_{st}$ and
$P_{st}*a=P_{su}$ for any atom $a\in P_{tu}$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Every nonempty primitive loop palette eventually fills
declarations.heading: A finite bad-cycle bound on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Every nonempty primitive loop palette eventually fills]
\label{lem:locality-positive}
On a primitive named sort $t$, let $\varnothing\ne W\subseteq
P_{tt}$ be an arbitrary atomic subset, with no assumption that
$W$ is an original exact menu or a represented word profile.
Put $m=|P_{tt}|\ge1$. Then
\[
                 W^{*2m}=P_{tt}
       \quad\text{and}\quad
                 W^{*n}=P_{tt}\quad(n\ge2m).
\]
Thus the eventual-fullness exponent is UNIFORM in the
nonempty atomic subset $W$, and the statement does not
merely assert eventual stabilization of its powers.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Bounded cycle-obstruction locality
declarations.heading: A finite bad-cycle bound on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Bounded cycle-obstruction locality]
\label{thm:locality-bound}
The proper-profile automaton is acyclic. There is an integer $\ell$
such that every positive typed word longer than $\ell$ has its full
endpoint palette as profile. One may take
\[
 \ell\le\max_s\sum_t(2^{|P_{st}|}-2).
\]
Every noncompletable simple typed cycle has length at most
$b=\max\{3,\ell+1\}$. In particular, by semantic homomorphic CCO,
a finite typed partial diagram can be completed whenever all its
specified cycles of length at most $b$ admit a typed completion.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Binary/unary irreducible substructures are covered pairwise by local closed supports
declarations.heading: Local irreducible supports in binary/unary partial structures
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Binary/unary irreducible substructures are covered pairwise by local closed supports]
\label{lem:typed-binary-irreducible-local-cover}
Let \(C\) be a finite
PARTIAL relational
structure with total
named UNARY functions
and relational symbols
of arity AT MOST TWO,
closed under all the
named functions.
For every vertex \(v\in C\)
form the closed support
\(\cl_C\{v\}\).
For every ACTUALLY
DISPLAYED binary relation
tuple on two distinct
vertices \(u,v\in C\),
also form the closed
support \(\cl_C\{u,v\}\).
Let \(\mathscr H(C)\)
be this finite family
of induced functionally
closed substructures.

Then for EVERY nonempty
functionally closed
IRREDUCIBLE induced
substructure \(D\subseteq C\),
and EVERY pair of distinct
vertices \(x,y\in D\),
SOME member of
\(\mathscr H(D)\)
contains BOTH \(x,y\).

Consequently, if
\(f:C\to H\) is a
sort- and
unary-function-preserving
homomorphism to a
COMPLETE target, and
\(f|_A\) is an induced
EMBEDDING for every
\(A\in\mathscr H(C)\),
then \(f\) is a
HOMOMORPHISM-EMBEDDING
on all of \(C\):
its restriction to EVERY
source irreducible
substructure is an
embedding.

This conclusion is
specific to the binary
relational/unary-functional
signature. For a higher
arity relation, pairwise
reflection does NOT
by itself reflect a
missing tuple of
three or more roots.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Local irreducible supports in binary/unary partial structures

declarations.title: HN irreducibility forces completed unary-generated diagrams
declarations.heading: Local irreducible supports in binary/unary partial structures
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[HN irreducibility forces completed unary-generated diagrams]
\label{lem:hn-irreducible-forces-unary-admissible}
Let $L$ be a finite many-sorted language with arbitrary
relational symbols and only UNARY function symbols.
In this lemma, function symbols of a finite PARTIAL
$L$-structure $C$ are permitted to have proper domains,
as in the HN 2019 finite-model convention.
An induced $L$-substructure means an EMBEDDED one:
its inclusion reflects not only relations but also
the DOMAINS of all partially defined functions.
Thus a substructure containing $x$ necessarily
contains the value of every unary function which
is already defined at $x$ in $C$.

Let $\mathcal K$ be any class of finite COMPLETED
$L$-structures whose named unary functions are
TOTAL on their intended input sorts.
Assume EVERY irreducible induced $L$-substructure
of $C$ is an ACTUAL member of $\mathcal K$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every $x\in C$, the substructure
$U_x=\cl_C\{x\}$ generated by all iterated
ALREADY DEFINED unary values is IRREDUCIBLE,
and belongs to $\mathcal K$.
\item Consequently every intended unary function
is already TOTAL in $C$ on its named input sort,
and every actual unary term identity valid in
$\mathcal K$ holds in $C$ pointwise.
\item If all completed one-generated $\mathcal K$
members have size at most $m$, then
$|U_x|\le m$ for EVERY $x\in C$, and
$|\cl_C(B)|\le m|B|$ for each finite
generator set $B\subseteq C$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular the HN local-finiteness requirement
that every irreducible substructure of $C$
already belong to the completed target age
implies the unary-admissibility condition needed
for the RESTRICTED hidden bounded-obstruction
theorem, even though the ambient HN language
permits PARTIAL unary functions.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Local irreducible supports in binary/unary partial structures
