declarations.title: Universal irreflexive edge restores local irreducible reflection
declarations.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Universal irreflexive edge restores local irreducible reflection]
\label{lem:typed-universal-edge-hn-reflection}
Let $L$ be a finite many-sorted language with unary functions and relations
of arbitrary finite arity. Let $\mathcal K$ be a hereditary class of
completed induced unary-closed $L$-structures such that every
$L$-homomorphism-embedding between two members of $\mathcal K$ is an
embedding. This condition holds, in particular, if every completed member
is irreducible, or if every homomorphism between completed members is an
embedding. Positive binary coverage of every distinct pair is a sufficient
condition by \cref{lem:typed-unary-binary-irreducibility}.

Expand each member by a universal irreflexive binary relation $E_*$, and
write $\mathcal K^*$ for the resulting class. Let $C$ be a finite partial
$(L\cup\{E_*\})$-structure whose every induced irreducible substructure
belongs to $\mathcal K^*$. If its $L$-reduct $C^-$ has an
$L$-homomorphism-embedding $h:C^-\to H$, where $H\in\mathcal K$, then
\emph{the same vertex map} is a homomorphism-embedding $C\to H^*$.
Global injectivity of $h$ is not asserted.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer

declarations.title: The completed-map rigidity hypothesis cannot be omitted
declarations.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The completed-map rigidity hypothesis cannot be omitted]
\label{rem:typed-universal-edge-old-completeness}
Take the empty relational/function language and let $\mathcal K$ be all
finite sets. It is hereditary and has SAP, but the constant map from a
two-point set to a singleton is a homomorphism-embedding, since its old
irreducible pieces are singletons. Let $C$ be a two-point member of
$\mathcal K^*$ with $E_*$ on its distinct pair. Every irreducible source
piece is completed, but the constant map from $C^-$ to a singleton does
not preserve $E_*$: it sends its edge to a forbidden diagonal.
A different injective completion of $C$ exists; the failure concerns only
transport of the \emph{same} arbitrary old map. Thus some completed-map
rigidity is necessary for this general argument. Binary completeness is
one sufficient hypothesis, not a necessary one: unary-generated
irreducibility can provide the same rigidity.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Unary HN transfer from irreducible-source obstructions
declarations.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Unary HN transfer from irreducible-source obstructions]
\label{thm:unary-hn-irreducible-source-transfer}
Let $L$ be a finite many-sorted language with relations of arbitrary finite
arity and only unary functions. Let $\mathcal K$ be a hereditary class of
finite completed induced unary-closed \emph{irreducible} $L$-structures
with SAP. Suppose there is an integer $N$ such that every finite partial
$L$-structure $C$ satisfying
\[
  \text{every induced irreducible substructure of $C$ belongs to
  $\mathcal K$}
\]
and having no $\mathcal K$-homomorphism-embedding completion contains an
induced unary-closed noncompletable substructure of size at most $N$.
Then the class $\mathcal K^<$ of all members with arbitrary strict linear
orders is locally finite in the class of all finite ordered $L$-models,
in the sense of \cite[Definition~2.8]{HN-Ramsey}, with the uniform bound
$n=\max\{1,N\}$. Consequently $\mathcal K^<$ is Ramsey.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer

declarations.title: Direct unary HN transfer for irreducible SAP ages
declarations.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Direct unary HN transfer for irreducible SAP ages]
\label{thm:typed-direct-irreducible-unary-HN}
Let $L$ be a finite many-sorted language with relations of arbitrary finite
arity and only total unary functions on their prescribed source sorts.
Let $\mathcal K$ be a hereditary class of finite induced unary-closed
irreducible $L$-structures with SAP. Suppose there is one integer $N$
such that every noncompletable finite partial $L$-structure whose every
one-generated induced closure is already a completed member of
$\mathcal K$ contains an induced unary-closed noncompletable substructure
of size at most $N$. Completions here are homomorphism-embeddings.
Then $\mathcal K^<$, with arbitrary strict linear orders, is locally
finite with bound $\max\{1,N\}$ and is Ramsey.

The obstruction premise is required only on this unary-admissible domain;
no bound for arbitrary malformed unary cycles is assumed. No positive
binary pair cover, auxiliary universal relation, CCO or exact geometry
is part of this abstract theorem.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer

declarations.title: A unary homogeneous finite-obstruction Ramsey transfer
declarations.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[A unary homogeneous finite-obstruction Ramsey transfer]
\label{thm:typed-abstract-unary-HN-ramsey}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:typed-direct-irreducible-unary-HN},
replace the irreducibility assumption by the following sufficient
condition: the relational symbols have arity at most two, and in every
completed member every ordered pair of distinct vertices is covered by a
positive named binary relation. Then the same Ramsey conclusion holds.
In particular, the bounded-obstruction hypothesis remains restricted to
sources with completed one-generated closures; it is not supplied by
binary coverage or by this theorem.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Unary completion and ordered Ramsey transfer

declarations.title: Typed Set-Pasch from original strong amalgamation
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed Set-Pasch from original strong amalgamation]
\label{lem:typed-set-pasch}
In any finite complete typed binary SAP source as above,
including the later terminal original-sort source, let
$i,j,k,\ell$ be named sorts, possibly repeated, and let
$A\subseteq L_{ij}$,
$B\subseteq L_{jk}$, $C\subseteq L_{i\ell}$,
$D\subseteq L_{\ell k}$ be nonempty diversity
menus.  Then
\[
 (A*B)\cap(C*D)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 (\bar A*C)\cap(B*\bar D)\ne\varnothing.
\]
No exactness, primitivity, CCO, or identity atom is
required; every displayed product is the genuine STRONG
diversity product between pairwise distinct points.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal

declarations.title: The off-diagonal identity firewall
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The off-diagonal identity firewall]
\label{rem:typed-identity-firewall}
Some ordinary endpoint formalisms adjoin an artificial identity atom
$1_i$ to the loop palette and close under unital products and meets.
The resulting \emph{unital envelope} $\mathrm{OEnd}(i,i)$ need not equal
\eqref{eq:typed-H-definition}.  Its menu $\{1_i\}$ can be artificial
on a pair of distinct formal vertices.  Our $\mathcal H_{ii}$ is the
\emph{strong} family $\mathrm{SEnd}(i,i)$: it consists exclusively of
nonempty \emph{diversity} menus, with no freely adjoined equality.
In particular no equality survivor appears in the arguments below.
For example, a single-sort class with only one diversity colour
$f$ has strong off-diagonal family $\{\{f\}\}$, while its formal
unital envelope also contains the artificial singleton $\{1_i\}$.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Injectivising typed homomorphisms over fixed roots
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Injectivising typed homomorphisms over fixed roots]
\label{lem:typed-injectivisation}
For this lemma, let $U$ be any homogeneous complete binary relational
structure on named sorts whose age has SAP. No CCO, primitivity or
relative-index assumption is required.
Let $P$ be any finite partial diagram on the named sorts of $U$, with
only diversity atoms on specified edges.  Let $f:P\to U$ be a
colour- and sort-preserving homomorphism, and let $S\subseteq V(P)$
be a set of designated vertices on which $f$ is injective.  For any
finite $Z\subseteq U\setminus f(S)$ there is an \emph{injective}
colour- and sort-preserving homomorphism $f':P\to U$ such that
$f'|_S=f|_S$ and $f'(V(P)\setminus S)\cap Z=\varnothing$.

In particular, for every positive typed word $w$ of diversity atoms,
its represented endpoint relation on \emph{distinct} vertices has
exactly the strong word profile of $w$.  If a represented word includes
identity factors, they may be deleted first; an all-identity word has
an empty diversity guard.  Thus represented multiplication followed
by restriction to a diversity pair palette and strong multiplication
agree on the positive words used in this section.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal

declarations.title: SAP-upgraded semantic CCO cycle criterion
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[SAP-upgraded semantic CCO cycle criterion]
\label{lem:typed-strong-cycle-completion}
Let $U$ be a homogeneous finite-complete named-sorted binary
RELATIONAL structure whose old finite age has SAP and semantic
HOMOMORPHIC CCO. Let $P$ be a finite typed partial diagram in
which every specified pair has ONE legal old DIVERSITY atomic
colour (with its correctly typed converse); all other pairs
are unrecorded. Then $P$ has an INJECTIVE colour-preserving
completion on its original formal vertex set if and only if
EVERY specified simple cycle of $P$ has a colour-preserving
HOMOMORPHISM to $U$.

If $P$ contains a prescribed complete old base $D$, the
injective completion can fix one prescribed actual copy
of $D$. No artificial STRONG identity edges, higher-arity
constraints or partial functions are included.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal

declarations.title: The strong guard needs SAP
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[The strong guard needs SAP]
\label{ex:typed-walk-SAP-sharp}
The distinction above is real without SAP, even for a symmetric
triangle-defined homogeneous CCO source.  In the four-point
translation structure $\mathbb F_2^2$ of
Example~\ref{ex:exact-ball-sharp}, choose distinct nonzero
$d,e\in\mathbb F_2^2$ and consider the positive diversity word
$w=(a_d,a_d,a_e)$.  Its represented relation between distinct
endpoints is the diversity atom $a_e$: the only walk starting at
$x$ is $x,x+d,x,x+e$.  But this walk repeats its first vertex at
the third position, and no injective realisation of this labelled
path exists.  Thus the guarded represented profile is nonempty
while the corresponding strong profile is empty.  The original
four-point age has AP but not SAP, since two copies of the unique
$a_d$-neighbour of a vertex cannot be strongly amalgamated over
that vertex.  This is \emph{not} a counterexample to the strong
typed calculus, which is invoked only after the full-owner
transversal has been shown to have SAP.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Strong typed theta semantics and $2$-Helly
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Strong typed theta semantics and $2$-Helly]
\label{lem:typed-helly}
For fixed $(i,j)$, every finite pairwise-intersecting family of
positive typed word profiles has nonempty total intersection.
Consequently every finite pairwise-intersecting family in
$\mathcal H_{ij}$ has nonempty total intersection; a nonempty
intersection of exact menus is exact.  Moreover every
$D\in\mathcal H_{ij}$ is exactly the set of possible atomic colours
between two distinct roots of types $(i,j)$ in a finite strongly
completable typed path diagram.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal

declarations.title: Exact products and finite-meet distributivity
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact products and finite-meet distributivity]
\label{lem:typed-exact-products}
Every $\mathcal H_{ij}$ contains every singleton atom and its typed
top, is closed under converse and nonempty intersections, and the
family $\mathcal H$ is closed under compatible strong products.
More precisely, for presentations
$A=\bigcap_{r}P_r\in\mathcal H_{ij}$,
$B=\bigcap_{s}Q_s\in\mathcal H_{jk}$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:typed-exact-product}
 A*B=\bigcap_{r,s}(P_r*Q_s),
\end{equation}
with the usual convention that a typed top imposes no restriction.
For a finite nonempty exact meet $B=\bigcap_sB_s$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:typed-distrib}
 A*B=\bigcap_s(A*B_s),\qquad
 B*Q=\bigcap_s(B_s*Q)
\end{equation}
for every compatible exact $A,Q$.  All displayed products and the
nonempty intersections on the right belong to the indicated exact
families.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal

declarations.title: Exact triple occurrence
declarations.heading: Strong typed exact domains on the primitive transversal
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact triple occurrence]\label{lem:typed-triple-occurrence}
Three menus $A\in\mathcal H_{ij}$, $B\in\mathcal H_{jk}$,
$C\in\mathcal H_{ik}$ occur simultaneously as the \emph{exact
strong} endpoint domains of three distinct designated vertices in
a finite completable typed partial diagram if and only if
$\mathrm{PC}_{ijk}(A,B,C)$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Profile Helly converse
declarations.heading: Completion from positive profile Helly
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Profile Helly converse]\label{lem:helly-to-cco}
Let a finite symmetric typed atomic palette have a total associative Peircean
product and a nonempty diversity palette for every permitted ordered
pair of vertex sorts. Consider the FULL triangle-defined class of all complete atomic
networks admitted by this table. If its reachable profiles are
\(2\)-Helly, then this class satisfies semantic CCO. If, in
addition, the required atomic forks are realisable by distinct
vertices, then this full complete class has SAP.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Canonical typed exact fixed-point domains
declarations.heading: Strong typed path-consistency fixed-point semantics
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical typed exact fixed-point domains]
\label{lem:typed-PC-fixedpoint-exact}
Let $\Dat^{ab}$ consist of all NONEMPTY
$D^\infty_G(x,y)$ where $x,y$ are DISTINCT
formal vertices of sorts $(a,b)$ in some
finite strongly completable old partial graph.
Then
\[
 \boxed{\Dat^{ab}=\mathcal H_{ab}
 =\{\bigcap\mathcal F:
     \mathcal F\subseteq\Rch^{ab}\text{ finite},
     \ \bigcap\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\}.}
\]
Every finite pairwise-intersecting family in
one $\Dat^{ab}$ has nonempty intersection.
For three distinct root vertices of sorts
$a,b,c$, domains $A\in\Dat^{ab}$,
$B\in\Dat^{bc}$ and $C\in\Dat^{ac}$
occur simultaneously as their three PC
fixed-point domains in a finite strongly
completable old typed partial graph if and
only if
\[
 C\subseteq A*B,\quad
 A\subseteq C*\bar B,\quad
 B\subseteq\bar A*C.
\]
This is a theorem in the STRONG diversity-only
SAP calculus, not a claim about AP-only RAW
identity-inclusive words.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed same-sort pure-power saturation without CCO
declarations.heading: Terminal strong orbital powers without CCO
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed same-sort pure-power saturation without CCO]
\label{lem:typed-terminal-pure-power}
Let $a$ be one named transitive sort of an actual
homogeneous finite complete typed symmetric source
with visible SAP. Assume the FULL original invariant
equivalence lattice on $a$ has no relative-index-two
interval; semantic CCO is NOT assumed. For every old
same-sort diversity atom $t$, let $F_t$ be the diversity
palette of connectivity in its undirected orbital graph.
Then there is $N_t$ such that
\[
                \{t\}^{\starprod n}=F_t
                      \qquad (n\ge N_t).
\tag{TPP}\label{eq:typed-terminal-pure-power}
\]
The left side is the STRONG diversity word profile and
the right side omits literal equality.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Joint pruning maps
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Joint pruning maps]
\label{def:joint-pruning}
A \emph{joint hereditary pruning} $R$ assigns to every exact
$D\in\mathcal H_{ij}$ a nonempty (possibly nonexact) subset
$R_{ij}(D)\subseteq D$.  It is \emph{converse-compatible} if
$R_{ji}(\bar D)=\overline{R_{ij}(D)}$; it \emph{preserves PC} if
all three inclusions in \eqref{eq:typed-PC} hold for its three
outputs whenever they hold for the input; and it has \emph{survivor
heredity} if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:typed-survivor}
 E\subseteq D,\quad E\cap R(D)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad R(E)=E\cap R(D)
\end{equation}
whenever $D,E\in\mathcal H_{ij}$.  An \emph{exact contraction} is
such a map with each output in $\mathcal H_{ij}$.  A \emph{joint
hereditary selector} (HS) is a singleton-valued joint hereditary
pruning; write $R(D)=\{h_{ij}(D)\}$.

The implication \eqref{eq:typed-survivor} is an additional axiom:
conservativity, converse and triangle legality alone do not imply
it.  In the proof below every intermediate map is an exact
contraction and hence its output belongs to the \emph{original}
$\mathcal H$, while the final selector chooses atomic elements.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: All three PC coordinates survive one gate
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[All three PC coordinates survive one gate]
\label{lem:typed-all-PC}
Let $\mathcal J,\mathfrak F$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Definition~\ref{def:typed-filter} and
\eqref{eq:relative-visibility}.  Then the gate $\mathcal G$
of \eqref{eq:typed-gate} has nonempty exact outputs, commutes with
converse, satisfies survivor heredity and preserves
\emph{all three} support inclusions in every typed PC triple.
The statement includes $i=j$, $j=k$, $i=k$ and coinciding source
menus; no injectivity assumption on the variables denoting menus
is made.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Image, composition and strict contraction
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Image, composition and strict contraction]
\label{lem:typed-gate-image}
Under the preceding hypotheses, $\mathcal G$ fixes its image
pointwise; that image is a converse-closed downward subfamily of the
\emph{original} $\mathcal H$ and contains all atomic singletons.
Successive gates compose to exact conservative converse-compatible
PC-preserving maps with survivor heredity.  If some
$A\in\mathfrak F_{ij}$ has
$\varnothing\ne A\cap D\subsetneq D$ for a current menu
$D\in\mathcal J_{ij}$, then $\mathcal G(D)\subsetneq D$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Self-converse loop stabilization from (NR2)
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Self-converse loop stabilization from (NR2)]
\label{lem:typed-loop-stable}
For every nonempty loop exact menu $P\in\mathcal H_{ii}$,
there exists $N$ such that $P^{*n}=P^{*(n+1)}$ for all $n\ge N$.
This is not a claim that the stable menu is the entire palette
$L_{ii}$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Parallel-menu separation
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Parallel-menu separation]
\label{lem:typed-no-return}
For any exact seed $C\in\mathcal H_{ab}$ let
$\mathfrak F(C)$ be the smallest \emph{tagged} family of original
exact menus containing $C$, closed under converse and all
compatible left/right multiplication by \emph{original} exact
menus.  If $A,B\in\mathcal H_{ij}$ are parallel menus and
$\mathfrak F(A)=\mathfrak F(B)$, then $A=B$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Gate iteration from pure-tag no-return
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Gate iteration from pure-tag no-return]
\label{lem:typed-pure-action-gate-engine}
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite group permuting the named sorts of the
original strong exact typed system $\mathcal H$.  Assume this is a
\emph{pure tag action}: it fixes literal original fine-colour names
and transports all legal atomic triangles, converse, exact menus
and typed strong multiplication to the relabelled sort signatures.
For an original exact seed $C$, let $\mathfrak F_\Lambda(C)$
be the smallest family of \emph{original tagged exact menus}
containing $C$ and closed under converse, compatible left and
right multiplication by arbitrary original exact menus, and the
$\Lambda$ action.  Suppose that for every seed $C$ and every
parallel $A,B\in\mathfrak F_\Lambda(C)$,
\[
 \mathfrak F_\Lambda(A)=\mathfrak F_\Lambda(B)
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A=B
\]
as literal subsets of their original fine-colour palette.
Then the whole original $\mathcal H$ admits one joint
singleton-valued hereditary selector preserving converse and
all three PC inclusions, and satisfying
\[
 h_{\lambda i,\lambda j}(D)=h_{ij}(D)
 \quad(\lambda\in\Lambda,\ D\in\mathcal H_{ij}),
\]
where the same literal menu $D$ is regarded in the relabelled
palette by the pure action.  The conclusion does not assert
covariance under an action which permutes actual fine-colour names.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Existence of a joint hereditary selector
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Existence of a joint hereditary selector]
\label{thm:typed-HS}
Let $\mathcal K$ be any finite-sorted symmetric complete atomic
binary triangle Fra\"iss\'e class with SAP, semantic homomorphic
CCO, and (NR2) on every named sort.  Its full strong exact family
$\mathcal H=(\mathcal H_{ij})$ admits a joint hereditary selector
$h$: it chooses $h_{ij}(D)\in D$, commutes with converse, preserves
all typed PC triples, and satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:HS-heredity}
 E\subseteq D,\ h_{ij}(D)\in E\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 h_{ij}(E)=h_{ij}(D).
\end{equation}
No common identification of the palettes $L_{ij}$ is required.
In particular this theorem applies to the actual joint primitive
transversal from Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-transversal}.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters

declarations.title: Scope of the selector theorem
declarations.heading: Joint hereditary selectors by finite descending filters
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope of the selector theorem]
\label{rem:typed-selector-scope}
The theorem establishes \emph{one joint selector} for the fixed
\emph{named} typed source and supports all three PC coordinates,
including parallel or repeated menus and sort labels.  It does
\emph{not} imply that the selector is covariant under an arbitrary
permutation of owner names, even if such a permutation preserves all
atomic triangle tables.  The additional pure-owner action and its
covariant selector descent are treated separately in the next
construction chapter; they cannot be obtained by naively averaging
selectors over a group.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: One-edge recolouring from strong $S$-amalgamation
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[One-edge recolouring from strong $S$-amalgamation]
\label{lem:one-edge-safe-recolour}
Let $C$ be any finite \emph{complete} typed structure in a
hereditary class with strong $S$-amalgamation of all finite
typed spans.  For any two distinct vertices $x,y\in C$,
there exists a complete typed structure $C'$ on the
\emph{same vertex set and with the same owner labels},
which agrees with $C$ on every pair other than $xy$
and has $\col_{C'}(x,y)\in S_{\operatorname{own}(x),\operatorname{own}(y)}$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Safe traces and arbitrary-multiplier product identity
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Safe traces and arbitrary-multiplier product identity]
\label{lem:safe-trace-product}
Let $U$ be the primitive, typed, SAP and CCO transversal,
with a nonempty pure-$\Gamma$-covariant palette
$S_{st}\subseteq L_{st}$ which \emph{strongly}
$S$-amalgamates every finite typed span.
For every nonempty original strong exact menu $D\in\mathcal H_{st}$,
the trace $D\cap S_{st}$ is nonempty unless $D$ is
an atomic singleton outside $S_{st}$.  Whenever
$D\cap S_{st}\ne\varnothing$, for every nonempty
\emph{arbitrary atomic subset} $E\subseteq L_{tu}$, not
necessarily original exact, one has
\[
          (D\cap S_{st})*E=D*E,
\]
and likewise on the left with matching types.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface

declarations.title: Explicit skeleton calculus for augmented safe traces
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Explicit skeleton calculus for augmented safe traces]
\label{lem:augmented-safe-skeleton-calculus}
Work in the finite original
typed strong exact family
$\mathcal H$ of
\cref{lem:safe-trace-product}.
For each actual typed
hom-palette $L_{st}$,
put $S^0_{st}=L_{st}$
(the genuine FULL
DIVERSITY palette)
and $S^1_{st}=S_{st}$.
Write any nonempty
augmented typed menu
$X\subseteq L_{st}$ in
the form
\[
        X=D_X\cap S^\epsilon_{st},
 \qquad
 \epsilon\in\{0,1\},
\]
where $D_X$ belongs to the
ORIGINAL exact family and
the displayed menu is
nonempty; for $\epsilon=0$,
this means literally $X=D_X$.
This representation need
not be unique. For any
compatible augmented
$X,Y$ with chosen original
skeletons $D_X,D_Y$,
\[
                       X*Y=D_X*D_Y
                  \in\mathcal H.
\tag{AS1}\label{eq:augmented-skeleton-product}
\]
For any NONEMPTY finite
intersection of parallel
augmented menus,
\[
  \bigcap_{i=1}^m X_i
   =\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^m D_{X_i}\right)
             \cap S^{\max_i\epsilon_i},
\tag{AS2}\label{eq:augmented-skeleton-meet}
\]
which is again one of
the displayed nonempty
augmented menus. In
particular for all
compatible augmented
$X,Y,Z$ with
$Y\cap Z\ne\varnothing$,
both right- and left-
multiplication preserve
this nonempty meet:
\[
       X*(Y\cap Z)
          =(X*Y)\cap(X*Z).
\tag{AS3}\label{eq:augmented-skeleton-distrib}
\]
No identity or FALSE
distributivity over EMPTY
exact intersections is
being introduced by
$S^0$; it is only a
NOTATIONAL absent-trace
flag. Converse transports
these formulas to reversed
sorts because $S$ is
converse-compatible.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface

declarations.title: Augmented safe-domain algebra
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Augmented safe-domain algebra]
\label{lem:augmented-safe-algebra}
Under the preceding hypotheses, the nonempty augmented
families
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal H}_{st}=\mathcal H_{st}\cup
 \{D\cap S_{st}:D\in\mathcal H_{st},\ D\cap S_{st}\ne\varnothing\}
\]
are finite, closed under nonempty meets, strong products and
converse, satisfy nonempty Helly and meet-product
distributivity, and are pure-$\Gamma$-covariant.
They admit a joint hereditary singleton selector which,
when precomposed with the safe trace whenever that trace
is nonempty, chooses from $S_{st}$ for every such menu.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Finite orbit bound for the augmented pure-owner gate iteration
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Finite orbit bound for the augmented pure-owner gate iteration]
\label{cor:augmented-gamma-orbit-gate-bound}
Under the hypotheses of
\cref{lem:augmented-safe-algebra},
put
\[
 \mathscr M_{\ge2}
  =\{(s,t,D):D\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{st},
                         \ |D|\ge2\},
 \qquad
 N_\Gamma=|\Gamma\backslash\mathscr M_{\ge2}|.
\]
After the conservative pre-gate $T$,
at most $N_\Gamma$ PROPER
$\Gamma$-closed descending filter
gates are needed to obtain one joint
pure-$\Gamma$-covariant
hereditary singleton selector.
In particular
\[
 N_\Gamma\le
 \sum_{s,t}\bigl(
       |\widehat{\mathcal H}_{st}|
                   -|L_{st}|\bigr)
 \le\sum_{s,t}
              (2|\mathcal H_{st}|-|L_{st}|).
\]
No free action on the owner sorts
or on the tagged menus is required.
In fact an owner-tag stabiliser acts
trivially on each literal original
symmetric fine atom name.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Why pure owner covariance cannot be replaced by atom permutations
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Why pure owner covariance cannot be replaced by atom permutations]
\label{rem:augmented-safe-pure-gamma-essential}
The $\Gamma$-action used in
\cref{lem:augmented-safe-algebra}
permutes only the ACTUAL
owner SORT TAGS and fixes
every literal original
fine atomic colour name.
This is essential for the
no-positive-return gate
argument and cannot be
weakened to an arbitrary
$\Gamma$-permutation of
fine atomic colour names.

Indeed consider only the
ABSTRACT finite selection
problem on one
two-element atom set
$L=\{a,b\}$, with
$\Gamma=C_2$ interchanging
a and b and with the
$\Gamma$-invariant
menu $D=L$.
A conservative
$\Gamma$-covariant
singleton selector
would satisfy
\[
                  \gamma(h(D))
                    =h(\gamma D)=h(D)
\]
for the nontrivial
$\gamma$. No atom of D
is fixed by $\gamma$,
so such a selector is
IMPOSSIBLE. This is
an obstruction to the
proposed STRONGER
abstract selector scope,
not an assertion that
these toy data form
an actual homogeneous
CCO structure.

In the actual
full-owner transversal,
the simultaneous owner
permutation is realised
by an ambient original
automorphism and fixes
the literal old fine
atom names. The
unilateral thin-$G$
switch instead moves
both endpoint tags and
colour names and is
handled by the SEPARATE
moving-reading
\cref{prop:moving-readings}.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Safe completion from an injective certificate
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Safe completion from an injective certificate]
\label{lem:safe-global-completion}
In the primitive owner-typed SAP source with strong $S$-amalgamation,
let $P$ be a finite partial diagram with an injective completion
and at most one recorded literal atomic colour per pair.
There exists an injective \emph{same-vertex} completion in which
every originally unrecorded pair receives a colour in its
corresponding typed $S$ palette.
Moreover, if $P$ admits a structural pure-$\Gamma$ action,
the greatest nonempty strong-PC fixed family followed by the
augmented hereditary selector produces one legal complete
colouring preserving all these automorphisms and filling
all originally unrecorded pairs in $S$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: The actual nontrivial packet interface
declarations.heading: Safe traces and the selector interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The actual nontrivial packet interface]
\label{rem:safe-gauge-firewall}
For nontrivial thin $G$, the safety condition must be checked
for \emph{entire interpacket matrices}, under every unilateral
thin translation.  This orbit-safe full-matrix palette is
not automatically invariant under a new action on the
\emph{literal} raw colour names.  The selected reading
$h^u_{st}$ is obtained from the pure owner selector using the
original rectangular switching construction of
Proposition~\ref{prop:moving-readings}.  Its compatibility
with the $G$ endpoint switch is a \emph{separate}
requirement; it cannot be deduced merely by replacing the
pure $\Gamma$ action by an action permuting raw colours.
For the actual residual full-owner source, this packet-safe instance
is supplied by \cref{lem:orbit-safe-strong,lem:orbit-safe-all-row-interface}.
The first uses absolute real closure and full-owner closed SAP; the second
uses the injective full-row completion certificate from
\cref{lem:R07-W-completable}, with no equivariance requirement on that
certificate. Its rooted use is explicit in
\cref{lem:acf-relative-mi-normal}. These named provider hypotheses remain
part of the source-relative verification of the global theorem.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: No positive return through a proper menu
declarations.heading: Pure owner covariance and moving endpoint readings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[No positive return through a proper menu]
\label{lem:covariant-no-return}
A directed closed walk in this generation graph through a
proper menu cannot use a multiplication move.  If two parallel
menus generate the same $\Gamma$-closed family, then they are
equal as actual raw-colour subsets.

More quantitatively, put
$m_0=\max_t|P_{tt}|\ge1$.
If a closed-word transformation $T$ has a genuine
nonempty positive outside multiplier, then
$T^{4|\Gamma|m_0}(D)=P_{st}$ for EVERY nonempty
parallel atomic menu $D\subseteq P_{st}$.
Here all compositions are STRONG and the exponent
counts iterations of $T$, not edges in an HKN reservoir.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Pure-tag covariance still needs symmetric RAW fine names
declarations.heading: Pure owner covariance and moving endpoint readings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Pure-tag covariance still needs symmetric RAW fine names]
\label{rem:covariant-converse-symmetry-firewall}
The final PARALLEL-menu step of
\cref{lem:covariant-no-return}
uses a stronger fact than
the condition that $\Gamma$
fixes fine-colour symbols:
in the ACTUAL owner transversal
all old fine atoms come from one
SYMMETRIC original binary structure.
Consequently taking typed converse
reverses the endpoint OWNER TAGS
but fixes the LITERAL underlying
old fine-colour name. Pure
$\Gamma$-relabelling likewise
fixes that name. A closed
sequence consisting solely of
these operations cannot change
a menu of parallel literal
fine-colour names.

This is FALSE in an arbitrary
ASYMMETRIC typed language,
even with SAP and CCO.
For a concrete negative
scope check, take two infinite
named sorts $U,V$, one
unconstrained symmetric
same-sort diversity atom
and two cross-sort DIRECTED
diversity atoms $a,b$ whose
typed converse interchanges
$a$ and $b$. Permit EVERY
consistent complete coloured
diagram (all typed atomic
triangles are legal).
The resulting random two-sort
age has free SAP and semantic
homomorphic CCO. Let
$\Gamma=C_2$ exchange $U,V$
while keeping the literal
directed atom names $a,b$.
On the cross-sort full menu
$D=\{a,b\}$, pure covariance
would give
\[
       h_{VU}(D)=h_{UV}(D),
\]
whereas converse compatibility
would give
\[
       h_{VU}(D)=\overline{h_{UV}(D)}.
\]
Neither $a$ nor $b$ is
self-converse, so no such
covariant singleton selector
exists. Equivalently the
parallel singleton menus
$\{a\}_{UV}$ and $\{b\}_{UV}$
generate the same
$\Gamma$-and-converse-closed
family WITHOUT any positive
multiplication; parallel-menu
separation is genuinely false.

Our ACTUAL symmetric-original
scope excludes this example.
One must NOT export the
present $\Gamma$-selector
argument to directed or
asymmetric original atoms
without an additional
converse-invariance criterion.
\end{remark}

essential later for three distinct valuations to decode a legal

declarations.title: Rooted automorphism-transport ACF
declarations.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Rooted automorphism-transport ACF]
\label{def:rooted-acf}
For nonempty finite \(A_0\subseteq M\), a finite induced
\(W\subseteq M\) has \emph{rooted \(S\)-ACF over \(A_0\)} if it
contains \(\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0)\) and for every nonempty
\(Z\subseteq W\) such that
\(\col_W(x,y)\notin S\) whenever \(x,y\in Z\) are distinct,
and every selected \(z\in Z\), there exists
\(\alpha\in\Aut(W)\) satisfying
\[
 \alpha(Z)\subseteq\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0),
 \qquad \alpha(z)\in A_0.
\]
We also call such a \(Z\) an \emph{unsafe clique}.  The definition
requires one common \(W\) for all unsafe cliques, selected roots
and partial automorphisms of \(A_0\); it does not assert coherent
extensions.  In the AP-not-SAP situation the closure target is
essential: \(\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0)\) cannot be replaced in
general by \(A_0\).
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Finite exact intersections vanish
declarations.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite exact intersections vanish]
\label{lem:acf-finite-exact-intersection}
If \(E\) is an exact invariant equivalence and \(a\) an actual
nonempty symmetric atomic orbital, then
\[
 E\cap a^2\subseteq F\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 E\cap a^2=\Id.
\]
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates

declarations.title: Concentration of unsafe pairs
declarations.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Concentration of unsafe pairs]
\label{lem:acf-unsafe-concentration}
Suppose \(S\) has strong closed amalgamation.  For any two
distinct minimal infinite cuts \(E_i,E_j\),
\[
   \mathcal D(M)\setminus S\ \subseteq\ R_i\cup R_j
   \quad\text{as unions of complete original orbitals}.
\]
Every finite unsafe clique is contained in one \(R_i\)-class
or in one \(R_j\)-class.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates

declarations.title: Canonical exact MI coordinates
declarations.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Canonical exact MI coordinates]
\label{lem:acf-canonical-coordinates}
If \(r\ge2\), all \(C_i\) are infinite nonidentity exact
equivalences, and
\[
        \bigcap_iR_i=F,\qquad
        \bigcap_iC_i=\Id.
        \tag{\(\ddagger\)}\label{eq:acf-core-meets}
\]
For each \(i\), the actual exact quotient \(Q_i=M/C_i\)
has a meet-irreducible largest finite-class equivalence
\(F_i=R_i/C_i\), so
\[
     \operatorname{acl}_{Q_i}(U)=F_i[U]
               \quad\text{for every finite }U\subseteq Q_i.
               \tag{\(\heartsuit\)}\label{eq:acf-MI-closure}
\]
If \(S\) has strong closed amalgamation, every unsafe clique
\(Z\) satisfies, for some index \(i_0\),
\[
   \pi_j(Z)\subseteq F_j[\pi_j(z)]
              \quad(j\ne i_0,\ z\in Z).
        \tag{\(\clubsuit\)}\label{eq:acf-one-free}
\]
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates

declarations.title: Avoiding arbitrary quotient safety
declarations.heading: Real algebraic closure and canonical safe coordinates
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Avoiding arbitrary quotient safety]
The full-support safe-palette descent for the canonical
normalised factors will be proved after selecting maximal
exact cores in Lemma~\ref{lem:acf-quotient-safety} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:acf-hat-factors}.  It relies on a
\emph{harmless complementary exact split}.  The corresponding
statement for an arbitrary infinite exact quotient is false.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Exact pseudocomplement
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact pseudocomplement]
\label{lem:acf-hat-pseudocomplement}
For invariant exact $H$ one has
\[
         H\subseteq R_i
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H\cap E_i=\Id.
\]
The $\widehat C_i$ are the exact-lattice pseudocomplements of
the distinct atoms $E_i$.  They contain $E_j$ for $j\ne i$,
are disjoint from $E_i$, and satisfy $\bigcap_i\widehat C_i=\Id$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: No new finite exact kernels
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[No new finite exact kernels]
\label{lem:acf-hat-normalised}
For each nonempty $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put
$K_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}\widehat C_i$.
Every actual quotient $M/K_I$ has no nonidentity finite-class
exact equivalence.  Its minimal infinite directions are exactly
$(E_i\vee K_I)/K_I$, $i\in I$.
In particular for $r\ge2$ each
$Q_i=M/\widehat C_i$ is a strict, normalised source with
one minimal infinite direction, finite bottom
$F_i=R_i/\widehat C_i$, and
\[
       \operatorname{acl}_{Q_i}(A)=F_i[A].
\]
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Projection of algebraicity through an exact quotient
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Projection of algebraicity through an exact quotient]
\label{lem:acf-acl-projects-exact}
Let \(Q\) be any standing countable
homogeneous transitive finite complete
symmetric binary AP+homomorphic-CCO
source, let \(E\) be one of its ACTUAL
invariant FULL EXACT equivalences,
and write \(\pi:Q\to T=Q/E\).
For every finite real \(A\subseteq Q\),
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \pi\bigl(\operatorname{acl}_Q(A)\bigr)
       \subseteq
       \operatorname{acl}_{T}(\pi A).
 \qquad}
\tag{APJ}\label{eq:acf-acl-projects-exact}
\]
The reverse inclusion after taking
full preimages is NOT claimed when
\(E\) has infinite classes.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Finite intersection of absolutely closed exact quotient preimages
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite intersection of absolutely closed exact quotient preimages]
\label{lem:acf-finite-exact-closed-preimages}
Let $M$ be a standing homogeneous
finite-complete symmetric binary
source satisfying original semantic
homomorphic CCO. Let
$E_1,\ldots,E_m$ be ACTUAL
invariant FULL EXACT
equivalences on $M$ whose
common meet
$K=\bigcap_{i=1}^m E_i$
has FINITE original real
classes. For each i let
$D_i\subseteq M/E_i$ be
a finite induced ABSOLUTELY
real-algebraically-closed
set. Then any NONEMPTY
intersection of FULL
original inverse images
\[
          W=\bigcap_{i=1}^m
                  \pi_{E_i}^{-1}(D_i)
\tag{FPCL}\label{eq:acf-finite-exact-closed-preimages}
\]
is FINITE and
$\operatorname{acl}_M(W)=W$.

No pairwise-compatible owner
tuple assumption, surjectivity
$\pi_{E_i}(W)=D_i$, or
algebraic closure of a
common owner quotient is
needed for this assertion.
The finite-class hypothesis
on the common kernel is
essential for FINITENESS.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Absolute acl closure of a full exact rectangle
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Absolute acl closure of a full exact rectangle]
\label{lem:acf-rectangle-acl}
Let \(C,K\) be original full exact invariant
equivalences of one homogeneous transitive
symmetric binary source, with \(C\cap K=\Id\),
and set \(J=C\vee K\), \(Y=M/C\),
\(X=M/K\), \(T=M/J\). Let \(B\subseteq T\)
be any finite, induced, NONEMPTY owner set;
it need NOT be absolutely
$\operatorname{acl}_T$-closed for THIS
rectangle-closure assertion.
Suppose \(D\subseteq Y\) and \(P\subseteq X\)
are finite, induced, ABSOLUTELY real-acl-closed
in their respective ambient quotient sources,
and each projects ONTO precisely \(B\).
Then their FULL rectangle
\[
       R=D\times_B P
       =\{(d,p):d\in D,\ p\in P,\
                     \pi_T(d)=\pi_T(p)\}
\]
is a finite induced, absolutely
real-acl-closed subset of the ACTUAL
original \(M\), via the exact CRT
bijection \(M\cong Y\times_T X\).
No harmlessness assumption on B
in EITHER quotient factor is needed
for this particular closure assertion.
The stronger closure assumption
$\operatorname{acl}_T(B)=B$
appearing later in the
safe-quotient DESCENT proof
is used THERE to control the
projections of auxiliary
helper closures; it is not
part of the present lemma.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Complete complementary owner-pair spectrum
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Complete complementary owner-pair spectrum]
\label{lem:acf-complementary-spectrum}
Keep the complementary exact quotients
\(Y=M/C\), \(X=M/K\), \(T=M/(C\vee K)\)
with \(C\cap K=\Id\). Let
\(B\subseteq T\) be a finite induced
set of ACTUAL owner classes, and let
\(P\subseteq X\) be a finite induced
structure projecting ONTO \(B\).
Assume \(P\) contains, for EVERY
ordered owner pair \((t,t')\in B^2\)
and every ACTUAL \(X\)-atomic orbital
\(b\) realized between some two
\(X\)-points above exactly \(t,t'\),
a pair \(p,p'\in P\) with owners
\(t,t'\) and orbital \(b\).
The diagonal \(b=\Id_X\) is included
when the two owner labels agree.

Let \(y,y'\in Y\) be ACTUAL DISTINCT
quotient points, with owners
\(t,t'\in B\), and let
\(q=\col_Y(y,y')\). Then as \(p,p'\)
range over all \(P\)-points with
owners \(t,t'\), the pairwise old
fine colours of the CRT points
\[
               (y,p),\ (y',p')
                   \quad\in M
\]
include EVERY original fine atomic
colour \(a\) lying over the quotient
orbital \(q\) (that is,
\(a\subseteq C;q;C\), using the
actual saturated old pullback).
In particular no individual
\(C\)-representative or \(K\)-representative
choice is assumed to realize all fine
colours at once.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: An opposite-coordinate diagonal is a genuine fine lift
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[An opposite-coordinate diagonal is a genuine fine lift]
\label{rem:acf-opposite-diagonal-fine-lift}
In \cref{lem:acf-complementary-spectrum}
the two \(Y\)-coordinates \(y\ne y'\)
need NOT have distinct
\(X\)-coordinates \(p,p'\).
Equality \(p=p'\) is one of the
ACTUAL RAW \(X\)-pair orbitals
that must occur in the single
complementary helper spectrum.

For example take the original
Cartesian-phase source
\(M_*=\mathbb N^2\times\mathbb F_2\)
of \cref{ex:two-coordinate}.
Its EXACT row-and-phase and
column-and-phase kernels
\(C,K\) have
\(C\cap K=\Id\), while its
finite two-point phase packet
bottom \(F\) is NONEXACT.
Fix different rows \(r\ne r'\),
one column \(c\) and one phase
\(g\). The distinct old real
points \((r,c,g)\),
\((r',c,g)\) have DIFFERENT
\(Y=M_*/C\)-coordinates
but the SAME \(X=M_*/K\)
coordinate. Their old fine
diversity atom is thus
witnessed over the ACTUAL
\(X\)-DIAGONAL pair \(p=p'\).
Discarding diagonal \(X\)
orbital witnesses because
the original real endpoints
are distinct would omit
a genuine fine lift and
invalidate full-support
\(S_Y\)-safety. No exactness
of the unrelated finite
bottom \(F\) is used.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: A non-Boolean actual exact owner split with diagonal lifts
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A non-Boolean actual exact owner split with diagonal lifts]
\label{ex:acf-nonboolean-phase-safety}
In the ACTUAL Cartesian-phase
homogeneous AP+semantic-CCO
source $M_*=\mathbb N^2\times\mathbb F_2$
of \cref{ex:two-coordinate},
the named fine atomic colour
of two distinct points
$(r,c,g),(r',c',g')$
records exactly
$\mathbf 1_{r=r'}$,
$\mathbf 1_{c=c'}$
and $g+g'$.
Let $C$ be SAME ROW AND
SAME PHASE, and $K$ SAME
COLUMN AND SAME PHASE.
Then $C,K$ are FULL RAW exact,
$C\cap K=\Id$ and
$J=C\vee K$ is SAME PHASE,
strictly below $\Top$.
Indeed the old atomic row-edge
with zero phase difference
has represented square
exactly $C$, and similarly
the column-edge square is
$K$; their RAW product is J.

The ORIGINAL FULL RAW exact
invariant-equivalence lattice
is the genuinely NONBOOLEAN
five-element distributive
lattice
\[
          \Id<C,K<J<\Top,
 \qquad C\not\le K,\quad
        K\not\le C.
\]
Every nonempty old atomic
word forces ONE endpoint
phase difference, so every
PROPER full RAW exact
equivalence, which must
contain real equality,
preserves phase.
Within each phase layer,
the invariance and
transitivity of an
equivalence on the
Cartesian grid give
ONLY equality, same row,
same column, or the
whole phase layer:
if an equivalence relates
a pair differing in BOTH
coordinates, its
two-edge compositions
generate row and column
pairs; if it contains
both row and column
differences, their
composition generates
every pair.

Here $Y=M_*/C$ has
points $(r,g)$,
$X=M_*/K$ has
points $(c,g)$, and
$T=M_*/J$ has the
TWO phase owners $g$.
Consider the ORIGINAL
diversity safe palette
$S=\{a\in\mathcal D(M_*):
                       a\not\subseteq F\}$,
where $F$ is the
two-point thin
same-$(r,c)$ packet
equivalence. This is
a SET OF OLD DIVERSITY
ATOM NAMES, not a
set-theoretic difference
between a palette and a
binary relation. Thus
S consists precisely
of old fine diversity
atoms for which
$r\ne r'$ OR $c\ne c'$.
It has strong closed
amalgamation. In fact
every finite nonempty
absolutely acl-closed
real set is a COMPLETE
rectangle $R_0\times
C_0\times\mathbb F_2$:
the original
\(\Aut(M_*)=
 \operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)
 \times\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)
 \times\mathbb F_2\)
stabiliser fixes the
finitely named rows and
columns, and every
corner of the resulting
rectangle has finite
orbit. To strongly
amalgamate closed spans,
rename all row coordinates
new to the two sides
disjointly, and do
likewise with all new
column coordinates;
all new cross pairs
then have at least
one different coordinate,
so their literal old
fine colour lies in S.
For the empty base,
choose disjoint finite
row and column sets
for the two factors.

The FULL-support
projected safe palette
on $Y$ is
\[
 S_Y=\{\,q\in\mathcal D(Y):
       \text{the two }Y\text{-points
       have DIFFERENT rows}\,\}.
\]
For different rows,
EVERY old fine lift
belongs to S; for equal
rows the two distinct
$Y$-points have opposite
phases and the lift with
the SAME column is the
unsafe thin phase flip.
This $S_Y$ strongly
amalgamates finite
absolutely closed
$Y$-rectangles
$R_0\times\mathbb F_2$,
by making all newly
introduced row values
disjoint.

The common owner set
$B=T=\mathbb F_2$
is nonempty and
absolutely acl-closed.
Take finite sets of
rows $R_0$ and columns
$C_0$, and the FULL
acl-closed complementary
helper
$P=C_0\times\mathbb F_2$
in X. The full rectangle
$D\times_B P$ for
$D=R_0\times\mathbb F_2$
is exactly
$R_0\times C_0\times
\mathbb F_2$, independently
acl-closed by
\cref{lem:acf-finite-exact-closed-preimages}.

Finally take $r\ne r'$
with one common
phase $g$ and fix a
column c. The DISTINCT
old points
$(r,c,g),(r',c,g)$
have different $Y$-classes
but IDENTICAL $X$-classes
$p=p'=(c,g)$. Their
old atom $(0,1,0)$
can be witnessed among
the helper lifts ONLY
using this ACTUAL
X-diagonal orbital.
Discarding diagonal
X witnesses would
therefore destroy the
full fine-lift spectrum
\cref{lem:acf-complementary-spectrum},
even though original
real endpoints are
distinct. This is a
NONBOOLEAN exact-lattice
test, not an assumption
that the two quotient
coordinates are independent
or that original
$M_*$ has SAP.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Finite avoidance while fixing harmless quotient owners
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite avoidance while fixing harmless quotient owners]
\label{lem:acf-harmless-owner-avoidance}
Let $Y$ be a homogeneous
finite-complete ORIGINAL
exact quotient source, let
$T$ be one ACTUAL further
invariant exact quotient,
and let $B\subseteq T$
be a finite set of ACTUAL
quotient classes whose
simultaneous naming does
NOT enlarge real algebraic
closure in Y.
Let $A\subseteq Y$
be finite and ABSOLUTELY
acl-closed, and let
$L\supseteq A$ be a finite
induced extension in Y.
For every finite
$Z\subseteq Y\setminus A$,
there is ONE
\[
             g\in\Aut(Y/A,B)
\]
such that
\[
                    g(L\setminus A)
                                  \cap Z=\varnothing.
\tag{OAV}\label{eq:acf-harmless-owner-avoidance}
\]
In particular, if every
vertex of L projects into B,
its ENTIRE owner assignment
is retained pointwise
under g. Two extensions
$A\subseteq L,R$ may be
placed sequentially over
A with exactly their
original owner names,
with their off-base parts
pairwise disjoint and
disjoint from any
specified finite helper
outside A. No input
closure of L or R is
needed for this finite
avoidance lemma, although
the safe quotient descent
will subsequently close
the helper factors.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Full-support safety under a harmless exact split
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full-support safety under a harmless exact split]
\label{lem:acf-quotient-safety}
Suppose exact $C,K$ satisfy $C\cap K=\Id$ and put
$J=C\vee K$, $Y=M/C$, $X=M/K$, $T=M/J$.
Suppose naming finite actual $T$-owner sets does not enlarge
\emph{real algebraic closure in $Y$}.  If the original palette
$S$ strongly amalgamates finite real-acl-closed spans, then
\[
 S_Y=\{q\in\mathcal D(Y):
       \text{every original fine lift of }q\text{ lies in }S\}
\]
strongly amalgamates finite real-acl-closed spans in $Y$,
with every distinct projected unsafe original pair remaining unsafe.
\emph{No harmlessness assumption in the opposite factor $X$ is
required for this conclusion.} Symmetrically, harmlessness only in
$X$ suffices for $S_X$. In particular if both owner cuts are
harmless, both full-support palettes are strongly safe.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Intrinsic minimum-ancestor description of the joint owner cut
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Intrinsic minimum-ancestor description of the joint owner cut]
\label{lem:acf-joint-owner-minimum-ancestors}
Let $\mathcal L$ be a FINITE
distributive lattice, presented as
$\operatorname{Down}(P)$ by
Birkhoff's theorem. Suppose
$P$ has $r\ge2$ distinct
minimal points $p_1,\dots,p_r$.
For $q\in P$ write
\[
    \operatorname{Anc}(q)=
         \{\,i\in[r]:p_i\le q\,\}.
\]
This set is NONEMPTY for every
$q\in P$. Let the maximal
pseudocomplements of its exact
atoms be
\[
 C_i=P\setminus\uparrow p_i
       =\{q:i\notin\operatorname{Anc}(q)\}.
\]
Put $J_{ij}=C_i\vee C_j$,
$H_i=\bigwedge_{j\ne i}J_{ij}$
and $H_*=\bigwedge_{i<j}J_{ij}$.
Under the literal downset
representation these have
the EXACT descriptions
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_{ij}
    &=\{q:\{i,j\}\not\subseteq
                     \operatorname{Anc}(q)\},\\
 H_i
    &=\{q:i\notin\operatorname{Anc}(q)
                 \text{ OR }
                 \operatorname{Anc}(q)=\{i\}\},\\
 H_*
    &=\{q:|\operatorname{Anc}(q)|=1\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{MO}\label{eq:acf-joint-owner-minimum-ancestors}
\]
Consequently
\[
 H_*>0,\qquad
 \bigwedge_iH_i=H_*,
 \qquad H_i\vee H_j=J_{ij}
                     \quad(i\ne j).
\tag{MOR}\label{eq:acf-joint-owner-relations}
\]
The first inequality is STRICT
and uses no original
amalgamation: every atomic
minimal point $p_i$ belongs
to $H_*$. In the standing
finite-exact-normalised AP+CCO
source, take $C_i=\widehat C_i$,
so the joint owner quotient
$M/H_*$ is therefore an ACTUAL
STRICT exact quotient (lower
diversity rank) and the
pairwise joins are precisely
the common owner quotients
used by finite exact CRT.
This proof is pure finite
distributive-lattice algebra;
it does not assume independent
coordinate factors or Boolean
original orbit structure.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Maximal cores give admissible simultaneous factors
declarations.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Maximal cores give admissible simultaneous factors]
\label{cor:acf-hat-factors}
Assume $r\ge2$ and use $\widehat C_i$ as above.  Put
\[
 J_{ij}=\widehat C_i\vee\widehat C_j,\qquad
 H_i=\bigcap_{j\ne i}J_{ij},\qquad
 H_*=\bigcap_{i<j}J_{ij},\qquad
 \Omega=M/H_*.
\]
Then $H_*>\Id$, $H_i\vee H_j=J_{ij}$ and
$\bigcap_iH_i=H_*$, with their exact
minimum-ancestor normal form supplied
by \cref{lem:acf-joint-owner-minimum-ancestors}.
The actual owner source $\Omega$
is therefore a strict exact quotient.
Every $Q_i=M/\widehat C_i$ has a global full-support
strong closed safe palette as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:acf-quotient-safety}; and every original
unsafe clique has at most one projection not contained
in a single finite $F_i$ packet.  Also
\[
 \operatorname{acl}_M(A)=
 \bigcap_i\pi_{\widehat C_i}^{-1}
          \bigl(F_i[\pi_{\widehat C_i}(A)]\bigr)
 =\bigcap_iR_i[A].
\]
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Maximal exact pseudocomplements and normalised MI factors

declarations.title: Full unary-term code reconstructs generated embeddings
declarations.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full unary-term code reconstructs generated embeddings]
\label{lem:foundational-full-code-embeddings}
In the full-code setting above, the code of $A^o$ reconstructs $h(A^o)$
up to unique isomorphism over the root coordinates. For every
$D^o\in\mathcal H^o$ there is a natural bijection
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Emb_{\mathcal V^o}(A^o,N(D^o))
  \cong
 \Emb_{\mathcal H^o}(h(A^o),D^o).
 \quad}\tag{FCODE}\label{eq:foundational-full-code-embeddings}
\]
Neither Ramsey nor EP is assumed. Multiary hidden functions are not
covered by this binary code theorem.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings

declarations.title: Definedness and complete coding
declarations.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Definedness and complete coding]
Finite normal forms alone do not record partial-function domains: already
on one point, an undefined $F$ differs from a fixed point of $F$.
The full code distinguishes them by $E_{F,F}(x,x)$. When function domains
are determined by sorts and all intended functions are total there, these
definedness codes are redundant. More generally, any code may be omitted
only after proving that it is uniformly quantifier-free definable from
the retained relations, so that the embedding sets are unchanged. This includes
replacing non-order codes by original fine visible relations in a concrete
application; the reconstruction theorem does not supply that definability.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Finite-tuple hidden Ramsey readout
declarations.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite-tuple hidden Ramsey readout]
\label{thm:ramsey-tuple-readout}
In the full-code setting of \cref{lem:foundational-full-code-embeddings},
if $\mathcal H^o$ is Ramsey for embeddings, then so is $\mathcal V^o$.
No cofinal root cover, EP, visible SAP, or additional order on the visible
tuples is required.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings

declarations.title: Cofinality from an ambient root cover
declarations.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Cofinality from an ambient root cover]
\label{lem:foundational-root-cover-cofinal}
Let $P$ be an (arbitrary possibly infinite) hidden
structure with finitely many unary-term normal forms
from each root-coordinate sort. Let $\mathcal H$ be
the hereditary age of finite \emph{unary-closed}
induced substructures of $P$, and suppose every
finite $D\in\mathcal H$ embeds into $P$.
Assume each hidden element $z\in P$ is a unary-term
value $\tau(\eta(r))$ of \emph{some valid visible
root tuple} $\eta(r)\in N(P)$.
Then every finite $D\in\mathcal H$ embeds into a
finite $E\in\mathcal H$ with
\[
                         h(N(E))=E .
\tag{RC}\label{eq:foundational-root-cover}
\]
No Ramsey, expansion property, CCO or SAP hypothesis
is involved.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Full term codes and generated embeddings

declarations.title: Same-host lifting from the complete root code
declarations.heading: Unexpanded supports and the extra obligations for EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Same-host lifting from the complete root code]
\label{lem:foundational-same-host-code}
Let $E\in\mathcal H$ be finite and
$B=N(E)|_{\mathcal V}$ its full \emph{unexpanded}
visible root interpretation. Assume
\[
                         h(N(E))=E,
\]
and that the \emph{unexpanded} fine-coloured
visible object $B$ determines the hidden
unexpanded generated support canonically,
up to its unique isomorphism over root-coordinate
presentations. For every allowed expanded representation $B^o$, assume
also that the reduct of $h(B^o)$ is this canonical unexpanded support,
under the same root-coordinate identification. This holds automatically
for relational hidden expansions retaining the unary functions.
Suppose allowed visible expansions
are precisely the hereditary induced \emph{full
unary-term codes} of finite hidden expanded objects
of $\mathcal H^o$, with all hidden term equality,
function, unary/binary relation and comparison
information retained. Then every allowed
expansion $B^o$ of this fixed $B$ has a hidden
realisation $E^o\in\mathcal H^o$ on the
\emph{same underlying unexpanded $E$}, and its
root code on $B$ is precisely $B^o$.

Such $E^o$ is unique as a structure on $E$
once the chosen identification of $E$ with
the unexpanded root-generated template is fixed.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Unexpanded supports and the extra obligations for EP

declarations.title: Cofinal full-code EP transfer
declarations.heading: Unexpanded supports and the extra obligations for EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Cofinal full-code EP transfer]
\label{thm:foundational-cofinal-tuple-EP}
Assume $\mathcal H^o\to\mathcal H$ and
$\mathcal V^o\to\mathcal V$ are reasonable precompact expansions,
and that the hidden expansion has EP. Suppose the tuple interpretation
and its full unary-term, equality, relational and comparison code satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item for every visible $A\in\mathcal V$ the unexpanded
isomorphism type of $h(A)$ is determined by the
unexpanded visible fine-coloured $A$, and the expansion
$A^o$ induces one compatible hidden expansion of $h(A)$;
\item every finite hidden $D\in\mathcal H$ embeds into
a finite $E\in\mathcal H$ such that
\[
                         h(N(E))=E;
\]
\item \emph{every} allowed visible expansion of
$N(E)$, for such a full root-generated $E$, lifts to
a hidden $\mathcal H^o$ expansion of the \emph{same
underlying unexpanded $E$}, preserving all full
term/equality/relational/comparison codes;
\item every visible embedding extends \emph{uniquely}
to the unary-generated hidden supports, sends each
valid visible root tuple to a valid root tuple,
and the tuple interpretation recovers every original
fine visible binary atom.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal V^o$ has the expansion property
relative to its unexpanded age $\mathcal V$.
This result requires neither CCO nor SAP, and
does not assert the four hypotheses for any
particular MI/MR interpretation.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Unexpanded supports and the extra obligations for EP

declarations.title: EP for an ambient root-covered full-code interpretation
declarations.heading: Unexpanded supports and the extra obligations for EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[EP for an ambient root-covered full-code interpretation]
\label{cor:foundational-root-covered-full-code-EP}
Let $\mathcal H^o\to\mathcal H$ and
$\mathcal V^o\to\mathcal V$ be reasonable precompact expansions in
the full-code setting above. Suppose:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=*]
\item the hidden expansion $\mathcal H^o\to\mathcal H$
has EP and its finite unexpanded source is represented
by unary-closed finite substructures of one ambient
hidden $P$;
\item every hidden point of $P$ is an applicable unary
term of some valid visible root in $N(P)$, with finitely
many unary-term normal forms;
\item the complete \emph{unexpanded} visible fine code
canonically reconstructs the hidden unary-generated
support and all original visible fine atoms; moreover the reduct of
each allowed expanded generated support is that same canonical
unexpanded support over its root-coordinate presentations;
\item the allowed visible expansions are precisely
the hereditary full unary-term codes induced from
hidden $\mathcal H^o$ objects, retaining all term
equalities, unary/binary relations and hidden comparison
codes, with embeddings given by those complete codes.
\end{enumerate}
Then the visible full-code expansion $\mathcal V^o$
has the expansion property over $\mathcal V$.
No Ramsey theorem, CCO, or SAP conclusion for the
visible source is used.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Ramsey inheritance under a unary-closed sort restriction
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Ramsey inheritance under a unary-closed sort restriction]
\label{lem:foundational-ramsey-sort-restriction}
Let $\mathcal R$ be a hereditary Ramsey class
of finite structures in a finite language with
named disjoint sorts, arbitrary relations, and
unary partial functions whose domains are
determined by source sorts. Let $I$ be a fixed
collection of sort symbols such that no unary
function with source in $I$ has its target
outside $I$. Define $\mathcal R|_I$ to be
the class of structures obtained by restricting
objects of $\mathcal R$ to their vertices in
sorts $I$, retaining all induced symbols on
those sorts. Then $\mathcal R|_I$ is hereditary
and Ramsey. If $\mathcal R$ has JEP or SAP,
then so does $\mathcal R|_I$.
No extra strong-amalgamation or real-representative
choices are needed for the Ramsey inheritance.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Ramsey inheritance under a functorial normalization
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Ramsey inheritance under a functorial normalization]
\label{lem:foundational-ramsey-normalization}
Let $\mathcal R$ be a hereditary Ramsey class of finite structures,
with embeddings as morphisms. Let $N$ be an endofunctor such that
$N(A)$ has the same universe as $A$, $N(f)$ is the same vertex map
as $f$ for every embedding, and $N^2=N$. Then the full class
\[
                  \mathcal R_N=\{A\in\mathcal R:N(A)=A\}
\]
is hereditary and Ramsey for embeddings. If $\mathcal R$ has JEP,
then so does $\mathcal R_N$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Functorial normalization of synchronized quotient orders
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Functorial normalization of synchronized quotient orders]
\label{lem:foundational-hierarchical-order-normalization}
Let the hidden finite-sorted language have a finite
family of proper meet-irreducible quotient sorts
\(B_J\), indexed by a finite distributive
equivalence lattice on each actual named original
sort, together with all definable upward quotient
maps and named quotient-transition bijections.
Assume closed transition holonomy is the identity.
Fix a priority on sort symbols, a priority on
the finitely many strict coarser coordinates
above each \(J\), and one representative
\(B_J\) of every transition orbit of cuts
\(J\prec J^+\).

From ANY total order on each hidden quotient sort,
extract for each representative cut the induced
order on the \(J\)-points INSIDE each fixed
\(J^+\)-class; transport that family of fibre
orders to all transition-equivalent copies.
Order all quotient sorts recursively from coarser
to finer, by first lexicographically comparing
the already ordered tuple of ALL strict coarser
proper MI coordinates and then, on equality
of that tuple, using the extracted order inside
the common \(J^+\)-fibre. Across different
hidden sort symbols use the fixed priority.

This construction is a functorial idempotent
normalization \(N\) on finite functionally
closed ordered hidden objects: it preserves
all old hidden structures and embeddings,
and its image is precisely the synchronized
parent-lex order class. Reversing the orders
of ONE selected cut task simultaneously along
its transition orbit does not change any
coarser task, and all finer derived comparisons
can be recomputed functorially. In particular
no independent sort-order or parent-lex choice
is made after a host has been selected.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Single-task reset-midpoint EP criterion
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Single-task reset-midpoint EP criterion]
\label{thm:abstract-reset-order-EP}
Let $\mathcal R$ be a hereditary Ramsey class with JEP of finite
ordered structures (possibly with unary partial functions, whose
domains are fixed by sorts and whose closures are finite).
Let $\mathcal U_1\to\mathcal U_0$ be reducts of $\mathcal R$,
reasonable, precompact and reduct-surjective, with
$\mathcal U_0$ forgetting \emph{one} task of ordering distinct
points inside designated disjoint finite fibres. Assume:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item Every $\mathcal U_1$ object has a full $\mathcal R$
expansion. The only data in $\mathcal U_1$ not present in
$\mathcal U_0$ are the linear orders on the designated fibres
and their functorially determined codes. Reversing the orders
in \emph{all} designated fibres of a $\mathcal U_1$ object,
with the derived codes changed accordingly, gives another
legal $\mathcal U_1$ object on exactly the same
$\mathcal U_0$ reduct.
\item The designated fibre equivalence and the symmetric
old binary relation $\mathfrak m$ are named or
quantifier-free definable already in the
$\mathcal U_0$ reduct. The relation $\mathfrak m$
only joins distinct designated points \emph{in one fibre},
and its complete finite \emph{unary-generated expanded}
ordered edge type is always ONE isomorphism type
$H_{\mathfrak m}$ when the first endpoint precedes
the second. In particular, the whole edge closure,
including all named fine relations and all auxiliary
order/equality codes, is determined by the oriented edge.
\item For every $A\in\mathcal R$ and each designated-fibre
comparison $u<v$ in $A$, there is an \emph{induced}
embedding $A\hookrightarrow A^+\in\mathcal R$ and
a fresh designated point $z$ in the same fibre with
\[
       u<z<v,\qquad
       u\,\mathfrak m\,z\,\mathfrak m\,v.
\]
The extension preserves the entire earlier expanded
structure. By iteration the same can be done for
\emph{every} such comparison in any one finite input.
\end{enumerate}

Then $\mathcal U_1$ has the expansion property over
$\mathcal U_0$. The witness is an unexpanded
$\mathcal U_0$ object chosen \emph{before} any competing
task-order expansion. No Ramsey hypothesis is imposed
on the intermediate classes $\mathcal U_0$ or
$\mathcal U_1$ separately.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Fresh reset midpoints from closed SAP
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Fresh reset midpoints from closed SAP]
\label{lem:abstract-fresh-reset-midpoint}
Let $\mathcal H$ be a hereditary class of finite
unary-functionally closed structures with SAP,
and let $\mathcal H^o$ be an ordered SAP
expansion whose orders can be freely extended
inside the designated fibres compatibly
with existing closed substructures.
Suppose for each pair of distinct same-fibre
points $u,v$ of a member $A\in\mathcal H$,
some permitted finite closed extension of
the unary closure $\langle u,v\rangle$ contains
$z$ in that fibre, outside $\langle u,v\rangle$,
such that $u\,\mathfrak m\,z\,\mathfrak m\,v$.
Then property (iii) of
\cref{thm:abstract-reset-order-EP} holds in
$\mathcal H^o$, provided the two-root generated
structures of the existing pair and of the
midpoint witness have the same \emph{complete}
unexpanded named type.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Composition of relative expansion properties
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Composition of relative expansion properties]
\label{lem:foundational-relative-EP-composition}
Let $\mathcal K_2\to\mathcal K_1\to
\mathcal K_0$ be reduct maps of hereditary
finite relational/unary-functional ages, with
each expanded age reduct-surjective onto its
predecessor. If $\mathcal K_2$ has EP over
$\mathcal K_1$ and $\mathcal K_1$ has EP over
$\mathcal K_0$, then $\mathcal K_2$ has EP
over $\mathcal K_0$. The same holds for
any finite chain. No Ramsey assumption on
the intermediate classes is necessary.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Source and quantifier firewall
declarations.heading: A reset-midpoint criterion for relative ordering EP
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Source and quantifier firewall]
\label{rem:abstract-reset-EP-scope}
Condition (ii) is about the \emph{entire}
unary-generated expanded fine type, not just
the two-point equivalence reduct.
A relation $\mathfrak m$ satisfying
$\mathfrak m;\mathfrak m=J^+$ supplies
one midpoint for each pair in the same
$J^+$ fibre, but \emph{by itself} does
not supply a fresh midpoint in every
finite closed configuration: the latter
also needs the closure type and SAP in
\cref{lem:abstract-fresh-reset-midpoint}.
The ordering reversal in (i) concerns
only the \emph{one current order task};
earlier named order tasks remain fixed.
For multiple tasks, relative EP must
be composed separately along the tower
of reasonable precompact reducts.
The proof never treats an intermediate
partially ordered class as Ramsey.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Finite-base restriction
declarations.heading: Finite-base lifting over a fixed quotient
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite-base restriction]\label{lem:finite-base}
Let $X$ be homogeneous in a finite relational language, and let
$\pi:X\to T$ be an invariant quotient whose quotient pair colours
are determined by the fine pair colours. Assume $\Age(X)$ has
ordinary EPPA. Fix finite $B\subseteq T$, $A\subseteq\pi^{-1}(B)$,
and finitely many compatible requirements $(p,\gamma)$, where
$p$ is a partial automorphism of $A$, $\gamma\in\Aut(B)$ and
$\pi p=\gamma\pi$ on $\operatorname{dom}(p)$. Suppose each pair
has a simultaneous ambient lift in $\Aut(X)$.
Then a single finite $W\subseteq\pi^{-1}(B)$ containing $A$ has
$\pi W=B$ and extends all requirements: for every pair $(p,\gamma)$
there exists $\beta\in\Aut(W)$ extending $p$ and inducing $\gamma$
on the entire $B$. Empty-domain requirements are included.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: A completable structural HKN reservoir
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Exact HKN scope]
HKN Theorem~1.2 controls the $\Gamma$-structure on at most
$n$ \emph{vertices}, so the locality parameter is
$b|G|$, not just $b$.  Irreducible structure faithfulness
controls functional closure and the all-or-nothing recorded
matrices.  Neither of these alone implies completion in the
CCO source; completion additionally uses closed SAP, the
origin-transversal reduction, and finite bad-cycle locality.
The result is ordinary structural $\Gamma$-EPPA at this stage;
coherence is not used and no second valued HKN application is
assumed.
\end{remark}

declarations.heading: Packet completion in the named-owner source
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Collision separation for recorded packet diagrams]
\label{lem:packet-collision}
Let $P$ be a finite partial diagram consisting of literal disjoint
regular full $G$-packets, with exactly one actual owner label at
each point, total functions $t_g$ within each packet, and only
complete fine interpacket matrices in colours outside $F$ as
records.  Suppose there is an owner-preserving, packetwise injective
homomorphism $q:P\to N$ respecting all the records, and let $A_\ast$
be a specified complete full-packet base on which $q$ is already
an induced embedding.  It can be modified to an \emph{injective
completion} in $N$ of the displayed partial diagram, with all
distinct packets separated, while fixing $q|_{A_\ast}$.
The base may be empty.  Here ``completion'' adds colours to
unrecorded pairs; this is not an HKN embedding reflecting their
absence.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Realisation of tree amalgams over complete packet bases]
\label{lem:packet-tree-realisation}
Let $D$ be a finite free tree amalgam of copies of $A$ with
independently permitted $\Gamma$-relabelled owner predicates and
unchanged function symbols $t_g$.  There is an injective map
$\iota:D\to N$ preserving every displayed relation, owner predicate
and unary function, and restricting to an induced embedding on each
complete source copy.  If a designated source copy has already been
realised in $N$, its image may be kept fixed.

declarations.title: What an HKN homomorphism-embedding preserves
declarations.heading: Local HKN maps and injective packet completions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[What an HKN homomorphism-embedding preserves]
\label{lem:hkn-irreducible-packet-control}
Let $P$ be a finite unary-function-closed partial diagram made of
literal disjoint regular full $G$-packets, with recorded interpacket
edges only in complete fine matrices.  Let $f:P\to D$ be a
$\Gamma$-homomorphism-embedding in the HKN sense, allowing its one
global language component.  Then $f$ restricts to an embedding on
\emph{each} full packet and on the union of \emph{each recorded pair}
of distinct packets.  In particular, it preserves the entire
specified function-value sets and all recorded fine edges on those
substructures.  It need not be injective on the union of two
\emph{unrecorded} packets.
\end{lemma}
