declarations.title: Global language normalisation for local HKN tree maps
declarations.heading: Local HKN maps and injective packet completions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Global language normalisation for local HKN tree maps]
\label{lem:hkn-global-language-normalisation}
Let $P$ be any finite $\Gamma$-structure
in the owner-language/packet signature
and let $f=(\gamma,f_V):P\to D$ be a
$\Gamma$-homomorphism-embedding, where
$D$ is a free tree amalgamation of
permitted $\Gamma$-relabelled copies
of one complete full-packet source $A$.
Here $\Gamma$ permutes ONLY owner
predicate names, fixing all literal
fine binary atoms and all named
unary translations $t_g$.

Then, after replacing the ENTIRE
target $D$ by its ONE GLOBAL language
relabel $D'=\gamma^{-1}D$, the same
vertex map defines a
homomorphism-embedding
\[
              f'=(\mathrm{id}_L,f_V):P\to D'.
\tag{HLN}\label{eq:hkn-global-language-normalisation}
\]
The structure $D'$ remains a free
tree amalgamation of permitted
$\Gamma$-relabelled copies of $A$.
Every source irreducible substructure
on which $f$ was an embedding
remains embedded by $f'$.
In particular, a protected complete
source copy has its ACTUAL original
owner predicates, fine atom names
and unary translation equations
preserved literally BEFORE any
tree realisation inside $N_B$.

No choice of a separate language
component on individual tree
copies, nor a group-theoretic
section $\Gamma\to\Aut(N_B)$, is
involved in this normalisation.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Injectivisation of a local HKN tree packet map
declarations.heading: Local HKN maps and injective packet completions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Injectivisation of a local HKN tree packet map]
\label{lem:hkn-local-tree-packet-injectivisation}
Let \(P\) be a finite partial
\(\Gamma\)-diagram on \(k\) distinct
ACTUAL regular full \(G\)-packets,
with exactly one owner label on
each point, all unary
\(t_g\)-functions total, and
recorded interpacket relations
consisting only of entire
nonthin fine-colour matrices.
Assume there exists a
\(\Gamma\)-homomorphism-embedding
\[
        f:P\longrightarrow D,
\]
where \(D\) is a finite free
tree amalgam of permitted
\(\Gamma\)-relabelled copies of
the same complete full-packet
source \(A\). Then \(P\)
admits an INJECTIVE
record-preserving completion
in \(N_B\) on its original
finite vertex set, with
all \(k\) packets occupying
distinct actual \(F\)-classes.

If \(P\) contains a designated
complete full-packet copy
\(A_\ast\) on which \(f\)
restricts to an embedding,
its image can be identified
with the prescribed copy
of \(A_\ast\subseteq N_B\)
and kept pointwise fixed
throughout injectivisation.
No global injectivity of
\(f\) is assumed.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Chord-complete HKN locality on short origin cycles
declarations.heading: Local HKN maps and injective packet completions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Chord-complete HKN locality on short origin cycles]
\label{lem:hkn-chord-complete-short-cycle}
Let \(P\) be a finite
partially recorded actual
regular full-\(G\)-packet
diagram satisfying the
three source conditions
of
\cref{lem:hkn-local-tree-packet-injectivisation}.
Fix a simple SPECIFIED
origin cycle with \(k\)
DISTINCT actual packet
indices
\(p_1,\ldots,p_k\),
and assume \(k|G|\le n\).
Suppose the HKN locality
condition of Theorem~1.2
holds for EVERY
functionally closed
substructure of \(P\)
with at most \(n\)
actual vertices.
Then the COMPLETE
INDUCED partial packet
diagram on the packets
\(p_1,\ldots,p_k\)
admits an injective
same-vertex completion
in \(N_B\), preserving
ALL its recorded
nonthin fine matrices,
including EVERY recorded
chord between
nonconsecutive indices
of the chosen cycle.
In particular the
cycle has an injective
typed origin completion.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Unrecorded packets can collapse under an HKN map
declarations.heading: Local HKN maps and injective packet completions
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Unrecorded packets can collapse under an HKN map]
\label{ex:hkn-unrecorded-collapse}
Take $G\cong C_2$ and three regular packets
$\Pi_0,\Pi_1,\Pi_2$.  Record one complete nonthin matrix
between $\Pi_0,\Pi_1$ and the same matrix between
$\Pi_1,\Pi_2$, but no matrix between $\Pi_0,\Pi_2$.
The map to a complete two-packet source which identifies
$\Pi_0$ with $\Pi_2$ and fixes $\Pi_1$ is a
homomorphism-embedding: all irreducible substructures lie in
one packet or one recorded adjacent pair, on which the map is
an embedding.  It is not globally injective.  In a source with
infinitely many regular packets and the same nonthin matrix
between distinct packets, the diagram nevertheless has an
injective completion using three distinct packets.  This example
separates the HKN definition from the later, genuinely injective
completion step.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Relative owner $\Gamma$-EPPA
declarations.heading: Full-row universe, lifts and output
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Relative owner $\Gamma$-EPPA]
\label{thm:R07-relative-eppa}
The colouring~\eqref{eq:R07-decoding}, together with its
original full-packet structure, is a finite member of the
actual owner-typed age of $N$, containing $A$ as an induced
complete full-packet substructure. For \emph{every} structural
$\Gamma$-automorphism $s$ of $B_0$ as in
\eqref{eq:R07-structural} and \emph{every} matrix $C$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:R07-correction}, the map $\alpha_C$ is a
$\Gamma$-automorphism of this \emph{same} completed structure,
with the owner-language component of $s$. It need not preserve
the zero-row source setwise.

For a prescribed source-extension request, choose $s$ extending
its structural map and $C$ satisfying its zero-row conditions.
Then $\alpha_C$ extends that request. Consequently every finite
family of compatible relative requests over the fixed owner set
$B$, including empty-real-domain requests, has one common finite
$\Gamma$-EPPA witness.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Quantifiers, size, and scope of the argument
declarations.heading: Full-row universe, lifts and output
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Quantifiers, size, and scope of the argument]
\label{rem:R07-scope}
The finite construction uses one $B_0$, one full-row set $W$,
one injective completion certificate for $W^\#$, one greatest
strong-PC fixed family and one decoder.  Only afterwards are
individual correction matrices chosen.  The size is exactly
$|I|\,|G|^{|I|+1}$ and no uniform size bound across varying
finite quotient witnesses is claimed.  We have not assumed
$H=1$, equivariant packet origins, coherent EPPA, equality of PC
menus with full solution spectra, or that HKN faithfulness alone
gives a completable reservoir.  All the statements here depend
on the preceding in-manuscript relative closure, full-owner
transversal, typed gate and reading proofs, together with
published HKN and the CCO-specific RAW-HULL route using Erd\H{o}s.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Exact finite compatibility criterion for prescribed full rows
declarations.heading: Completion certificate and compatible row requests
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact finite compatibility criterion for prescribed full rows]
\label{lem:R07-row-compatibility-iff}
Fix one structural map
$s(i,z)=(\sigma i,z+b_i)$ as in
\eqref{eq:R07-structural}. For each $i\in I$
let $T_i\subseteq G^I$ be a finite
set of ACTUAL source rows, possibly
empty. For each $f\in T_i$ prescribe
one target row $r_{i,f}\in G^I$
at structural index $\sigma i$.
For $f\in T_i$ put
\[
 A_{i,f}(j)=r_{i,f}(\sigma j)+f(j)+b_i
                  \qquad(j\in I).
\tag{RC1}\label{eq:R07-row-compatibility-shift}
\]
There is ONE matrix $C$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:R07-correction} such that
$\alpha_C$ sends EACH requested
ACTUAL packet $(i,f)$ to the
packet $(\sigma i,r_{i,f})$ if
and only if BOTH conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item for every $i$, the functions
$A_{i,f}$ are identical over
ALL $f\in T_i$ (denote this
common function by $A_i$ when
$T_i\ne\varnothing$);
\item for every UNRECORDED pair
of DISTINCT structural indices
$\{i,j\}$ with
$T_i,T_j\ne\varnothing$,
\[
                         A_i(j)=A_j(i).
\tag{RC2}\label{eq:R07-row-compatibility-edge}
\]
\end{enumerate}
When each touched index has
ONE requested row and the
touched indices form a
recorded clique, both
conditions are automatic.
No condition is imposed
on diagonal entries $C_{ii}$,
nor on RECORDED off-diagonal
pairs. The source rows and
target rows are ACTUAL full
functions on all of $I$,
not owner-stabiliser cosets.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Completion certificate and compatible row requests

declarations.title: Sharp obstructions for independently forced rows
declarations.heading: Completion certificate and compatible row requests
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Sharp obstructions for independently forced rows]
\label{rem:R07-row-conflict-controls}
Even with $G=\mathbb F_2$,
two different rows $f\ne f'$
over the SAME structural index
cannot both be sent to target
zero rows by one $\alpha_C$:
then the two functions in (RC1)
differ by $f+f'$, violating
condition (i). For two touched
DISTINCT UNRECORDED indices
$i,j$, choose source rows
with $f_i(j)=1$, $f_j(i)=0$,
target both zero, and $b_i=b_j=0$.
This forces $C_{ij}=1$ and
$C_{ji}=0$, contradicting
\eqref{eq:R07-correction}.
These failures explain why
the later unsafe-clique
argument first proves ONE
touched ACTUAL packet over
each structural index and
a RECORDED clique on those
indices, rather than choosing
row corrections independently.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Full-row permutations and zero-row requests

declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full-row permutations and zero-row requests]
\label{lem:R07-zero-row}
For every $C$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:R07-correction},
$\alpha_C$ is a permutation of $W$, commutes with every $t_g$,
preserves all the recorded fine colours of $W^\#$ and induces
$\gamma$ on its owner predicates.  Moreover, for every requested
source map that has structural extension $s$, a matrix $C$ can be
chosen such that $\alpha_C$ extends that map on the zero-row
source.  This includes requests with empty real domain.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Effective rows and verification of the decoder
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Global diagonal thin translations survive the R07 decoder]
\label{lem:R07-global-diagonal-thin}
Let $\rho:G\to\Gamma$
be the ACTUAL homomorphism
induced by the original global
thin translations on the
finite $G$-invariant owner
set $B$. The map $\rho$
is NOT assumed injective:
a nontrivial thin owner
stabiliser $H$ may lie
in its kernel.
On the completed full-row
R07 universe $W$ define,
for every $g\in G$,
\[
          \widehat t_g(i,f,z)=(i,f,z+g).
\tag{RDT}\label{eq:R07-global-diagonal-thin}
\]
Then $\widehat t_g$ is a
$\Gamma$-automorphism of the
SAME decoded COMPLETE finite
structure, with owner-language
component precisely $\rho(g)$,
and fixes EVERY literal
original fine binary
colour, not just its palette.
It preserves EACH actual
full packet setwise and acts
regularly on that packet.
No freeness is asserted for
the induced action of $G$
on OWNER labels, whose
stabiliser may be nontrivial.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Orbit-safe typed palettes
declarations.heading: Orbit-safe full-packet completion under thin translations
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Orbit-safe typed palettes]
\label{def:orbit-safe}
For a diversity colour $a\in P_{st}$ set
\[
  a\in S^{G}_{st}\ \Longleftrightarrow\
           ga\in S\quad\text{for every }g\in G.
\]
Equivalently, if $x,y$ are origins of two distinct full
$G$-packets and $\col(x,y)=a$, then $a\in S^G_{st}$
precisely when \emph{every} entry of their full
$G\times G$ colour matrix belongs to $S$.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: One full thin packet covers one whole owner orbit
declarations.heading: Orbit-safe full-packet completion under thin translations
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[One full thin packet covers one whole owner orbit]
\label{lem:orbit-safe-owner-helper}
Let $G$ be the ACTUAL finite regular
thin translation group on every
real full $F_Q$-packet, acting on
the named fine $E$-owner set $U$.
For any actual packet $\Pi=F_Q[x]$
whose origin has owner
$s=\operatorname{own}(x)\in U$,
\[
 \{\operatorname{own}(y):y\in\Pi\}=G s,
 \quad
 |\{y\in\Pi:\operatorname{own}(y)=t\}|
        =|\operatorname{Stab}_G(s)|
       \quad(t\in Gs).
\tag{OH}\label{eq:orbit-safe-owner-helper}
\]
Thus for finite $G$-invariant
$U$, exactly ONE actual full
packet from EACH $G$-orbit
of owner labels suffices for
a full-packet helper containing
a representative of EVERY
named owner in $U$. This
does NOT assume the $G$-action
on owners is free; it only uses
the regular action on REAL
packet vertices. Given any
finite full-packet closed
old real set $V$, the helper
can be realised packetwise
DISJOINT from $V$ in $N_U$
by relative full-packet
closed SAP.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Closed strong $S$ supplies strong orbit-safe transversal palettes
declarations.heading: Orbit-safe full-packet completion under thin translations
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Closed strong $S$ supplies strong orbit-safe transversal palettes]
\label{lem:orbit-safe-strong}
Assume original strong $S$-amalgamation over finite
\emph{absolute real acl-closed} spans and normalised unary
closure $\operatorname{acl}_{Q}(A)=F_Q[A]$.
Then the tagged palettes $S^G_{st}$ are nonempty and
strongly amalgamate \emph{all} finite spans in the
primitive all-owner transversal $\mathcal U_U$.
They are converse compatible, pure-$\Gamma$-covariant,
and equivariant under each unilateral endpoint translation:
\[
     gS^G_{st}=S^G_{gs,t}=S^G_{s,gt}
       \quad\text{(as raw fine-colour subsets, with moved types).}
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: All-row orbit-safe R07 interface
declarations.heading: Orbit-safe full-packet completion under thin translations
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[All-row orbit-safe R07 interface]
\label{lem:orbit-safe-all-row-interface}
Work in the actual full-owner source of
\cref{lem:orbit-safe-strong}, with the ORIGINAL
fine-colour palette \(S\), its thin-saturated
orbit-safe palettes \(S^G_{st}\), and a
pure-\(\Gamma\)-covariant augmented selector
\(h=h_{S^G}\). Assume that \(\Gamma\) contains the
owner action of the global thin translations, as required for
\cref{prop:moving-readings}. Let \(W^\#\) be one fixed
finite R07 partial packet reservoir, and
suppose the origin transversal has an
INJECTIVE completion in the owner-typed
SAP source. Run the greatest strong-PC
procedure ONCE on the actual packet
indices \(p=(i,f)\), and denote its
terminal exact menus by \(D_{pq}\).

Then for EVERY pair of DISTINCT actual
packets \(p=(i,f)\ne q=(j,k)\)
the following exhaustive alternatives hold.

\smallskip
\noindent\textup{(R)} If \(\{i,j\}\) is an
originally RECORDED structural pair
(\(i\ne j\)), then \(D_{pq}\) is the
literal original singleton \( \{c_{ij}\}\).
For every \(z,w\in G\) the decoded
old fine atom of \((i,f,z),(j,k,w)\)
is precisely the original recorded
structural fine colour
\[
       \operatorname{col}_{B_0}((i,z),(j,w))
                          =(z+w)c_{ij}.
\]

\smallskip
\noindent\textup{(U)} Otherwise the pair
is originally UNRECORDED. This includes
the case \(i=j\) with \(f\ne k\).
Then \(D_{pq}\cap S^G_{\beta_i,\beta_j}
\ne\varnothing\), and for ALL
\(z,w,u,g,h\in G\), the reading
\[
 a=h^u_{z\beta_i,w\beta_j}
             \bigl((z+w)D_{pq}\bigr)
\]
lies in \(S^G_{z\beta_i,w\beta_j}\).
Moreover its entire translated
interpacket matrix
\[
             (g+h)a
\]
consists of ORIGINAL fine atoms in
\(S\), with the properly shifted owner
tags. No old singleton record is
recoloured to achieve this property.

All these conclusions hold in ONE
preselected finite PC fixed family,
independently of which permitted
R07 structural extension and correction
matrix will be chosen later.
The completed structure has no extra
assumption that the structural
automorphism of the INCOMPLETE
reservoir preserves its arbitrary
completion certificate.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Safe moving readings preserve every missing matrix
declarations.heading: Orbit-safe full-packet completion under thin translations
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Safe moving readings preserve every missing matrix]
\label{lem:orbit-safe-readings}
Assume $\Gamma$ contains the induced diagonal thin-owner action.
Let $h=h_{S^G}$ be the pure-$\Gamma$-covariant,
converse-compatible, survivor-hereditary full-PC selector
from Lemmas~\ref{lem:augmented-safe-algebra} and
\ref{lem:orbit-safe-strong}, and let
\[
      h^u_{st}(D)=u\,h_{us,t}(uD)
\]
be its moving-type readings as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:moving-readings}.
Whenever an original exact $D\in\mathcal H_{st}$ meets
$S^G_{st}$, then for \emph{every} $u\in G$
\[
                 h^u_{st}(D)\in S^G_{st}\subseteq S.
\]
Suppose an R07 full-row reservoir has an injective
completion of its \emph{origin transversal} in
$\mathcal U_U$.  After greatest strong-PC and the safe
selector on the original packet-pair domains,
\emph{every} originally unrecorded actual interpacket
pair receives a fine $S$-colour under the entire R07
row decoder, for \emph{all} values of the reading
parameter $u(x,y)$ and \emph{all} endpoint translations.
All structural source extensions and their row corrections
continue to preserve the decoded fine colours.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Simultaneous full-row zeroing on a recorded packet clique
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous full-row zeroing on a recorded packet clique]
\label{lem:acf-recorded-row-zeroing}
Use the R07 full-row packet universe
\(W=\{(i,f,z):i\in I,\ f\in G^I,\ z\in G\}\)
and a structural packet automorphism
\(s(i,z)=(\sigma i,z+b_i)\).
Let \(J\subseteq I\) be a set of DISTINCT
structural indices such that EVERY two
different indices of \(J\) are a
RECORDED pair in \(\mathcal R\).
For each \(i\in J\), specify one actual
row \(f_i\in G^I\). Then some correction
matrix \(C\in G^{I\times I}\) satisfies
the R07 equations
\(C_{ij}+C_{ji}=0\) on all UNRECORDED
\(i\ne j\), and the associated
automorphism \(\alpha_C\) sends
\[
     \{(i,f_i,z):z\in G\}
        \quad\text{onto}\quad
     \{(\sigma i,0,z):z\in G\}
\]
up to its fixed internal translation \(b_i\),
SIMULTANEOUSLY for every \(i\in J\).
This is a clique-transport correction,
not an assertion that the automorphism
also fixes all original zero-row source packets.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Unsafe multi-packet cliques descend to the padded source
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Unsafe multi-packet cliques descend to the padded source]
\label{lem:acf-multipacket-rooted-transport}
Let \(A^+\) be a finite complete full-packet
source obtained from \(F_Q[A_0]\) by adding
padding packets with EVERY new cross matrix
\(S_Q\)-safe, including all padding-to-original
pairs. Build the finite R07 full-row decoder
from a completable HKN structural reservoir
\(B_0\supseteq A^+\), using the orbit-safe
selector \(h_{S^G}\) on its originally
unrecorded packet pairs.

For every all-non-\(S_Q\) clique \(Z\)
in the decoded finite witness that
meets at least TWO distinct actual packets,
there is one decoded \(\widetilde\Gamma\)-
automorphism taking \(Z\) into
\(F_Q[A_0]\). More precisely, its
structural component moves all touched
structural packet indices into those of
the padded source \(A^+\), and one
simultaneous full-row correction moves
the selected actual packet of each such
index into its zero row.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Invariant full-packet orbit trim and selected-root correction
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Invariant full-packet orbit trim and selected-root correction]
\label{lem:acf-invariant-packet-orbit-trim}
Let $D_0$ be a finite complete original-language structure,
$F$ an actual invariant finite regular packet equivalence, and
$G\le K\le\Aut(D_0)$. Suppose the global thin group $G$
leaves each $F$-packet setwise invariant and acts regularly on it.
For nonempty $A_0\subseteq D_0$ put
\[
 F[A_0]=\bigcup_{a\in A_0}F[a],
 \qquad D=\bigcup_{\beta\in K}\beta(F[A_0]).
\tag{OT}\label{eq:acf-packet-orbit-trim}
\]
Then $D$ is a finite induced, full-$F$-closed, $K$-invariant
substructure containing $F[A_0]$. For every nonempty subset
$Z\subseteq D$ contained in one $F$-packet and every selected
$z\in Z$, some $\alpha\in K|_D$ satisfies
\[
 \alpha(Z)\subseteq F[A_0],\qquad \alpha(z)\in A_0.
\tag{OTR}\label{eq:acf-packet-orbit-root}
\]
More generally, if $Z\subseteq D$ is nonempty and some
$\delta\in K$ carries it into $F[A_0]$, then \textup{(OTR)}
holds for every selected $z\in Z$, even when $Z$ meets several
packets. For a $K$-equivariant owner map $\pi:D_0\to B$,
\[
                    \pi(D)=K\cdot\pi(F[A_0]);
\]
in particular $\pi(D)=B$ if $K\cdot\pi(A_0)=B$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Full-owner support makes the R07 language component recoverable
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full-owner support makes the R07 language component recoverable]
\label{lem:acf-full-owner-language-faithfulness}
Let $U$ be a finite set of actual fine owner labels and
$\widetilde\Gamma\le\operatorname{Sym}(U)$. Let $D_0$ be a
complete finite owner-typed R07 decoder in which every label
in $U$ is realised. Its semilinear automorphisms are pairs
$(\gamma,\alpha)$, where $\gamma\in\widetilde\Gamma$ permutes
owner predicates and $\alpha$ preserves every literal original
fine atomic binary colour. Let $K$ be their underlying
permutation group. Then the forgetful map
\[
 \Aut_{\widetilde\Gamma}(D_0)\longrightarrow K,
 \qquad (\gamma,\alpha)\longmapsto\alpha
\tag{FOL}\label{eq:acf-full-owner-language-faithfulness}
\]
is an isomorphism. In particular the owner-language component
is a well-defined homomorphism on $K$.

Suppose $D_0$ is the full-row decoder of a structural
$\widetilde\Gamma$-EPPA reservoir containing a complete
full-packet source $A^+$ that meets every owner in $U$, and the
reservoir extends every empty-real-domain
$\widetilde\Gamma$-request. Then $K\to\widetilde\Gamma$ is onto.
If an equivariant surjection $U\to B$ induces an onto map
$\widetilde\Gamma\to\Gamma_B$, the composite $K\to\Gamma_B$
is onto as well. None of these assertions requires a group
section or faithfulness of the original thin action
$\rho:G\to\widetilde\Gamma$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Normalised relative rooted MI construction
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Normalised relative rooted MI construction]
\label{lem:acf-relative-mi-normal}
Let \(Q\) be an infinite standing homogeneous source with no
nonidentity finite-class exact equivalence, and let
\(S_Q\subseteq\mathcal D(Q)\) have strong closed amalgamation.
Write \(F_Q\) for its greatest finite-class invariant equivalence
and \(E\) for its unique minimal infinite direction. Let
\(H\ge E\) be an actual invariant FULL EXACT owner equivalence,
and assume \(\Age(Q/E)\) has ordinary EPPA.
Let \(A_0\subseteq Q\) be finite
nonempty and let \(B\subseteq Q/H\) be finite, induced and
satisfy
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(B\) contains the owner projection of \(A_0\),
  is an ordinary EPPA witness for that projection,
  and the union of their owner orbits covers \(B\):
  \(\Gamma_B\cdot\operatorname{own}_H(A_0)=B\);
\item \(B\) is closed under the largest finite-class
  equivalence of the actual owner quotient \(Q/H\).
\end{enumerate}
Here \(\Gamma_B=\Aut(B)\) in the actual quotient language, and
\(\operatorname{own}_H(x)=[x]_H\). A source request \((p,\gamma)\)
is \emph{compatible} precisely when
\[
 \operatorname{own}_H(p(x))=\gamma(\operatorname{own}_H(x))
 \qquad(x\in\operatorname{dom}p).
\]
This includes every \((\varnothing,\gamma)\).
There exists one finite, full-\(F_Q\)-closed, original-language
\(D\subseteq Q\), projecting onto exactly \(B\) and
containing \(F_Q[A_0]\), such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every compatible source partial automorphism
  \((p,\gamma)\), \(p:A_0\rightharpoonup A_0\),
  \(\gamma\in\Gamma_B\), extends to a relative
  automorphism of \(D\) with owner component precisely
  \(\gamma\); this includes all compatible singleton
  and empty-real-domain requests;
\item for every nonempty all-non-\(S_Q\) clique
  \(Z\subseteq D\) and \(z\in Z\), some relative
  automorphism \(\alpha\) satisfies
  \[
       \alpha(Z)\subseteq F_Q[A_0],
                   \qquad \alpha(z)\in A_0.
  \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors

declarations.title: Prescribed owner action on one point
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Prescribed owner action on one point]
\label{lem:acf-point-homogeneity}
Let \(D\subseteq Q\) be a finite induced structure whose image
under an invariant owner quotient is a finite set \(B\), and
suppose every automorphism of \(D\) induces an automorphism of \(B\).
Suppose every point of \(D\) is moved into the original
nonempty \(A_0\subseteq D\) by some relative
automorphism, and every compatible singleton request
\(a\mapsto a'\) on original points \(a,a'\in A_0\),
with \emph{every} prescribed compatible
\(\gamma\in\Aut(B)\), extends in \(D\).
Then for arbitrary \(x,y\in D\) and
\(\gamma\in\Aut(B)\) with
\(\gamma(\operatorname{own}(x))=\operatorname{own}(y)\),
there exists \(\beta\in\Aut(D)\) inducing precisely
\(\gamma\) and sending \(x\) to \(y\).
Consequently it sends any subset of \(F_Q[x]\)
into \(F_Q[y]\).
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors

declarations.title: Finite exact reconstruction preserves a root
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite exact reconstruction preserves a root]
\label{lem:acf-finite-lift}
Let \(K\) be a finite-class \emph{exact} invariant
equivalence of a standing source \(Q\), and write
\(\pi:Q\to\overline Q=Q/K\).
For any finite real \(A_0\) one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:acf-finite-acl}
 \operatorname{acl}_Q(A_0)=
 \pi^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{acl}_{\overline Q}(\pi A_0)\bigr).
\end{equation}
The strong closed-\(S_Q\) hypothesis descends to
\(\overline Q\) for the full-matrix palette
\[
 \overline S=\{q\in\mathcal D(\overline Q):
                    \Lambda_K(q)\subseteq S_Q\},
\]
where \(\Lambda_K(q)\) denotes the set of original fine
colours occurring in full \(K\times K\) cross matrices over \(q\).
For nonempty \(A_0\), if \(\overline D\) is an ordinary EPPA
witness with rooted \(\overline S\)-ACF over \(\pi(A_0)\),
then \(D=\pi^{-1}(\overline D)\) is an ordinary EPPA witness
with rooted \(S_Q\)-ACF over \(A_0\).

For the following STRONGER RELATIVE
assertion, assume explicitly that the
original owner quotient is an ACTUAL
invariant FULL EXACT quotient \(Q/H\).
Its corresponding coarse owner quotient
after factoring out \(K\) is
\[
 \overline Q/\overline H=Q/(K\vee H),
 \qquad \overline H=(K\vee H)/K .
\]
Suppose a finite relative rooted ACF
witness \(\overline D\) for \(\pi(A_0)\), with safe palette
\(\overline S\), is available in \(\overline Q\) over a finite
coarse owner set
\(\overline B\subseteq Q/(K\vee H)\).
Let \(B\subseteq Q/H\) be the
\emph{complete finite inverse owner
packet} over \(\overline B\), and suppose
the induced map
\(\Aut(B)\to\Aut(\overline B)\) is
surjective with kernel transitive on
each owner-cover fibre. Then
\(D=\pi^{-1}(\overline D)\) is a rooted
relative ACF witness over \(B\) for
\(A_0\), with all compatible source
requests and rooted targets preserved.
The explicit exactness of \(H\)
is needed here to invoke joint
exact-sort homogeneity; no claim is
made for an arbitrary nonexact owner
quotient under these hypotheses alone.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors

declarations.title: The finite owner hypotheses
declarations.heading: Rooted relative witnesses on unary-closure factors
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The finite owner hypotheses]
The finite owner-packet and kernel-transitivity
hypotheses in Lemma~\ref{lem:acf-finite-lift}
are substantial.  They will be furnished
simultaneously for all canonical MI factors by
the finite exact-quotient master below, rather
than by choosing incompatible finite owner
sets independently.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Finite-base EPPA and point homogeneity
declarations.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite-base EPPA and point homogeneity]
\label{lem:acf-owner-provider}
Let \(\pi:Q\to O\) be an actual exact quotient
of a standing source.  Assume \(\Age(Q)\) has ordinary EPPA.
Let \(B\subseteq O\)
be finite, nonempty, induced and \(F_O\)-closed.
For any finite \(A\subseteq\pi^{-1}(B)\) there
is a finite induced \(D\subseteq Q\), containing
\(A\), which is \(F_Q\)-closed, projects
precisely onto \(B\), and has:
\begin{enumerate}
\item every compatible pair \((p,\gamma)\),
  with \(p\) a partial automorphism of \(A\)
  and \(\gamma\in\Aut(B)\), extended by an
  automorphism of \(D\) inducing \(\gamma\);
\item for arbitrary \(x,y\in D\) and
  \(\gamma\in\Aut(B)\) satisfying
  \(\gamma(\pi x)=\pi y\), an automorphism
  of \(D\) inducing exactly \(\gamma\)
  and carrying \(x\) to \(y\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular \(\Aut(D)\to\Aut(B)\) is onto
and its kernel is transitive on each fibre.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients

declarations.title: Automorphisms of a full exact fibre product
declarations.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Automorphisms of a full exact fibre product]
\label{lem:acf-fibreproduct-aut}
Let \(X\) be a source in the standing one-sort symmetric
homomorphic CCO setting, and let \(E,J\) be invariant full exact
equivalences on \(X\). Put
\(K=E\cap J\) and \(H=E\vee J\), and
regard \(X/K\) as the ACTUAL fine-coloured
fibre product
\[
       X/K=(X/E)\times_{X/H}(X/J).
\]
Let \(D\subseteq X/E\) and \(C\subseteq X/J\)
be finite induced structures whose images
in \(X/H\) are one and the same finite
induced set \(B\), and assume both
\(D\to B\), \(C\to B\) are surjective.
Let \(W=D\times_B C\) be the FULL finite
fibre product, with its original induced
fine-colour structure from \(X/K\).
Then restriction to the two coordinates
gives a natural group isomorphism
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
  \operatorname{Aut}(W)\cong
  \operatorname{Aut}(D)
       \times_{\operatorname{Aut}(B)}
  \operatorname{Aut}(C).\qquad}
\tag{FPA}\label{eq:acf-fibreproduct-aut}
\]
In particular, the formula concerns
automorphisms of the FULL finite induced
fibre product; it does not hold merely
from a set-theoretic bijection for an
arbitrary coloured subset of that product.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients

declarations.title: Full-fibre-product prescribed-owner kernels and EPPA
declarations.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Full-fibre-product prescribed-owner kernels and EPPA]
\label{lem:acf-fibreproduct-owner-kernels}
Let $D\to O$ and $C\to O$
be finite induced, SURJECTIVE
actual exact quotient systems,
and let $W=D\times_O C$ be
their FULL induced fine-coloured
fibre product. Assume the ACTUAL
group identity
\[
   \Aut(W)=\Aut(D)\times_{\Aut(O)}
                                \Aut(C)
\tag{FK}\label{eq:acf-fibreproduct-kernel-action}
\]
from \cref{lem:acf-fibreproduct-aut}.
Let $T$ be an actual quotient of $D$, with its induced
automorphism action. The quotients $T$ and $O$ need not be nested.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\Aut(D)\to\Aut(T)$
is ONTO and its kernel acts
TRANSITIVELY on each fibre
of $D\to T$;
\item $C$ has prescribed-owner
point homogeneity: for ALL
$x,y\in C$ and EVERY
$\delta\in\Aut(O)$ with
$\delta(\pi_Cx)=\pi_Cy$,
there exists $h\in\Aut(C)$
inducing EXACTLY $\delta$
and satisfying $hx=y$.
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $\Aut(W)\to\Aut(T)$
is ONTO and its kernel is
TRANSITIVE on each fibre
of $W\to T$;
\item if the projection $D\to O$ factors through $T$ and
$W_T=T\times_O C$
is also a FULL induced
actual exact fibre product
with its corresponding
automorphism-group identity,
then $\Aut(W)\to\Aut(W_T)$
is ONTO and its kernel is
TRANSITIVE on every fibre
of $W\to W_T$.
\end{enumerate}
In either case no group section
is assumed.

Moreover let $A_W\subseteq W$
be an actual finite induced
source whose quotient
projections $A_D,A_C$
are as displayed.
Suppose $D$ has EPPA for
$A_D$, and $C$ extends
EVERY compatible partial
automorphism of $A_C$
with EVERY prescribed
owner permutation
$\delta\in\Aut(O)$.
Then $W$ has ordinary
EPPA for $A_W$, provided
the two projection kernels
and quotient atomic orbitals
are ACTUAL invariant old
fine-colour unions so that
partial automorphisms of
$A_W$ descend to genuine
partial maps of $A_D,A_C$.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients

declarations.title: Finite exact-quotient owner master
declarations.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite exact-quotient owner master]
\label{thm:acf-owner-master}
Let \(X\) be a nonempty transitive standing
source, and assume ordinary EPPA for \(\Age(X/E)\) for
\emph{every} exact quotient \(X/E\), including \(E=\Id\).
Let
\(\mathcal E_{\rm ex}(X)\) be its full finite
lattice of invariant exact equivalences.
For every finite nonempty \(A\subseteq X\)
there is \emph{one} finite induced \(B\subseteq X\)
containing \(A\), with
\(B_E=\pi_E(B)\subseteq X/E\) for every exact \(E\),
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(M1)] each \(B_E\) is an ordinary EPPA
  witness for \(\pi_E(A)\);
\item[(M2)] each \(B_E\) is \(F_{X/E}\)-closed
  in its actual ambient quotient;
\item[(M3)] for \(E\le H\) exact, the natural
  \(\Aut(B_E)\to\Aut(B_H)\) is onto, and
  its kernel acts transitively on \emph{each}
  fibre of \(B_E\to B_H\);
\item[(M4)] for every finite family
  \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) of exact equivalences,
  \(B_{\cap_iE_i}\) is precisely the set of
  tuples from \(\prod_iB_{E_i}\) whose images
  agree in every \(B_{E_i\vee E_j}\).
\end{enumerate}
The construction uses only finitely many
ordinary EPPA-provider steps and no safe
palette or ACF induction hypothesis.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Why the master is not a coloured product assumption
declarations.heading: A simultaneous finite master for exact owner quotients
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Why the master is not a coloured product assumption]
The finite \(\operatorname{Down}(P)\)
coordinatisation is applied to the lattice
of \emph{actual exact equivalences}.
The intermediate sources \(X_U\) retain
all their original fine binary orbitals.
They need not be pure sets, Cartesian
Hamming products, or freely coloured
primitive structures.  The new local
\(D_p\) is obtained by ordinary EPPA
on its actual quotient source.
The sole padding occurs in an ordinary
EPPA construction, not in a rooted
ACF target; this is essential when
owner-relative closure is larger than
the absolute real algebraic closure.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Joint-owner prescribed-action homogeneity of a full MI tuple witness
declarations.heading: Rooted closure-faithful ordinary EPPA
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Joint-owner prescribed-action homogeneity of a full MI tuple witness]
\label{lem:acf-multi-owner-point-homogeneity}
Let $X$ be a source in the standing one-sort symmetric
homomorphic CCO setting. Let $r\ge1$ and let
$C_1,\ldots,C_r$ be ACTUAL
invariant FULL EXACT kernel
equivalences, with
$\bigcap_i C_i=\Id_X$,
and choose ACTUAL exact
$H_i\ge C_i$, with
$H_*=\bigcap_i H_i$.
Assume the CRUCIAL
pairwise-common-quotient
JOIN GATE
\[
               C_i\vee C_j
                  =H_i\vee H_j
                          \qquad(i\ne j).
\tag{JOG}\label{eq:acf-joint-owner-join-gate}
\]
Write $Q_i=X/C_i$,
$\Omega=X/H_*$, and
$O_i=X/H_i$.

Let $B_\Omega\subseteq\Omega$
be a finite INDUCED owner
structure whose projections
$B_i\subseteq O_i$ satisfy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $B_\Omega$ is EXACTLY
the full set of compatible
tuples from the $B_i$,
with pairwise equality
tested in their actual
common quotient
$X/(H_i\vee H_j)$;
\item every
$\gamma\in\Gamma=
 \Aut(B_\Omega)$ induces
a well-defined automorphism
$\rho_i(\gamma)$ of each $B_i$.
\end{enumerate}
For every i, let
$D_i\subseteq Q_i$ be
a finite induced structure
projecting ONTO $B_i$,
with PRESCRIBED-OWNER POINT
HOMOGENEITY:
for EVERY $x_i,y_i\in D_i$
and EVERY
$\delta_i\in\Aut(B_i)$
carrying the owner of
$x_i$ to the owner of
$y_i$, there is
$\alpha_i\in\Aut(D_i)$
with EXACT owner component
$\delta_i$ and
$\alpha_i(x_i)=y_i$.

Let $W$ be the FULL finite
compatible tuple set
\[
 W=\{(x_i)_{i\le r}\in
             \prod_i D_i:
    \pi_{H_i\vee H_j}(x_i)=
    \pi_{H_i\vee H_j}(x_j)
                        \ (i<j)\}.
\tag{JOW}\label{eq:acf-joint-owner-full-witness}
\]
Then the ACTUAL exact CRT,
using the JOIN GATE
\eqref{eq:acf-joint-owner-join-gate},
identifies $W$ with a
finite induced subset of
original X, with owner
projection $\pi_{H_*}(W)$
EXACTLY $B_\Omega$.
Every coordinate projection $W\to D_i$ is also surjective.

Write $\operatorname{own}_i:\Aut(D_i)\to\Aut(B_i)$
for the actual induced owner-action map;
it is well-defined because the owner
kernel $H_i/C_i$ and all its quotient
pair orbitals are unions of the named
$Q_i$ fine binary orbitals.
The ENTIRE automorphism group, not just
the separately constructible maps, is
the actual finite group pullback
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \Aut(W)\cong
 \bigl\{(\alpha_i)_i\in\prod_i\Aut(D_i):
   \exists\gamma\in\Gamma\
   \forall i\
   \operatorname{own}_i(\alpha_i)
                    =\rho_i(\gamma)\bigr\}.
 \quad}
 \tag{JWA}\label{eq:acf-joint-owner-automorphisms}
\]
The witnessing $\gamma$ is UNIQUE:
the full owner set $B_\Omega$ is
determined pointwise by its complete
tuple of $B_i$ coordinates. This is
a group identity, not a choice of a
section $\Gamma\to\Aut(W)$.

Moreover for EVERY
$\gamma\in\Gamma$ and
EVERY $x,y\in W$ with
\[
            \gamma(\pi_{H_*}x)
                           =\pi_{H_*}y,
\]
there is ONE
$\alpha\in\Aut(W)$,
inducing precisely
$\gamma$ on ALL of
$B_\Omega$ and satisfying
$\alpha(x)=y$.
Thus the natural
$\Aut(W)\to\Gamma$
is ONTO and its kernel
is transitive on EVERY
full $B_\Omega$ owner
fibre. This conclusion
does not claim any
group section
$\Gamma\to\Aut(W)$.
The JOIN GATE is
ESSENTIAL: if two
$C_i=\Id$ while their
$H_i=\Top$ in a
nontrivial source,
coarse owner agreement
would admit ALL formal
ordered pairs $(x,y)$,
whereas the actual CRT
only permits $(x,x)$.

If in addition the
owner input
$B_\Omega$ has ordinary
EPPA for the projection
of a finite original
$A_0\subseteq W$, and
each $D_i$ extends
EVERY compatible partial
automorphism of its
projected input with
EVERY prescribed owner
component $\delta_i$,
then W has ordinary
EPPA for $A_0$ as well.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Rank-relative rooted ACF construction
declarations.heading: Rooted closure-faithful ordinary EPPA
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Rank-relative rooted ACF construction]
\label{lem:acf-rank-step}
Let \(M\) be a nonempty standing symmetric binary source,
and assume the rooted theorem, ordinary EPPA and the all-exact
finite owner-master theorem for \emph{every strictly smaller
actual exact quotient} of \(M\).  Let
\(S\subseteq\mathcal D(M)\) have strong closed
amalgamation as in Definition~\ref{def:rooted-acf}.
The local normalised MI safe-selector/R07 construction is the
explicit direct provider at this rank.

For every finite nonempty original real input
\(A_0\subseteq M\), there exists a finite induced
\(W\subseteq M\) containing \(\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0)\)
such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item every partial automorphism of \(A_0\) extends to
  an automorphism of the same \(W\);
\item for every nonempty \(Z\subseteq W\) whose distinct
  pairs have colours outside \(S\), and every selected
  \(z\in Z\), some \(\alpha\in\Aut(W)\) satisfies
  \[
       \alpha(Z)\subseteq\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0),
                 \qquad \alpha(z)\in A_0 .
                 \tag{\(\mathrm{ACF}\)}\label{eq:acf-main}
  \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus the witness is ordinary EPPA and
automorphism-transport closure-relative
\(S\)-clique faithful, in fact with a specified
root.  No coherent extension assignment is asserted.
\end{lemma}

\label{rem:acf-firewall}
This lemma uses no same-rank global ordinary EPPA or

the fine owner source $M/E$ is a strict quotient,
or a singleton when $E=\Top$.  The sole original-
source constructional obligation is the normalised
relative safe-MI HKN/R07 lemma, whose augmented safe
selector and orbit-covariant packet-matrix steps are
still subject to a separate end-to-end mathematical audit.
The following phased proof preserves these interfaces
and does not assert coherent EPPA.
\end{remark}

declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Rooted closure-faithful ordinary EPPA]
\label{thm:main-rooted-acf}
Let $M$ be a transitive countable homogeneous complete structure
in a finite named symmetric binary language, with AP/JEP and
semantic homomorphic CCO.  The age is triangle-defined by
Lemma~\ref{lem:cco-triangle-fullness}.  For every palette
$S\subseteq\mathcal D(M)$ strongly amalgamating finite
absolutely real-acl-closed spans, and every finite nonempty
$A_0\subseteq M$, there is one finite induced
$W\subseteq M$ containing $\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0)$
which extends every partial automorphism of $A_0$ and satisfies:
for every nonempty all-non-$S$ clique $Z\subseteq W$
and every $z\in Z$ some $\alpha\in\Aut(W)$ has
\[
 \alpha(Z)\subseteq\operatorname{acl}_M(A_0),
                 \qquad\alpha(z)\in A_0.
\]
This remains a source-relative candidate proof. Its packet-safe input
is \cref{lem:orbit-safe-all-row-interface}, and its normalised MI assembly
is \cref{lem:acf-relative-mi-normal}; the proof inherits their named
closure, safe-selector, reservoir and decoder hypotheses.
\end{theorem}

rooted construction keeps $A_0$ and $\operatorname{acl}(A_0)$

principal-factor provider is the rank-$n$ source itself.

\end{remark}

block-ordered hidden class is Ramsey.

declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Exact domains and equivalences are traces]
\label{prop:ep-exact-trace-surj}
Across any tower prefix, each nonempty trace of an original exact
domain is current exact, and each current exact domain is the trace
of an original exact domain. Equation~\eqref{eq:ep-tp} remains valid
across arbitrary prefix sorts whenever both input traces are nonempty.
For a realised current sort \(p\), restriction
\[
 \rho_p:\operatorname{ExEq}(M)\longrightarrow
                  \operatorname{ExEq}(p),\qquad
 H\longmapsto H|_{p^2}
 \tag{E1}\label{eq:ep-rho}
\]
is a surjective lattice homomorphism.
\end{proposition}

declarations.title: Original bipartite pivot and maximal gate
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Original bipartite pivot and maximal gate]
\label{lem:ep-old-gate}
If a current restriction \(c|_{p^2}\) is the odd pivot of a
genuine safe step, then the original atom \(c\) is bipartite.
Let \(Y_c<X_c\) be its original even-walk/connectivity interval,
and \(K_p\) the chosen current maximal exact gate. Then
\[
  Y_{\mathrm{current}}=Y_c|_{p^2},\quad
  O_{\mathrm{current}}=O_c|_{p^2},\quad
  X_{\mathrm{current}}=X_c|_{p^2},
 \tag{E4}\label{eq:ep-parity-trace}
\]
and \(L_p(K_p)\) is an \emph{original maximal exact complement}
to \(Y_c<X_c\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Finite type supports and exact meets
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite type supports and exact meets]
\label{lem:ep-phi-support}
Every \(\Phi_j\) preserves union, converse, identity
and represented relational composition. Its restriction to
original exact equivalences also preserves finite meets.
For every original invariant equivalence \(E\),
\(\Phi_j(E)\) is an equivalence on \(T_j\).
An actual \(E\)-class meeting type \(p\) meets
\emph{exactly every} type in the \(\Phi_j(E)\)-class of \(p\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: One original gate per connected step
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[One original gate per connected step]
\label{lem:ep-single-old-gate}
For a fixed connected full rigid-groupoid character step,
the canonical largest old lifts \(L_p(K_p)\) of the
active current gates \(K_p\) are \emph{equal} for all
active sorts \(p\). Write their common value \(G\).
Every current full exact bridge in that component is a
nonempty trace of an original full exact \(G\)-quotient
functional correspondence; conversely any such original
correspondence with nonempty trace is a current full bridge.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: The common exact kernel of the labels
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[The common exact kernel of the labels]
\label{prop:ep-common-kernel}
Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) be the original gates given by
\cref{lem:ep-single-old-gate}, with repetitions allowed.
Put \(K_{\rm com}=\bigcap_{i=1}^mG_i\) (or \(\Top\)
if \(m=0\)). This is the largest original full exact
equivalence all of whose classes lie in single final
unary type classes. In particular,
\[
  \Phi_m(K_{\rm com})=\Id_T,
  \qquad \bigcap_{i=1}^m\Phi_m(G_i)=\Id_T.
 \tag{E6}\label{eq:ep-common-kernel}
\]
\end{proposition}

declarations.title: Exact quotient commutation for safe towers
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Exact quotient commutation for safe towers]
\label{thm:ep-quotient-tower}
Let \(E\) be an original full exact equivalence.
Equip \(M/E\) with its actual saturated original quotient
binary orbitals. At prefix \(j\), label an \(E\)-class
by the \(\Phi_j(E)\)-class of the types which occur in it.
These labels form \(T_j/\Phi_j(E)\).
Up to renaming labels, the resulting sequence is itself a
genuine safe maximal-character tower after removing exactly
the steps \(i\) for which \(E\not\le G_i\). A kept step has
canonical old gate \(G_i/E\), after a prescribed
objectwise phase correction. The quotient tower has the
\emph{full} admissible character age, not merely a selected
orbit of markings. If the original tower is terminal,
the quotient tower is terminal.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Rank, notation and false shortcuts
declarations.heading: Exact trace geometry of safe unary towers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Rank, notation and false shortcuts]
\label{rem:ep-trace-audit}
If \(E>\Id\), the original quotient \(M/E\) has strictly
fewer original diversity orbitals: each quotient
orbital is the image of an old atom, and the diagonal
absorbs some nonidentity old orbital. This is the
strict induction parameter below. An arbitrary
quotient of a Ramsey/EP expansion does \emph{not}
inherit EP automatically; the full-age conclusion
of \cref{thm:ep-quotient-tower} is the needed substitute.
Trace products require \emph{both input traces
nonempty}; \(\Phi\) preserves only nonempty old
exact meets, not empty atomic meets.  Quotient
identities pull back to the whole gate, not raw
logical equality. The present theorem does not
assume that every old \(G_i\)-class meets every
current sort.
\end{remark}

\label{lem:ep-original-functional}
Let \(\mathscr H\) be the group of all
\(\operatorname{Aut}(M)\)-equivariant permutations
of the underlying original transitive set \(M\).
It is a finite elementary abelian \(2\)-group.
For nonidentity \(h\in\mathscr H\), its graph is
one original bipartite atomic relation. Each
\(h\) acts as a permutation on \emph{every}
prefix-type set \(T_j\); a nonidentity \(h\)
acts freely on \(T\).

Let \(E>\Id\) be original full exact, and let

declarations.title: Automatic complete separation and core
declarations.heading: Automatic core of the genuine terminal phase labels
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Automatic complete separation and core]
\label{thm:ep-automatic-core}
For every genuinely generated terminal tower
\eqref{eq:ep-tower} over the original one-sort
symmetric AP+homomorphic-CCO source, one has
\[
 \boxed{\quad s\ne t\ \Longrightarrow\
    \exists a\in\mathrm{BP}\ 
       (s,t)\in R_a .\quad}
 \tag{C2}\label{eq:ep-bp-separation}
\]
Consequently the graph of terminal types joined
by a common globally loopless old atom is
\emph{complete} and every endomorphism of
\(\mathbf T\) is an automorphism. In particular,
\(\mathbf T\) is a \emph{core}.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Proof boundaries and negative control
declarations.heading: Automatic core of the genuine terminal phase labels
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Proof boundaries and negative control]
\label{rem:ep-core-scope}
This theorem is stronger than core-ness alone;
it gives an original-bipartite-atom separator
for \emph{every pair} of terminal labels.
No intermediate step invokes Ramsey,
expansion property or an existing core theorem,
and the induction is on original
\emph{diversity rank}, not on tower length.

It is false if maximality of the chosen exact
complements is omitted, even while reachable
parity, full character transport, homogeneity,
SAP and CCO are retained. The explicit
four-atom source \(I\times\mathbb F_2\times\mathbb N\)
from the EP18 proof record has a safe first
parity orientation using the \emph{nonmaximal}
clone gate, followed by a maximal split;
its four-label table has the proper retraction
\((\lambda,\mu)\mapsto(\mu,\mu)\).
Choosing the actual first maximal gate
instead gives two terminal labels and a core.

Neither this theorem nor the shorter terminal
diagonal-palette lemma identifies a unique
preferred safe tower, proves a least vocabulary,
or extends without work to several \emph{original}
unary sorts. The source-level exact/quotient/phase
inputs require independent review before
formal verification or publication.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Simultaneous-singleton core criterion
declarations.heading: The explicit unfiltered Ramsey expansion has expansion property
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous-singleton core criterion]
\label{thm:ep-finite-core-criterion}
Let \(\mathcal K\) be a hereditary finite complete
atomic binary age (allowing original named unary sorts).
Let \(\mathcal U_T\) be a reasonable, reduct-surjective,
pair-locally specified finite unary expansion with
a finite set \(T\) of realised complete unary labels:
\[
 (A,\lambda)\in\mathcal U_T
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 A\in\mathcal K,\quad
 \col_A(x,y)=a\ \Longrightarrow\
         (\lambda(x),\lambda(y))\in R_a
 \quad(x\ne y).
 \tag{U1}\label{eq:ep-pair-local}
\]
Here every pair type is realised, the old atom
names and original sort predicates are retained,
and each \(R_a\subseteq T^2\) may overlap another.
Suppose \(\mathcal U_T\) has a reasonable hereditary
Ramsey expansion \(\mathcal R\) with JEP in which
there is exactly \emph{one expanded singleton type}
per label \(t\in T\). Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \operatorname{EP}(\mathcal U_T/\mathcal K)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \operatorname{End}(\mathbf T)
          =\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf T).
 \quad}
 \tag{U2}\label{eq:ep-core-iff}
\]
No new unary label is individually named inside
the \emph{finite template} \(\mathbf T\); otherwise
the endomorphism test would be vacuous.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Finite normalisation as an independent fallback
declarations.heading: The explicit unfiltered Ramsey expansion has expansion property
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Finite normalisation as an independent fallback]
\label{rem:ep-core-filter}
For an \emph{arbitrary} pair-local expansion,
the image of a minimum-rank idempotent
endomorphism of \(\mathbf T\) is an induced
core. Restricting to its labels preserves
reasonableness, reduct-surjectivity and a
relational Ramsey provider, and yields EP
by \cref{thm:ep-finite-core-criterion}.
This is a general finite algorithm, not
part of our main V27 recipe. Its necessity
on the legitimate V27 family is ruled out
by \cref{thm:ep-automatic-core}. An
arbitrarily added free terminal unary
partition, or the nonmaximal safe
orientation in \cref{rem:ep-core-scope},
can have a noncore type table.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Symmetry of equivariant coordinates
declarations.heading: The explicit unfiltered Ramsey expansion has expansion property
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of equivariant coordinates]
\label{lem:ep-unique-coordinate}
Let \(G\) act transitively on \(S\) and assume
all \(G\)-invariant binary relations on \(S\)
are symmetric. If \(\tau,\sigma:S\to B\)
are equivariant surjections onto the same
transitive \(G\)-set \(B\), then
\[
 \ker\tau=\ker\sigma,\qquad
 \sigma=f\circ\tau
\]
for an equivariant involution \(f:B\to B\).
If \(S\) has no proper finite-relative-index
invariant equivalence above \(\ker\tau\),
then \(f=\Id\) and \(\sigma=\tau\).
\end{lemma}

\label{lem:ep-reset-complete-edge}

terminal meet-irreducible cuts, let

$J$-semantic type, and suppose all

\emph{full transition-enriched hidden
language}; it would not follow from the
bare equivalence reduct or merely from
the RAW equality-inclusive identity
\(\mathfrak m;\mathfrak m=J^+\) from
\cref{eq:typed-relative-reset-raw} without completeness
of the named semantic type.

\begin{theorem}[Synchronized terminal subquotient-order EP]
\label{thm:ep-terminal-orders}
Let \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{imag}}\) be the
functionally closed PURE-IMAGINARY hidden
age obtained from the terminal V27 hidden
envelope by retaining all proper represented
quotient sorts, their unary upward maps,
quotient transitions and COMPLETE named
fine semantic cylinders, but forgetting
the clone-real hidden sorts. On this age
consider the explicit order expansion:
for each represented meet-irreducible cut
\(J<J^+\), order \(J\)-classes inside
each \(J^+\)-class; transport each order
along its definable quotient-transition
orbit, choose one independent task per
orbit, and use a fixed hidden-sort priority
and functorial parent-coordinate
lexicographic reconstruction for all
remaining comparisons.

This is a reasonable, precompact Ramsey
order expansion with EP over the
\emph{full fine-coloured} pure-imaginary
hidden age \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{imag}}\),
relative to the proved V27 typed hidden
Ramsey/SAP/reset source. It does NOT
claim relative EP for arbitrary orders
on deleted clone-real hidden vertices;
these orders are not part of the R18
MI/MR tuple readout.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Cofinal finite MI-tuple EP transfer
declarations.heading: The explicit unfiltered Ramsey expansion has expansion property
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Cofinal finite MI-tuple EP transfer]
\label{lem:ep-tuple-transfer}
Let \(\mathcal H^o\to\mathcal H\) be a reasonable
hidden finite-relational/unary-functional
precompact expansion with EP.
Suppose an interpretation \(N(D)\)
reads visible roots as finite compatible
tuples of selected unary hidden
quotient coordinates, and \(h(A)\)
is their finite unary-generated support.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textup{\roman*}),leftmargin=*]
\item the unexpanded \(h(A)\) depends only
on the old fine-coloured visible \(A\);
\item every finite hidden \(D\) extends
to a finite \(E\) with \(h(N(E))=E\);
\item \emph{every} allowed visible
expansion of \(N(E)\) lifts through
its full comparison/equality code
to a hidden \(\mathcal H^o\)
expansion of the \emph{same} \(E\);
\item visible embeddings extend uniquely
to generated supports, and \(N\)
recovers every original fine colour.
\end{enumerate}
Then the visible expansion has EP.
The full R18 compatible MI-tuple
readout of Part~III satisfies these
four contracts, including the MR case.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Explicit Ramsey and expansion-property theorem
declarations.heading: The explicit unfiltered Ramsey expansion has expansion property
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Explicit Ramsey and expansion-property theorem]
\label{thm:ep-unfiltered-main}
For every one-original-sort countable transitive
homogeneous complete finite symmetric binary
AP+homomorphic-CCO source, the following
\emph{unfiltered} finite unary/binary
expansion is reasonable, reduct-surjective,
precompact and Ramsey, and has the
\emph{expansion property} over the
original age:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textup{\arabic*}),leftmargin=*]
\item pass to the pure-clone SAP cover and
perform any \emph{genuine} finite
maximal-exact-character safe terminalisation;
retain \emph{every} realised joint
terminal unary type, removing \emph{none};
\item on terminal hidden MI quotients
use transition-synchronised
subquotient orders, fixed sort-block
priorities and parent-lex reconstruction;
\item read them back on the
original vertices as compatible
MI-coordinate tuples with the
finite \emph{full} unary/binary
term-equality, cylinder and
comparison code.
\end{enumerate}
No canonical choice of tower or
minimality of the signature is claimed.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: SIR in the no-finite-cover-index SAP case
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[SIR in the no-finite-cover-index SAP case]
\label{thm:sir-no-finite-cover}
Let \(M\) be a countable transitive homogeneous structure in a
finite complete atomic symmetric binary language. Suppose
\(\Age(M)\) has strong amalgamation (SAP) and semantic
homomorphic simple-cycle CCO. Assume that for every pair
\(E<F\) of \(\Aut(M)\)-invariant equivalence relations,
the relative index
\[
       [F:E]=\#\{E\text{-classes contained in one }F\text{-class}\}
\]
is infinite. Then \(M\) admits an \(\Aut(M)\)-invariant
\emph{stationary independence relation on all finite real sets},
including independence over the empty base.

In fact, the same conclusion holds for a finite-sorted,
named-sort homogeneous symmetric SAP+CCO structure as soon as
every named sort satisfies \emph{(NR2)}: no proper invariant
equivalence interval of relative index two. The independence
is given explicitly by the selected strong exact base-path
domains in \eqref{eq:sir-base-domain}--\eqref{eq:sir-independence}.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers

declarations.title: Precise boundary of the result
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Precise boundary of the result]
\label{rem:sir-positive-boundary}
The hypothesis is a prohibition of \emph{finite relative
indices between any two distinct invariant equivalences};
it is not just the absence of a finite \emph{global}
quotient. We assume SAP of the actual age on the
\emph{real} vertices; AP and CCO alone do not imply SAP,
even without finite relative indices. In the stronger
named-sorted version, only (NR2) is needed and it
is checked inside \emph{each named sort}, while the
language keeps those unary sort names. The theorem
does not assert a SIR on an unlabelled reduct obtained
by forgetting the sort names or on a general AP-only
exact quotient. Nor does it use the Ramsey, expansion
property or EPPA conclusions of the manuscript.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: The strong free-span domain network is PC
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[The strong free-span domain network is PC]
\label{lem:sir-free-span-PC}
Every \(D_C(a,b)\) is a nonempty member of the
original strong exact family
\(\mathcal H_{\operatorname{sort}(a),\operatorname{sort}(b)}\).
Put singleton literal domains on all pairs
inside \(A\) or \(B\), and \(D_C(a,b)\)
on the cross pairs. Every triple of
\emph{distinct} vertices of \(A\cup B\)
satisfies all three typed PC inclusions
\eqref{eq:typed-PC}. In particular, this
claim also holds for the empty base.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers

declarations.title: Canonical strong independent amalgam
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Canonical strong independent amalgam]
\label{prop:sir-HS-amalgam}
There is one finite complete amalgam
\(A\otimes_C^h B\) on the literal
disjoint union over \(C\), agreeing
with the two input structures and
assigning
\[
          \col(a,b)=h(D_C(a,b))
       \quad(a\in A\setminus C,\ b\in B\setminus C).
 \tag{SIR-A}\label{eq:sir-HS-amalgam}
\]
It lies in \(\Age(U)\).
It depends only on the two
complete finite structures and
their \emph{named} common base
\(C\), is natural under embeddings
of the ENTIRE SPAN that preserve
that specified common base as
the exact intersection of the
two factors, commutes with
converse symmetry, and uses
no linear ordering of vertices.
We do NOT claim that enlarging
the base from \(C\) to
\(C'\supsetneq C\) leaves the
selected cross colour unchanged:
the exact base-path menu can
shrink. Its behaviour under
base enlargement is precisely
the survivor-heredity calculation
in the transitivity proof below.
\end{proposition}

proofs.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers

declarations.title: The hereditary selected amalgam is stationary
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[The hereditary selected amalgam is stationary]
\label{thm:sir-HS-positive}
Under the hypotheses of
\cref{thm:typed-HS}, the relation
\(\downarrow^h\) from
\eqref{eq:sir-independence} is an
\emph{Aut-invariant stationary independence
relation on finite real vertex sets}.
It satisfies symmetry, existence,
monotonicity, both directions of
transitivity, and stationarity.
Consequently every finite-sorted
symmetric complete atomic SAP+
homomorphic-CCO class with no proper
finite-relative-index invariant
equivalence cover admits a SIR.
In particular, any named terminal SAP source
constructed in Part~III with homomorphic CCO
and (NR2) in each of its actual named sorts
satisfies this theorem. This is conditional
on the terminal \emph{age itself} having SAP;
neither terminality nor reasonable unary
expansion alone is being used to infer SAP.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers

declarations.title: Why SAP cannot be deleted from this argument
declarations.heading: Stationary independence with no finite relative equivalence covers
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Why SAP cannot be deleted from this argument]
\label{rem:sir-HS-AP-firewall}
The positive theorem applies to
the \emph{SAP} no-finite-cover
source, not automatically to
the original AP-only
class from Part~IV. A homogeneous
symmetric binary homomorphic-CCO
source can have \emph{no}
finite-relative-index invariant
equivalence cover and nevertheless
fail SAP.

Indeed let \(M=I\times J\) for
infinite pure sets \(I,J\).
Name exactly the three symmetric
diversity colours: same \(I\)
coordinate, same \(J\) coordinate,
and different in both.
This source is homogeneous,
with invariant equivalence lattice
\(\{\Id,E_I,E_J,\Top\}\);
all proper cover indices are
infinite. Homomorphic CCO holds:
an inconsistency in the row
coordinate is precisely a
specified row-disequality edge
closing a path of forced row
equalities; likewise for columns.
Such a contradictory path
plus edge is a noncompletable
specified simple cycle.
If no such contradiction occurs,
choose independent new row
values for row-equality components
and column values for
column-equality components,
giving a homomorphic completion.
But SAP fails: over two
opposite corners
\((i_0,j_0),(i_1,j_1)\)
with both coordinates different,
the cell \((i_0,j_1)\)
is the \emph{unique} point
simultaneously in the first
row and second column.
Two copies of that one-point
extension cannot remain disjoint
in any amalgam over the
two original corners.

The selector theorem
\cref{thm:typed-HS} uses
\emph{strong} products and
strong exact domains in an
SAP language. One cannot
replace them by equality-inclusive
AP products or infer SIR
on the original grid merely
from \eqref{eq:sir-HS-amalgam}.
A separate closure-aware
or compatible-imaginary
interpretation is required
for the general AP-only
case. No negative SIR claim
about this grid is being made.
\end{remark}

declarations.heading: Stationary independence: finite quotient obstructions and a relative control
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[A global two-class obstruction]
\label{lem:sir-global-two}
If a homogeneous one-sorted symmetric binary
structure \(M\) has a \(0\)-definable
equivalence \(E\) with exactly two classes,
then no SIR on the original real language
satisfies existence and stationarity
over the empty base.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Stationary independence: finite quotient obstructions and a relative control
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite relative Hasse index two]
\label{lem:sir-Hasse-two}
In a transitive homogeneous symmetric binary source with
semantic homomorphic CCO, every finite-index cover
$E\prec F$ in the \emph{full} invariant-equivalence lattice
has relative index two; hence all finite relative indices
are powers of two.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Stationary independence: finite quotient obstructions and a relative control
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite global quotients obstruct original one-sorted SIR]
\label{thm:sir-finite-global-no}
Let \(M\) be one-sorted, transitive,
homogeneous, complete finite named
symmetric binary with homomorphic semantic
CCO. If some proper invariant equivalence
\(E<\Top\) has finite global index
\([\Top:E]\), then \(M\) has \emph{no}
SIR on its original real one-sort language
with existence/stationarity over
the empty base.
\end{theorem}

\label{prop:sir-relative-positive}
There is a homogeneous one-sort finite

structure with invariant \(E<F\),
\([F:E]=2\), and infinite \(E\)-classes,

declarations.title: SIR status and nonclaims
declarations.heading: Stationary independence: finite quotient obstructions and a relative control
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[SIR status and nonclaims]
\label{rem:sir-status}
\cref{thm:sir-finite-global-no}
is a general \emph{negative} result
on the original real language,
not a positive SIR classification.
The positive relative-two-sheet
example shows finite \emph{relative}
index is not by itself an obstruction.
A finite global quotient can be
oriented by unary marks; the
resulting expansion may have an SIR
even though the original reduct
provably has none.
The historical primitive Q8 control
has prioritized independence without
genuine shortest-path POCS, so one
must never promote POCS to a necessary
CCO or SIR hypothesis.

The general claim that every
terminal symmetric CCO age has SIR
is \emph{not} proved here.
A plausible positive route is a
hereditary support-consistent
exact-domain selector with correctly
controlled algebraic closure, but
its stationary/transitivity
verification remains a separate
mathematical obligation.
Neither Ramsey+EP nor ordinary
EPPA implies an SIR automatically.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Pure-clone SAPification, A108
declarations.heading: Pure-clone SAPification of an AP source
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Pure-clone SAPification, A108]\label{thm:internal-clone-sap}
Let $Q$ be countable and homogeneous in a finite complete symmetric binary
language, with AP, triangle-definedness and semantic homomorphic CCO.
On $\widehat Q=Q\times\mathbb N$ define a new diversity atom $c$
between distinct clones of one old point, retaining old $Q$ colours between
distinct first coordinates. Then $\widehat Q$ is homogeneous,
triangle-defined, has SAP and semantic homomorphic CCO, and the clone
equivalence $K=\mathrm{Id}\cup c=c^2$ is exact with quotient $Q$.
The same holds in finitely many original unary sorts, with one clone atom
per sort.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: General hypotheses
declarations.heading: Standing assumptions and exact quotient notation
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{assumption}[General hypotheses]\label{ass:general}
Throughout the binary core of the paper, unless a stronger assumption is
explicitly invoked, we assume the following.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(A\arabic*)]
\item \label{A:finite} The typed atomic language is finite and complete, with paired converses
      between different named sorts and symmetric atoms on each same-sort
      palette; $\K$ is triangle constrained.
\item \label{A:sap} $\K$ has the strong amalgamation property.
\item \label{A:cco} $\K$ has semantic cycle constrainedness
      $\mathrm{CCO}_{\mathrm{sem}}$: a finite atomic partial structure is
      completable precisely when each of its specified simple cycles is
      completable.  Equivalently, in the profile formulation developed in
      \cref{sec:profiles}, the finite family of reachable path profiles is
      $2$-Helly.
\end{enumerate}
\end{assumption}

declarations.title: All definable equivalences and their joins
declarations.heading: The palette--lattice interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[All definable equivalences and their joins]
\label{prop:lattice-interface}
Every \(0\)-definable equivalence relation on \(M\) is uniquely of the form
\(E_X\) for some \(X\in\Lambda\).  The set \(\Lambda\) is a finite lattice,
ordered by inclusion, with
\[
 X\meet Y=X\cap Y,
 \qquad
 E_{X\join Y}=E_X\circ E_Y=E_Y\circ E_X.
 \tag{JC}\label{eq:join-composition}
\]
\end{proposition}

proofs.heading: The palette--lattice interface

declarations.title: Orbital parity
declarations.heading: Orbital parity and index two
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Orbital parity]\label{thm:orbital-parity}
Let $E<F$ be $0$-definable equivalences on one current
transitive unary sort and suppose $[F:E]=n<\infty$.
If $t\subseteq F\setminus E$ is a canonical diversity
pair orbit, then there are actual invariant equivalences
\[
 Y_t<E_t\leq F,\qquad [E_t:Y_t]=2,
\]
where $Y_t$ is the FULL RAW exact even-walk equivalence
(including real equality) and
$O_t=E_t\setminus Y_t$ is the odd-walk relation.
In the present SAP source, $Y_t>\Id$; moreover its
\emph{diversity part} $Y_t^\circ=Y_t\setminus\Id$
and $O_t$ are nonempty STRONG reachable profiles.

The distinction between the RAW equivalence $Y_t$
and its identity-free STRONG profile $Y_t^\circ$
is essential: no logical equality is inserted as
an artificial diversity edge.
\end{theorem}

proofs.heading: Orbital parity and index two

declarations.title: Finite covers have index two
declarations.heading: Orbital parity and index two
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite covers have index two]
\label{thm:finite-cover-two}
Let $E_X\prec E_Y$ be a cover in the lattice $\Lambda$ of
\cref{prop:lattice-interface}. If $[Y:X]$ is finite, then
$[Y:X]=2$. Hence any finite relative index between such
invariant equivalences is a power of two.
\end{theorem}

definable cover $K<X$, $[X:K]=2$, such that every unary orientation of the two
$K$-classes inside each $X$-class destroys AP.  The same structure has two
finer orbital coordinate covers which can be split successively.

declarations.title: Typed strong exact saturation commutes with nonempty meets
declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed strong exact saturation commutes with nonempty meets]
\label{lem:exact-saturation-intersection}
Let $K_a\in\mathcal H_{aa}$ and $K_b\in\mathcal H_{bb}$
be nonempty strong exact equivalence palettes in the
current SAP+homomorphic-CCO pair-shadow calculus.
If the nonempty strong exact menus
$D_i\subseteq\mathcal T^{ab}$ have a
\emph{nonempty} common exact intersection
$D=\bigcap_iD_i$, then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \bigcap_i(K_a\starprod D_i\starprod K_b)
     =K_a\starprod D\starprod K_b .
 \quad}
\]
Every product is the supported STRONG diversity product
of distinct-vertex legal triangles. This is a separate
application of the strong exact calculus, not the
equality-inclusive raw identity
\cref{lem:full-typed-exact-saturation}.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow

\begin{theorem}[Exact closure separation]
\label{thm:closure-separation}
Let $A,B$ be nonempty full exact same-sort domains in the
\emph{represented typed pair shadow}, both containing its identity
cell $e$. If $A\cap B=\{e\}$, then
\[
 \langle A\rangle\cap\langle B\rangle=\{e\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Rigid bridge groupoid
declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Rigid bridge groupoid]
\label{prop:rigid-bridge-groupoid}
Starting from $(a_*,K_*)$ and closing under full exact
bridges gives one finite connected component of current sorts.
For each reached sort $b$ its exact kernel $K_b$ is
path-independent. The quotient-functional $K_a,K_b$-bisaturated
full exact correspondences form the hom-set
$\mathcal H(a,b)$ of a connected groupoid with finite
elementary abelian $2$-group isotropy; every nonempty hom-set
is a torsor. In addition, for any bridge $R:a_*\to b$,
\[
             t_b=R^\smile t_*R
\]
is a path-independent nonidentity involution in the
$K_b$-semantic quotient, and every nonidentity exact
equivalence on that quotient contains $t_b$.
\end{proposition}

declarations.title: Groupoid phase labelling
declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Groupoid phase labelling]
\label{prop:groupoid-phase}
The character $\chi$ is a functor to $\mathbb F_2$,
with $\chi(t_b)=1$ for every reached sort $b$.
The quotient points admit global binary labels
satisfying
\[
 \lambda(Rq)=\lambda(q)+\chi(R).
 \tag{7}\label{eq:quotient-phase}
\]
A raw orbital whose $K_a,K_b$-semantic cylinder is
rigid has exactly its forced character phase; a
nonrigid cylinder admits both phase differences.
All finite old structures admit such phase
markings, hence the unary phase expansion is
reduct-surjective.
\end{proposition}

declarations.title: Rigid-product factorisation
declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Rigid-product factorisation]
\label{lem:rigid-product-factorisation}
Let $A\subseteq\mathcal T^{ab}$ and
$B\subseteq\mathcal T^{bc}$ be nonempty
reachable \emph{represented} profiles.
If $AB\subseteq R$ for one rigid arrow
$R\in\mathcal H(a,c)$, then $b$ is in the
same rigid component and there are arrows
$R_1\in\mathcal H(a,b)$,
$R_2\in\mathcal H(b,c)$ with
\[
 A\subseteq R_1,\qquad B\subseteq R_2,
                  \qquad R_1R_2=R.
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow

\begin{lemma}[Phase-primality sufficiency]
\label{lem:phase-primality-sufficiency}
Assume a finite typed unary phase sector is reduct-surjective, has total lifted
atomic products, and satisfies \cref{thm:typed-epp}.  If a lifted path has old
endpoint profile $P$ and total endpoint phase difference $\varepsilon$, then
its endpoint profile is exactly
\[
 P\cap A_{ab}^{\varepsilon}.
\tag{9}\label{eq:lifted-profile-normal-form}
\]
Consequently the lifted product is associative, its reachable profiles are
typed $2$-Helly, and the unary expansion has SAP and semantic CCO.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Safe exact-complement split
declarations.heading: Exact-complement pivot in a typed pair shadow
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Safe exact-complement split]
\label{thm:safe-exact-split}
Suppose a current unary sort of a finite-sorted symmetric SAP+CCO pair-shadow
has a proper finite relative index.  Then there is a finite precompact unary
expansion which is reduct-surjective, preserves SAP and CCO, and orients an
index-two orbital parity layer.  The split is chosen from a maximal exact
complement; it need not orient a preassigned finite cover.
\end{theorem}

declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite-cover elimination]
\label{thm:finite-cover-elimination}
Starting from a class satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:general}, finitely many
applications of \cref{thm:safe-exact-split} produce a finite precompact unary
expansion $\K^{\mathrm{term}}$ which has SAP and CCO and in which every proper
same-sort cover of definable equivalences has infinite relative index.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Root-free phase-safe detours
declarations.heading: Finite termination and the typed terminal interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Root-free phase-safe detours]
\label{lem:root-free-phase-safe}
Fix one safe split and let $c\in\mathcal T^{ab}$ be an old canonical pair
type together with an allowed endpoint phase difference $\varepsilon$.
There is a finite path gadget $W(c,\varepsilon)$ between two distinct roots
$x,y$ of sorts $a,b$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the root pair $xy$ itself is left unspecified and every internal vertex
      is private;
\item every consecutive edge carries a realised complete canonical
      two-point type with phase-compatible endpoint bits, and the gadget
      carries no relation tuple of support at least three;
\item if $P(c)$ is the old endpoint profile of the path, then
      $c\in P(c)$ and every member of $P(c)$ is compatible with the prescribed
      endpoint phases.
\end{enumerate}
If both endpoint sorts lie in the active rigid component, one may choose a
three-edge detour and, with
$C(c)=K_a\starprod\{c\}\starprod K_b$, arrange
\[
        c\in P(c)\subseteq C(c).
\]
No assertion that $C(c)$ itself is reachable or exact is made.
\end{lemma}
