declarations.title: Full-language finite-cover elimination
declarations.heading: Finite termination and the typed terminal interface
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Full-language finite-cover elimination]
\label{thm:full-language-elimination}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a homogeneous class in a finite relational language.
Pass to the finite quantifier-free definitional expansion naming all realised
unary and canonical pair types.  Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item all canonical pair types are symmetric;
\item the canonical pair shadow has SAP and semantic CCO;
\item complete old substructures are irreducible in the working expansion,
      and higher-support relations are \emph{support-normal} in the following
      explicit sense.  Whenever all specified support-$\ge3$ tuples of a
      finite partial canonical structure lie in finitely many distinguished
      complete old substructures and its canonical pair shadow admits a
      cycle-constrained completion fixing every pair inside those factors,
      the full partial structure admits a completion in $\mathcal C$ fixing
      each distinguished factor pointwise as an induced structure.  For the
      coherent-EPPA conclusion we moreover assume the automorphism-preserving
      form of this interface: an isomorphism-natural pair-shadow completion
      can be lifted while preserving every automorphism of the partial full
      structure which preserves the distinguished factors.
\end{enumerate}
Then the iterated exact-complement construction lifts to the full finite
language.  It yields a finite precompact unary expansion
$\mathcal C^{\mathrm{term}}$ whose reduct is $\mathcal C$, whose age has SAP,
and whose pair shadow is semantic CCO with all proper same-sort covers of
infinite relative index.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: RAW saturation versus STRONG diversity equivalence factors
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[RAW saturation versus STRONG diversity equivalence factors]
\label{lem:typed-raw-strong-saturation}
Let $M$ be a homogeneous complete binary structure with individually
transitive named sorts, symmetric same-sort atomic relations and SAP.
No CCO or terminality hypothesis is needed for this lemma.
Let \(J,K\) be NONZERO actual
invariant same-sort equivalences on
named sorts \(a,b\), and put
\(J^\circ=J\setminus\Id_a\),
\(K^\circ=K\setminus\Id_b\).
For every actual old DIVERSITY
atomic relation \(t:a\to b\),
\[
       (J;\{t\};K)^\circ
        =J^\circ\starprod\{t\}
                          \starprod K^\circ.
\tag{TSC}\label{eq:typed-raw-strong-saturation}
\]
In addition, for two NONZERO actual
equivalences \(J,K\) on the SAME named
sort one has
\[
     (J;K)^\circ
           =J^\circ\starprod K^\circ
           =(J\vee K)^\circ.
\tag{TSC2}\label{eq:typed-equivalence-join-strong}
\]
This two-factor identity does NOT
introduce an artificial identity
as an intermediate STRONG atom.

With an identity equivalence at
either endpoint the corresponding
STRONG exterior factor is OMITTED.
Accordingly, in the following
transition-enriched typed subsection,
any nonzero equivalence \(J\) used
as a factor of \(\starprod\) means
its diversity palette \(J^\circ\);
in RAW inclusions and quotient
transport \(J\) continues to mean
the full relation including
logical identity. This is an
explicit notational coercion,
NOT an extra identity atom in
the STRONG product.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed exact-domain calculus
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed exact-domain calculus]
\label{lem:typed-exact-domain-calculus}
For every ordered pair of current unary sorts \(a,b\),
\[
 \Dat^{ab}
 =\left\{\bigcap\mathcal F:
   \mathcal F\subseteq\Rch^{ab}\text{ finite and }
   \bigcap\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\right\}.
\tag{TED}\label{eq:typed-exact-domains}
\]
Finite pairwise-intersecting families in one \(\Dat^{ab}\) have non-empty
total intersection.  Moreover, for any sort triple \(a,b,c\), a triple
\[
 D_{ab}\in\Dat^{ab},\qquad
 D_{bc}\in\Dat^{bc},\qquad
 D_{ca}\in\Dat^{ca}
\]
occurs simultaneously as the three fixed-point domains of one completable
typed triangle network if and only if it is support-consistent under the typed
Peircean products.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Original quotient first-hit cover interpolation
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Original quotient first-hit cover interpolation]
\label{lem:typed-original-full-cover-interpolation}
Let $M$ be a finite-complete homogeneous
binary source with a named transitive
original real sort $a$, finite symmetric
SAME-SORT fine atomic palette, original
visible SAP and semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO.
Let $\Id_a<J\prec K$ be an ACTUAL FULL
original invariant-equivalence cover,
with $J$ MEET-IRREDUCIBLE (so $K$
is its UNIQUE FULL cover).
Assume that both $J^\circ$ and $K^\circ$
are single positive STRONG OLD typed
word endpoint profiles; their private
word interiors may use arbitrary named
original sorts. Then for EVERY nonempty
positive STRONG typed $a$--$a$ word profile
$P$, we have
\[
 P\cap J^\circ\ne\varnothing,\qquad
 P\setminus J\ne\varnothing
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
                   P\cap(K\setminus J)\ne\varnothing.
\tag{OWI}\label{eq:typed-original-full-cover-interpolation}
\]
There is NO exact-domain product calculus,
Set-Pasch, lattice distributivity or hidden
SAP assumption in this original theorem.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed cover interpolation
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed cover interpolation]
\label{lem:typed-cover-interpolation}
Let \(J\) be a represented proper meet-irreducible on a real sort \(a\), let
\(K=J^+\) be its unique cover, and let \(P\in\Rch^{aa}\), where the path
realising \(P\) may pass through arbitrary intermediate sorts.  If
\[
 P\cap J\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 P\setminus J\ne\varnothing,
\]
then \(P\cap(K\setminus J)\ne\varnothing\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Original STRONG exact-domain MI-primality from one cover
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Original STRONG exact-domain MI-primality from one cover]
\label{lem:typed-original-strong-exact-prime}
In the setting of
\cref{lem:typed-original-full-cover-interpolation},
let $J>\Id_a$ be the FULL original
meet-irreducible with unique FULL
cover $K=J^+$, and let $D_1,D_2$
be NONEMPTY finite intersections
of genuinely positive OLD STRONG
typed $a$--$a$ word profiles.
(The empty intersection means
the full diversity palette and
is handled separately.) If
\[
     D_1\cap D_2\ne\varnothing,\qquad
     D_1\cap D_2\subseteq J^\circ,
\]
then
\[
                 D_1\subseteq J^\circ
                   \quad\text{or}\quad
                 D_2\subseteq J^\circ.
\tag{OWP}\label{eq:typed-original-strong-exact-prime}
\]
The proof uses only ORIGINAL
SAP+homomorphic CCO positive-word
2-Helly, the direct quotient
cover-layer positivity, and
the first-hit quotient
interpolation. It does NOT
assume a typed exact-domain
product formula, distributivity,
original Set-Pasch, or hidden SAP.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: No algebraic real quotient under SAP
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[No algebraic real quotient under SAP]
\label{lem:no-real-algebraic-transition}
Assume visible SAP.  Let \(R\in\Rel^{ab}\) and let \(E\) be a proper
NONIDENTITY definable equivalence on sort \(a\), so \(E>\Id_a\), with
\(RR^{\smile}\subseteq E\).  Then the transported equivalence \(E^R\) on
sort \(b\) is proper; in particular \(E^R\) is not equality.
Moreover, if \(R\in\Rel^{ab}\) satisfies
\(RR^{\smile}=1'_a\), then \(a=b\) and \(R=1'_a\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Identity-containing quotient transport is redundant
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Identity-containing quotient transport is redundant]
\label{lem:typed-identity-transport-redundant}
Let \(R\in\Rel^{aa}\) contain the ACTUAL
logical diagonal \(\Id_a\), and let
\(J\) be a represented proper same-sort
equivalence with \(R;R^\smile\subseteq J\).
Then
\[
 R\subseteq J,\qquad
 J^R=R^\smile;J;R=J,\qquad
 q_{R,J}=\operatorname{id}_{a/J}.
\tag{QT-Id}\label{eq:typed-identity-transport}
\]
Such an \(R\) gives no new unary
quotient-transition function. Its map
is the existing identity on
\(B_{a,J}\), without any artificial
STRONG identity-labelled edge.
This includes \(R=\Id_a\)
and any mixture of identity and
genuine diversity atoms.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Finite typed quotient-transition composition normal form
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite typed quotient-transition composition normal form]
\label{lem:typed-transition-composition-normal-form}
Let \(R\in\Rel^{ab}\),
\(S\in\Rel^{bc}\) be
nonempty ACTUAL typed
invariant relations.
Let \(E\) be a represented
proper equivalence on
sort \(a\), and assume
\[
 RR^\smile\subseteq E,\qquad
 F=E^R,\qquad
 SS^\smile\subseteq F .
\]
Put \(T=R;S\) as an
equality-inclusive RAW
represented relation.
Then
\[
 TT^\smile\subseteq E,\qquad
 E^T=F^S,\qquad
 q_{T,E}=q_{S,F}\circ q_{R,E}.
\tag{TQC}\label{eq:typed-transition-composition}
\]
For any represented
equivalence \(H\ge F\)
on \(b\), let
\(H_0=(q_{R,E})^{-1}(H)\)
be its unique pullback
in the interval
\([E,\Top_a]\). Then
\(H_0^R=H\) and
\[
 u_{F,H}\circ q_{R,E}
 =q_{R,H_0}\circ u_{E,H_0}.
\tag{TQU}\label{eq:typed-upward-interchange}
\]
If \(H\) is a represented
proper meet-irreducible,
so is \(H_0\). If
\(a=c\) and the ACTUAL
diagonal \(\Id_a\)
belongs to \(T\), then
the composite quotient
map in (TQC) is exactly
the IDENTITY on \(a/E\),
by \cref{lem:typed-identity-transport-redundant};
it introduces no synthetic
STRONG diversity identity
or additional named unary
transition.

Consequently every
transition-only unary
composite between
represented proper
quotient sorts equals
either one quotient
transition \(q_{T,E}\)
of an ACTUAL member of
one of the finitely many
families \(\Rel^{ac}\),
or the old unary identity.
After moving upward maps
leftwards by (TQU),
every unary coordinate
term has one initial
projection/upward map
and one such transition
(or identity). Hence
there are finitely many
unary term FUNCTIONS
from each hidden sort.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed cylinder realisation and partition
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed cylinder realisation and partition]
\label{lem:typed-cylinder-realisation}
Let \(J\in\overline{\mathcal I}_a\) and
\(K\in\overline{\mathcal I}_b\).  Let \(q\in a/J\) and \(r\in b/K\),
where an equality-coordinate class is identified with its unique real point.
Suppose distinct representatives \(x\in q\), \(y\in r\) have atomic pair type \(t\).
Then the set of all atomic pair types realised by choices of representatives
\(x'\in q\), \(y'\in r\) with \(x'\neq y'\) is exactly
\[
 \operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t).
\]
Consequently this cylinder depends only on the ordered pair \((q,r)\), not
on the chosen representatives.  For every compatible ordered pair of
represented coordinate positions, including a real-sort endpoint interpreted
as equality, the distinct cylinders therefore partition the ordered pairs of
\emph{distinct} corresponding vertices (with the diagonal omitted when the
two endpoint positions are the same hidden sort); when both endpoints are real
this is simply the old atomic pair-type partition off the diagonal.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Quotient-transition cylinders
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Quotient-transition cylinders]
\label{lem:typed-transition-cylinder}
Let \(J\in\mathcal I_a\), let \(R\in\Rel^{ab}\)
be nonempty and contain NO ACTUAL logical identity,
assume \(RR^{\smile}\subseteq J\), and put \(K=J^R\).
For every DIVERSITY atomic pair type
\(t\in R\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t)
   =J^\circ\starprod R\starprod K^\circ.
\tag{QT-Graph}\label{eq:typed-transition-cylinder}
\]
In particular the left-hand side is independent of \(t\).  If
\(q\in a/J\) and \(r\in b/K\), then
\[
 \pi_{R,J}(q)=r
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{the type of representatives of \((q,r)\) lies in
 \(J^\circ\starprod R\starprod K^\circ\)}.
\]
Thus the graph of every quotient-transition function is represented by one
reachable visible pair profile.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Atomic naming of a quotient-functional strong branch
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Atomic naming of a quotient-functional strong branch]
\label{lem:typed-branch-atomic-transport}
Let \(P\in\Rch^{ab}\) be a nonempty
IDENTITY-FREE positive typed strong
word profile, and let \(J\) be a
represented proper equivalence on
the source sort \(a\) with
\(P;P^\smile\subseteq J\).
Choose ANY old diversity
atomic type \(t\subseteq P\).
Then
\[
      J^t=J^P,\qquad
      \pi_{t,J}=\pi_{P,J}.
\tag{QT-Atom}\label{eq:typed-atomic-transport}
\]
In particular, when \(J\) is a
represented proper meet-irreducible,
the transported target kernel
\(J^P\) is also a represented proper
meet-irreducible under visible SAP,
and the quotient map induced by
the WHOLE strong branch \(P\) is
ALREADY a named unary quotient
transition of the finite hidden
language. The assertion does NOT
identify old fine atomic relations
\(P\) and \(t\); only their
induced quotient maps agree.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Commutation of same-sort invariant binary relations
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Commutation of same-sort invariant binary relations]
\label{lem:typed-symmetric-orbital-commutation}
Let \(a\) be one named original
transitive sort of a homogeneous
complete SYMMETRIC binary source.
For any two invariant (equivalently,
unions of old named atomic orbitals)
relations \(P,Q\subseteq M_a^2\),
their equality-inclusive RAW
relational products commute:
\[
                    P;Q=Q;P.
\]
No assertion is made here about
relations with different source
and target sorts.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Modularity of the original same-sort invariant equivalence lattice
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Modularity of the original same-sort invariant equivalence lattice]
\label{lem:typed-invariant-equivalence-modularity}
Let $a$ be a transitive original named real sort
of a homogeneous COMPLETE binary source, whose
same-sort ORIGINAL atomic orbitals are symmetric.
The FULL invariant-equivalence lattice on $a$
is MODULAR, without assuming SAP, CCO,
terminal NR2, RAW exactness, or distributivity.
Precisely, for original invariant equivalences
$E,F,G$ with $E\le G$,
\[
             (E\vee F)\cap G
                    =E\vee(F\cap G).
\tag{MOD}\label{eq:typed-invariant-modularity}
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: An original exact $M_3$ forces failure of homomorphic CCO
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[An original exact $M_3$ forces failure of homomorphic CCO]
\label{lem:typed-exact-m3-cco-obstruction}
Suppose a homogeneous COMPLETE binary
same-sort symmetric original source has
three invariant equivalences
$E_1,E_2,E_3$ generating an actual
sublattice $M_3$:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 E_i\cap E_j=L<E_i\quad(i\ne j),\\
 E_i\vee E_j=H\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad L<H .
 \end{gathered}
\]
Assume each $E_i$ is the ACTUAL represented
RAW endpoint relation of at least one
finite original atomic word, including
true equality on the diagonal.
Then the original source does NOT have
semantic HOMOMORPHIC simple-cycle CCO.
No SAP or NR2 is needed for this implication.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: A finite modular $M_3$ diagnostic for non-CCO
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[A finite modular $M_3$ diagnostic for non-CCO]
\label{cor:typed-terminal-nondistributive-noncco}
Let $M$ be a homogeneous finite-complete
binary symmetric-on-each-sort source with
NO relative-index-two interval in the FULL
invariant-equivalence lattice on one original
transitive sort $a$; visible SAP is NOT assumed.
If the FULL invariant-equivalence lattice
on $a$ is NONDISTRIBUTIVE, then the
original source does NOT have semantic
homomorphic simple-cycle CCO.
In fact three nonidentity original
invariant equivalences in an $M_3$
sublattice yield an explicit finite
bad partial atomic network built from
their ACTUAL RAW atomic word presentations.
No converse is claimed:
a DISTRIBUTIVE invariant lattice
alone does not imply CCO.
\end{corollary}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: CCO-free quotient-orbital power dichotomy at a full invariant cover
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[CCO-free quotient-orbital power dichotomy at a full invariant cover]
\label{lem:typed-quotient-full-cover-powers}
Let $M$ be a homogeneous finite-complete binary structure
with finitely many named transitive original real sorts,
symmetric old same-sort orbitals, and visible SAP.
Fix an original sort $a$ and let
$\Id_a<J\prec K$ be a cover in the FULL original
invariant-equivalence lattice, with $J>\Id_a$.
Let $T\subseteq K\setminus J$ be the full OLD diversity
preimage of ONE non-diagonal complete $\Aut(M)$-orbital
on $(M_a/J)^2$. Exactly one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $[K:J]=2$, and for EVERY $n\ge1$ the actual
STRONG diversity powers alternate:
$T^{\starprod n}=T$ for odd $n$ and
$T^{\starprod n}=J^\circ$ for even $n$;
\item $[K:J]\ne2$, and there is $N_T$ such that
\[
                   T^{\starprod n}=K^\circ
                   \quad\text{for every }n\ge N_T.
\tag{QPP}\label{eq:typed-quotient-full-cover-powers}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus local exclusion of THIS index-two cover suffices;
no global NR2 or semantic CCO, exact-ball Helly,
distributivity, RAW exactness, or mixed-sort
quotient transport is needed for (ii).
The FULL-cover condition is essential.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Typed relative pure powers at a nonzero exact cut
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed relative pure powers at a nonzero exact cut]
\label{lem:typed-relative-pure-power}
Work in an actual finite-named-sorted, homogeneous, symmetric
on each sort, SAP and semantic homomorphic-CCO
\emph{terminal} source. Fix one original named sort $a$,
a \emph{nonzero} represented proper meet-irreducible
full exact equivalence $J$ on $a$, and its unique
represented exact cover $K=J^+$. Let
$T\subseteq K\setminus J$ be one complete
$J$-semantic same-sort cylinder. Then for some
$N_T$, in the guarded STRONG typed diversity product,
\[
                         T^{\starprod n}=K^\circ
                   \qquad(n\ge N_T).
 \tag{TRP}\label{eq:typed-relative-pure-power}
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Specified-cycle control for the typed reset theta network
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Specified-cycle control for the typed reset theta network]
\label{lem:typed-relative-reset-cycle-guard}
Let \(a\) be one original named
transitive sort of a typed
symmetric-on-sorts SAP source.
Let \(K\) be a NONZERO actual
same-sort invariant equivalence,
and write \(K^\circ\) for its
STRONG diversity palette.
Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_r\) be
nonempty positive exact
same-sort STRONG menus
contained in \(K^\circ\).
Suppose
\[
 T_i^{\starprod n}=K^\circ
       \qquad(n\ge N)
\]
for every \(i\), and that
\(K^\circ,T_1,\ldots,T_r\)
have finite PRIVATE theta
presentations: each branch
is a positive typed atomic
word whose strong endpoint
spectrum CONTAINS the
specified menu.

Let \(H\) be a SIMPLE
graph with edges labelled
\(1,\ldots,r\), of girth
strictly greater than
\(r(N-1)+1\).
Introduce a new formal
same-sort centre \(o\).
Attach one private
\(K^\circ\)-theta gadget
from \(o\) to each graph
vertex, and one private
\(T_i\)-theta gadget along
each graph edge of label
\(i\). Give all gadgets
pairwise disjoint interiors.
Then EVERY specified
simple cycle of the
resulting typed PARTIAL
atomic diagram admits
a colour-preserving
HOMOMORPHISM to the
original source.

This is a cycle-by-cycle
claim, not the assertion
that one arbitrary
completion simultaneously
realises all root colours
or that a CCO homomorphism
is injective.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Original one-word-path relative reset at a full cover
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Original one-word-path relative reset at a full cover]
\label{thm:typed-original-full-cover-reset-single-path}
Let $M$ be a finite-complete, homogeneous,
symmetric-on-one-original-transitive-sort $a$
binary source with original visible SAP and
semantic HOMOMORPHIC simple-cycle CCO.
Let $\Id_a<J\prec K$ be a cover in the FULL
original invariant-equivalence lattice,
with $J>\Id_a$ and $[K:J]\ne2$.
Suppose the old diversity palettes
$J^\circ$ and $K^\circ$ EACH have one
genuinely positive original atomic WORD
with exactly that STRONG endpoint profile.
Then there is ONE COMPLETE non-diagonal
$J$-semantic same-sort quotient orbital
$\mathfrak m\subseteq K\setminus J$ with
\[
 \mathfrak m\starprod\mathfrak m=K^\circ,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak m;\mathfrak m=K
 \quad\text{(ACTUAL equality-inclusive RAW).}
 \tag{OWR}\label{eq:typed-original-full-cover-reset}
\]
The proof uses ONE private OLD positive word
per graph/spoke edge, NOT private exact theta
presentations, typed Helly, distributivity,
a mixed-sort quotient groupoid or a hidden
SAP assumption. It does use original CCO
for ONE global homomorphic completion.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Typed relative reset for one named-sort cut
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Typed relative reset for one named-sort cut]
\label{thm:typed-relative-reset}
Under the hypotheses of
\cref{lem:typed-relative-pure-power}, there is
ONE complete named same-sort $J$-semantic
type $\mathfrak m\subseteq K\setminus J$ with
\[
                 \boxed{\quad
      \mathfrak m\starprod\mathfrak m=K^\circ.\quad}
 \tag{TR}\label{eq:typed-relative-reset}
\]
Equivalently, for the equality-INCLUSIVE
RAW relational product we have
\[
       \mathfrak m;\mathfrak m=K.
 \tag{TR-RAW}\label{eq:typed-relative-reset-raw}
\]
Only the second equation contains
actual logical identity. Products
marked \(\starprod\) here are
\emph{strong typed diversity products},
and $J$ contains some actual diversity colour;
the statement does not extend to the bottom/equality
palette by a formal-unit convention.
Private theta witnesses may have intermediate vertices
in other original named sorts. Thus the result applies
to the terminal transition-enriched hidden construction,
not only to the historical one-original-sort appendix.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Nonzero typed equivalence reproduction
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Nonzero typed equivalence reproduction]
\label{lem:typed-equivalence-reproduction}
Let $E$ be the diversity palette of a nonzero invariant
same-sort equivalence relation in a finite-named-sorted
homogeneous symmetric SAP source. If $C\subseteq E$ is
a nonempty set of same-sort diversity atoms, then
\[
                   E\starprod C=E=C\starprod E,
              \qquad E\starprod E=E.
 \tag{TER}\label{eq:typed-equivalence-reproduction}
\]
The assertion is about STRONG off-diagonal products,
not about an equality-labelled edge.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed no-return into a same-sort equivalence
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed no-return into a same-sort equivalence]
\label{lem:typed-terminal-no-return}
In a finite named-sorted homogeneous symmetric
terminal SAP+CCO source, let $J$ be a nonzero
represented full exact same-sort equivalence
palette on a sort $a$. For any two nonempty
SAME-SORT STRONG reachable profiles
$P,Q\in\Rch^{aa}$,
\[
       P\starprod Q\subseteq J
          \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
       P\subseteq J,\quad Q\subseteq J.
 \tag{TNR}\label{eq:typed-no-return}
\]
The same conclusion holds for any finite positive
product contained in $J$. Internal path vertices
of $P,Q$ may belong to other named sorts.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Eventual typed powers of a same-sort profile
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Eventual typed powers of a same-sort profile]
\label{lem:typed-profile-pure-power}
Let $W\in\Rch^{aa}$ be a nonempty STRONG
same-sort diversity word profile in a
terminal typed SAP+CCO source, and let $F_W$
be the diversity palette of connectedness in
the undirected old invariant $W$-graph.
There exists $N_W$ such that
\[
                  W^{\starprod n}=F_W
                            \quad(n\ge N_W).
 \tag{TWP}\label{eq:typed-profile-pure-power}
\]
In particular, $F_W$ is a nonempty strong
reachable idempotent equivalence palette.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Exact two-edge return test for complete $J$-cylinders
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact two-edge return test for complete $J$-cylinders]
\label{lem:typed-complete-J-cylinder-return}
Let $J>\Id_a$ be an invariant equivalence on
one original named transitive REAL sort of a
homogeneous symmetric visible SAP source.
Let $T,S$ be TWO nonempty, J-BISATURATED,
COMPLETE semantic same-sort DIVERSITY
cylinders, each DISJOINT from $J$.
Then the following are equivalent:
\[
        (T\starprod S)\cap J^\circ
                \ne\varnothing
             \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T=S.
\tag{JRT}\label{eq:typed-complete-J-cylinder-return}
\]
No CCO, NR2, MI, exact-domain Helly
or reset theorem is needed for this
purely complete-orbital return test.
The COMPLETENESS of the two cylinders
is indispensable: it is not a claim
for arbitrary J-saturated unions.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Exact STRONG lifting of original quotient relation composition
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact STRONG lifting of original quotient relation composition]
\label{lem:typed-quotient-strong-semigroup}
Let $M$ be an original finite-complete homogeneous
binary source with a transitive named real sort $a$
and visible SAP. Let $J>\Id_a$ be an ACTUAL
invariant equivalence on that sort, and
$Q=M_a/J$. For EVERY $\Aut(M)$-invariant
quotient binary relation $R\subseteq Q^2$,
define the ORIGINAL diversity pullback
\[
 \Phi(R)=\{(x,y)\in M_a^2:x\ne y,\
             ([x]_J,[y]_J)\in R\}.
\]
Then for any nonempty invariant $R,S$,
\[
                 \Phi(R)\starprod\Phi(S)
                       =\Phi(R;S).
\tag{QS}\label{eq:typed-quotient-strong-semigroup}
\]
All OLD original $J$-classes are infinite by SAP.
Therefore $\Phi$ is injective on quotient relations,
preserves finite unions/intersections, and sends
every nonempty quotient relation to a nonempty
OLD DIVERSITY palette (also for the quotient
diagonal). The product equality is on DISTINCT
old real endpoints, even when the intermediate
QUOTIENT class equals one endpoint's quotient
class; no old logical identity is inserted
into the STRONG palette. Finite concatenations
satisfy the analogous identity by choosing
ALL formal intermediate OLD representatives
pairwise distinct.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Original positive external layer at every nonzero full cover
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Original positive external layer at every nonzero full cover]
\label{thm:typed-original-full-cover-layer-word}
Let $M$ be a finite-complete homogeneous
binary source with a transitive named
original real sort $a$, finitely many
symmetric SAME-SORT fine atomic orbitals,
original SAP, and semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO.
Let $\Id_a<J\prec K$ be a cover in the
FULL original invariant-equivalence lattice.
Suppose $J^\circ$ is the STRONG diversity
endpoint profile of ONE positive ORIGINAL
atomic word on $a$. Then
\[
               K\setminus J
       \quad\text{is the STRONG endpoint profile
                   of ONE positive old atomic word.}
\tag{OWL}\label{eq:typed-original-full-cover-layer-word}
\]
No FULL NR2, distributivity, original exact
theta presentation, typed exact-domain
Helly, or hidden SAP is assumed.
The index-two cover case is allowed.
\end{theorem}

declarations.title: Reachable typed relative cover layer
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Reachable typed relative cover layer]
\label{thm:typed-cover-layer-reachable}

hypotheses, let $J$ be a nonzero represented
proper meet-irreducible FULL EXACT same-sort

\[
                         U=K\setminus J
\]
is a nonempty reachable typed $a$--$a$
word profile (even when its witnessing
positive words visit other named sorts).

declarations.title: Unary-admissible partial hidden sources
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Unary-admissible partial hidden sources]
\label{def:typed-unary-admissible-source}
A finite unary-functionally CLOSED PARTIAL terminal hidden
structure \(C\) is \emph{unary-admissible} if, for EVERY
\(x\in C\), the FULL induced hidden diagram on
\(\cl_C\{x\}\), including all named total unary functions,
their literal term equalities and the binary relations
internal to this closure, is isomorphic to an ACTUAL
completed one-generated induced hidden member.
This does NOT assume \(C\) itself is complete or
homomorphism-embedding completable.

The condition is substantive. Arbitrary finite partial
structures with total unary symbols may have arbitrarily
large one-generated closures and violate the named
quotient-transition identities; mere unary closedness
does NOT imply unary-admissibility.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Arbitrarily long malformed unary transition cycles
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Arbitrarily long malformed unary transition cycles]
\label{ex:typed-malformed-unary-long-cycles}
The distinction in
\cref{def:typed-unary-admissible-source}
already occurs in the ACTUAL two-original-sort
common-block SAP+CCO structure
\cref{ex:typed-mixed-block-orbital-diagonal}.
Its proper quotient sorts $Q_A,Q_B$ carry the
NAMED inverse transitions
$f=\pi_{r,E_A}:Q_A\to Q_B$
and $g=\pi_{r^\smile,E_B}:Q_B\to Q_A$,
with $g f=\operatorname{id}_{Q_A}$
in every COMPLETED hidden member.

For arbitrary $n\ge2$, take a finite
PARTIAL total-unary hidden source
with quotient vertices $x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}$
in $Q_A$ and $y_0,\ldots,y_{n-1}$
in $Q_B$, no real vertices and
NO displayed binary orbitals.
Put $f(x_i)=y_i$ and
$g(y_i)=x_{i+1\pmod n}$.
The generated transition orbit of ANY vertex
is the WHOLE $2n$-vertex structure,
so it has NO proper nonempty
unary-closed induced substructure and
is IRREDUCIBLE. It has no hidden
homomorphism-embedding completion:
function preservation would imply
$h(x_{i+1})=g f(h(x_i))=h(x_i)$,
contradicting injectivity on this irreducible source.
Thus no uniform bound on NONCOMPLETABLE
unary-CLOSED substructures can hold for
ARBITRARY total-unary partial inputs.

These malformed sources fail
HN Definition~2.8(ii): their
one-generated IRREDUCIBLE closures
are NOT completed hidden members.
In the actual HN test, (ii) enforces the
unary-admissibility needed for the
RESTRICTED bounded-obstruction proof;
the terminal Ramsey claim is NOT
refuted by this example.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Uniform typed unary closure in genuine hidden diagrams
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform typed unary closure in genuine hidden diagrams]
\label{lem:typed-unary-closure-bound}
There is a constant \(m_{\mathrm{typ}}\), depending only on
the finite terminal hidden language, such that the unary
functional closure of one vertex has at most
\(m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) vertices in EVERY ACTUAL completed
hidden member. Consequently the same bound holds for
every one-generated closure in a
\cref{def:typed-unary-admissible-source} source.
NO uniform bound is asserted for arbitrary total-unary
PARTIAL source structures.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Transition-closed root signature
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Transition-closed root signature]
\label{def:typed-transition-root-signature}
Let two real roots \(x\in a\), \(y\in b\) carry a guarded pair constraint
\(D\in\Dat^{ab}\).  Its canonical root signature contains, for every
represented \(J\in\mathcal I_a\) with
\(DD^{\smile}\subseteq J\), the direct quotient-transition identity
\[
 \pi_{D,J}(F_J(x))=F_{J^D}(y),
\]
together with its full functional closure.  If the constraint is represented
by a theta bundle
\(D=\bigcap_iP_i\) with \(P_i\in\Rch^{ab}\), we additionally include the
corresponding transition identities forced by each branch profile \(P_i\).
Thus both intersection-forced and branch-forced quotient data are retained.
\end{definition}

declarations.title: Typed coordinate-term normal form
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed coordinate-term normal form]
\label{lem:typed-coordinate-normal-form}
Let \(\tau\) be a unary term whose source is a real sort \(a\) and whose
value is either the source real point itself or a hidden quotient coordinate.
Then there is a definable equivalence \(K_\tau\) on \(a\), with
\(K_\tau\) equality exactly for the identity real-point term and otherwise a
proper meet-irreducible, such that for all real \(x,x'\in a\),
\[
 \tau(x)=\tau(x')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad xK_\tau x'.
\tag{QT-NF}\label{eq:typed-coordinate-normal-form}
\]
Moreover the value \(\tau(x)\) is obtained from the
\(K_\tau\)-coordinate of \(x\) by a finite chain of quotient transitions and upward quotient maps.
Consequently the stabiliser of \(\tau(x)\) in any automorphism group equals
the stabiliser of the \(K_\tau\)-class of \(x\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Named factorisation of forced typed real-source terms
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Named factorisation of forced typed real-source terms]
\label{cor:typed-forced-term-factorisation}
Let \(J\) be a represented proper meet-irreducible on original
sort \(a\), and let \(\tau\) be an ACTUAL unary term from \(a\)
with kernel \(K_\tau\).  If \(J\le K_\tau\), then there is a
literal NAMED unary term
\(\sigma_{\tau,J}:B_{a,J}\to\operatorname{cod}(\tau)\) such that
\[
                \tau(x)=\sigma_{\tau,J}(F_J(x))
                \qquad(x\in a).
\]
No choice of groupoid chart, quotient representative or
original-sort ordering is involved.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Typed return transport
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed return transport]\label{lem:typed-return-transport}
Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) be a composable typed word from a sort \(a_0\)
back to \(a_0\), and suppose
\[
 P_1\cdots P_n\subseteq E_0
\]
for a definable equivalence \(E_0\) on \(a_0\). Put
\(R_i=P_1\cdots P_i\). Every prefix transports \(E_0\)
to an invariant equivalence \(E_i\), every factor induces one
quotient bijection, and the loop has IDENTITY holonomy.
For EVERY represented proper meet-irreducible
\(J\supseteq E_0\), the corresponding intermediate
kernels are NAMED proper represented quotient coordinates
and the actual quotient return is the identity on \(a_0/J\).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: The mixed-block diagnostic
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[The mixed-block diagnostic]
The two-sorted mixed-block structure is the basic test which invalidates the
naive ``carry sort indices through'' proof.  Let \(E_A,E_B\) be the
same-block equivalences on the two real sorts and let \(r:A\to B\) be the
same-block cross type.  Then
\[
 rr^{\smile}=E_A,
 \qquad
 E_A^r=E_B,
\]
so the hidden transition \(\pi_{r,E_A}\) sends the represented
\(E_A\)-class of an \(A\)-point to the represented \(E_B\)-class of its
\(r\)-neighbour.  The return word \(rr^{\smile}\) therefore transports the
quotient from \(A/E_A\) to \(B/E_B\) and back with identity holonomy; no
cross-sort factor is asserted to lie in a same-sort equivalence.  Thus both
failure mechanisms of the naive typed proof are visible, and repaired, in
this smallest test case.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Chordless cycles over a complete named base
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Chordless cycles over a complete named base]
\label{lem:typed-complete-base-chords}
Let $D$ be a finite complete atomic typed diagram and
let $X$ be another disjoint finite set of formal vertices.
Suppose every $x\in X$ has a specified atomic edge to
EVERY $d\in D$, while the specified edges within $X$
are those of a graph $H$. Then each specified
\emph{chordless simple cycle} is either entirely contained
in $H$, or is a triangle meeting $D$.
In particular, to test individual old-cycle completability
it suffices to test all displayed triangles meeting $D$
and the chordless cycles of $H$.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed exact-coloured orbit infinitude
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed exact-coloured orbit infinitude]
\label{lem:typed-exact-orbit-infinitude}
Let \(p(x/D)\) be an exact atomic one-point type, with \(x\) in sort \(a\),
and, writing \(b_d\) for the unary sort of \(d\), let
\(t_d:a\to b_d\) be its spoke type to \(d\in D\).  Let \(J\) be a proper
represented meet-irreducible on \(a\).  If the \(J\)-class of \(x\) does
not belong to the full quotient-transition closure of \(D\), then
realisations of \(p\) occupy infinitely many \(J\)-classes.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: No hidden algebraicity outside unary closure of an original real base
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[No hidden algebraicity outside unary closure of an original real base]
\label{cor:typed-no-real-base-hidden-algebraicity}
In the terminal visible SAP+semantic-CCO named-sorted source,
for every finite COMPLETE original real $D$,
\[
 \left\{u\in|\widehat\M|:
       |\Aut(\M/D)\cdot u|<\infty\right\}
                =D^{\coord}.
 \tag{PG-ACL}\label{eq:typed-no-real-base-hidden-algebraicity}
\]
Here $\widehat\M$ is the ACTUAL full interpreted hidden
structure, including the original real and all proper
represented quotient sorts, and $D^{\coord}$ is its full
point-generated unary closure of $D$.  Consequently
the orbit-theoretic algebraic closure of the original
real base $D$ in that full hidden structure has size
at most $m_{\mathrm{typ}}|D|$, with the empty-base
case interpreted literally. This asserts nothing
about algebraicity over an arbitrary orphan-only base.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Meet-prime MI coordinate dichotomy inside one exact Helly fibre
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Meet-prime MI coordinate dichotomy inside one exact Helly fibre]
\label{lem:typed-mi-fibre-infinite-dichotomy}
Fix ONE original named transitive real sort $a$ of
the terminal symmetric-on-sorts SAP+homomorphic-CCO
source, with full invariant-lattice NR2.
Let $E_1,\ldots,E_m>\Id_a$ be original
invariant equivalences and let
$C_i$ be actual $E_i$-classes which
meet PAIRWISE (allow $m=0$).
Put
\[
       H=\bigcap_{i=1}^m E_i,\qquad
       X=\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i,
\]
with $H=\Top_a$, $X=M_a$ for $m=0$.
Then $X$ is ONE INFINITE actual $H$-class.
For EVERY proper meet-irreducible original
invariant equivalence $J$ on the SAME
original sort there is the dichotomy
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $H\le J$, then some $E_i\le J$,
  and the actual $J$-class of any $x\in X$
  is already determined by that SINGLE
  original $E_i$-class. This case cannot
  arise when $m=0$ and $J<\Top$.
\item If $H\nleq J$, then $X$ meets
  INFINITELY MANY actual $J$-classes:
  $[H:H\cap J]=\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, given finitely many such
unforced MI kernels $J_1,\ldots,J_s$
and for each a FINITE list of forbidden
actual $J_k$-classes, ONE $x\in X$
can be chosen to avoid all lists
SIMULTANEOUSLY.
This statement concerns genuine
original class incidence, NOT a complete
fine old one-point spoke type, and does
not replace \cref{lem:typed-exact-orbit-infinitude}.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: One fresh real frame for a compatible family of MI orphans
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[One fresh real frame for a compatible family of MI orphans]
\label{cor:typed-compatible-mi-single-real-frame}
In the setting of
\cref{lem:typed-mi-fibre-infinite-dichotomy},
suppose the $E_i$ are proper represented
MEET-IRREDUCIBLES on the SAME original
real sort $a$, with pairwise compatible
actual quotient class vertices
$b_i=C_i\in M_a/E_i$.
Put $A=\cl(\{b_1,\ldots,b_m\})$
in the ACTUAL MI-only hidden language.
For EVERY finite induced unary-closed
hidden $B\supseteq A$, there is ONE
original real point $x$ with
\[
   x\in\bigcap_i C_i,\qquad
   A\subseteq\cl(\{x\}),\qquad
   \cl(\{x\})\cap B=A.
 \tag{CMF}\label{eq:typed-compatible-mi-single-real-frame}
\]
In particular $x$ can avoid every
original real vertex of $B$.
This does NOT replace the full
\cref{lem:typed-fresh-representatives},
which allows mutually INCOMPATIBLE
or different-original-sort orphan bases.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Typed fresh representatives
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed fresh representatives]
\label{lem:typed-fresh-representatives}
Let $A\le B$ be finite actual induced unary-closed hidden structures,
and let $F$ be any additional finite set of actual hidden vertices.
For every proper coordinate vertex $b\in A$ of sort $B_{a,J}$,
one can choose a real representative $x_b\in M_a$ with $F_J(x_b)=b$
such that all representatives are distinct and outside
$(B\cup F)_{\mathrm{real}}$. For every real-source term $\tau$ on $a$:
if $J\le K_\tau$, its forced value $\tau(x_b)$ is the prescribed
named term value of $b$ in $A$; otherwise $\tau(x_b)$ avoids
$B\cup F$ and every unforced term value of earlier representatives.
This gives literal closure freshness as well as fresh real representatives. With $C=A_{\mathrm{real}}$ and
$X=\{x_b:b\in A\text{ is a proper coordinate vertex}\}$, one has
\[
                  B\cap(C\cup X)^{\coord}=A.
\]
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: CCO-free kernel criterion for fresh real frames
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[CCO-free kernel criterion for fresh real frames]
\label{rem:typed-fresh-frame-cco-free}
The common provider \cref{lem:foundational-quotient-fibre-avoidance}
uses only a transitive group action, finitely many equivariant term
functions, literal named factorisation of forced terms and infinite
relative indices for unforced terms. Thus the finite freshness step
requires no original CCO, SAP, symmetry, lattice distributivity or
model homogeneity once these inputs have been verified.
In the actual terminal signature the factorisation is
\cref{cor:typed-forced-term-factorisation}, and the index condition is
FULL original NR2. CCO is used upstream to establish the represented
quotient geometry and real-base orbit infinitude. Fresh frames alone
do not imply hereditary hidden SAP: the real-base orbit condition is
still needed in \cref{lem:foundational-real-frame-orbits}.
Nor does this argument authorize adding non-MI meet quotients to
the hidden language without rechecking both the term-kernel conditions
and the real-base orbit hypothesis.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: A finite relative cover visible only after naming its fine quotient
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A finite relative cover visible only after naming its fine quotient]
\label{ex:typed-term-visible-index-two-hidden-sap}
Let the ORIGINAL one-sort
real structure be
\[
            M=\mathbb N_{\rm block}
               \times\mathbb F_2
               \times\mathbb N_{\rm clone}.
\]
Name ALL complete symmetric
diversity old pair atoms
$p,q,r$ as follows:
$p$ means SAME block,
SAME bit and distinct
clone points;
$q$ means SAME block
and OPPOSITE bits;
$r$ means DIFFERENT
blocks. Real equality
is the separate
logical diagonal.
Let $K$ be same block
AND same bit, and J
be same block.
Then
\[
  \Id<K<J<\Top,\qquad
  [J:K]=2,
  \quad [K:\Id]=\infty.
\tag{F2C}\label{eq:typed-term-visible-two-cover}
\]

The old real structure
is homogeneous and
transitive: a finite
partial automorphism
preserves the partition
into blocks and the
within-block binary
bit comparison, and
extends by permutations
of the infinitely many
blocks, independent
within-block bit swaps
and arbitrary clone
permutations.
Its finite age has SAP:
in each J-block meeting
the common base, align
the at most TWO
K-classes from the two
extensions compatibly
with their common
already named K-classes,
but identify NO real
vertices. Other new
J-blocks can be kept
disjoint, and the
infinite clone fibres
supply all fresh real
points. It is
triangle-defined
(the triangle with
three mutually
q-related points
would require three
distinct bits).
It has semantic
homomorphic CCO:
a partial diagram of
$p,q,r$ edges is a
system of J-block
equalities/inequalities,
and of $\mathbb F_2$
parity equations
on J-equality edges.
A contradictory
J-inequality is closed
by a J-equality path;
a contradictory bit
equation is a
nonzero-parity cycle.
Choosing a SHORTEST
such witness gives a
specified SIMPLE cycle
with no homomorphism.
In the absence of
these obstructions,
give all J-equality
connected components
distinct block labels,
solve their consistent
bit equations, and use
fresh clone coordinates
to obtain even an
injective old completion.

Now first name ONLY the
nonreal quotient sort
$Q_J=M/J$ and its
projection $p_J$,
together with all ACTUAL
binary original/quotient
orbitals. Call this
finite many-sorted
homogeneous unary
structure $H_J$.
Its homogeneity is direct:
a finite old real/owner
partial isomorphism
preserves the explicit
same-block membership
relation and the fine
old p/q/r atoms, so
extends using the
displayed permutations.
The only distinct
original-real-source
unary TERM FUNCTIONS
are the original real
identity (kernel Id)
and $p_J$ (kernel J).
For $p_J$ the forced
factorisation through
$Q_J$ is the named
identity; for real
identity one has
$[J:\Id]=\infty$.
The REAL-BASE orbit
condition holds:
outside a finite real
set and its named
J-block values,
each real point has
an infinite clone
or new-block orbit,
and each unmentioned
J-block has infinite
orbit. Hence the
abstract iff
\cref{cor:typed-abstract-relative-kernel-sap-iff}
proves
\[
                 \Age(H_J)\text{ has SAP}.
\]
Thus the original
FINITE relative index
$[J:K]=2$ is harmless
to this narrower named
quotient signature.

Next ALSO name the
fine quotient
$Q_K=M/K$, its
projection $p_K$,
and the natural upward
unary map $Q_K\to Q_J$.
Call the resulting
full actual canonical
binary quotient
expansion $H_{K,J}$.
It is still homogeneous
by the same explicit
block/bit/clone
permutation argument.
But the original term
$\tau=p_K$ has kernel
K, and for the
named coarse quotient
J,
\[
                  J\nleq K,\qquad
                  [J:J\cap K]=2.
\]
For each orphan
$b\in Q_J$, EXACTLY
two $Q_K$ points lie
above b. They form
a finite b-definable
set, hence are
algebraic over b,
while the nontrivial
bit swap moves them
and no named unary
term from $Q_J$
selects either one.
Therefore
\[
                 \Age(H_{K,J})
                       \text{ does NOT have SAP}.
\]
This is the precise
term-visible
finite-index obstruction
of
\cref{cor:typed-abstract-relative-kernel-sap-iff}.

In particular global
FULL NR2 is a
SUFFICIENT input for
the terminal MI-only
argument but is
NOT NECESSARY for the
HEREDITARY hidden SAP
of an arbitrarily
chosen smaller
quotient signature.
The exact requirement
is the term-sensitive
criterion (RK)
together with
real-base
nonalgebraicity.
\end{example}

declarations.title: No algebraicity over arbitrary finite hidden closed bases
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[No algebraicity over arbitrary finite hidden closed bases]
\label{lem:typed-hereditary-hidden-orbits}
In the terminal ACTUAL transition-enriched hidden
interpretation $\widehat{\M}$, let $A$ be ANY
finite induced UNARY-FUNCTIONALLY CLOSED
hidden substructure, including one with ONLY
orphan proper quotient vertices.
For every actual hidden vertex $u\notin A$,
\[
       |\Aut(\M/A)\cdot u|=\infty.
 \tag{HO}\label{eq:typed-hereditary-hidden-orbits}
\]
Here $\Aut(\M/A)$ acts on every actual represented
hidden quotient sort and fixes all of $A$ POINTWISE.
Consequently, over an arbitrary finite hidden
parameter set $T$, the orbit-theoretic hidden
algebraic closure equals its finite unary term
closure:
\[
    \operatorname{acl}_{\widehat{\M}}(T)
      =\operatorname{dcl}_{\widehat{\M}}(T)
      =\cl_{\widehat{\M}}(T).
\]
This conclusion is about the named ACTUAL
terminal hidden sorts only; it does not
automatically extend to additional imaginary sorts.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: An exact non-MI meet quotient can destroy hidden SAP
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[An exact non-MI meet quotient can destroy hidden SAP]
\label{ex:typed-exact-nonmi-hidden-sap-failure}
The MEET-IRREDUCIBLE restriction on the
proper quotient sorts in this theorem is
ESSENTIAL, even if the original symmetric
binary source has SAP, homomorphic CCO,
and NO finite relative-index invariant cuts.

Take one original real sort
$M=\mathbb N_{\rm row}\times
\mathbb N_{\rm col}\times\mathbb N_{\rm clone}$,
and name its FOUR complete diversity atoms
by equality/disequality of the row and
column coordinates of DISTINCT real points.
The two coordinate equivalence relations
are independent, and each common cell
has INFINITELY many distinct clones.
This source is homogeneous and has SAP:
the two finite equivalence systems can
be amalgamated freely over their common
classes, while distinct real vertices
are realised by fresh clones even in
one forced common cell.  Its age is
triangle-defined, and semantic HOMOMORPHIC
CCO follows by detecting a coordinate
inequality edge joined by a path of
coordinate equality edges; a shortest
such path gives a forbidden SIMPLE cycle.
Without such an obstruction, give
each equality component a distinct
coordinate and all vertices fresh clones.

Put $J=E_{\rm row}$,
$K=E_{\rm col}$, and
$L=J\cap K=E_{\rm cell}$.
The FULL invariant-equivalence lattice is
\[
       \Id <L<J,K<\Top ,
\]
with ALL strict relative indices INFINITE.
Both $J,K$ are meet-irreducible, but $L$
is NOT.  All three are nevertheless
FULL RAW exact: if $p,u,v$ denote
respectively same-cell distinct-clone,
same-row different-column and same-column
different-row old atoms, then
\[
          L=p;p,\qquad J=u;u,\qquad K=v;v
\]
with the ACTUAL identity diagonal included
in these represented two-step products.

Now INCORRECTLY enlarge the hidden language
by the additional exact NON-MI quotient
sort $M/L$, with its actual unary projections
$\pi_J:M/L\to M/J$ and
$\pi_K:M/L\to M/K$.
Fix one row quotient vertex $a$ and one
column quotient vertex $b$. Their
unary closure $A=\cl\{a,b\}$ contains
no $M/L$ vertex: the stabiliser of
a single row or column acts transitively
on infinitely many cells above it,
so no equivariant unary term can
select a cell. Yet there is a UNIQUE
cell quotient vertex $c\in M/L$
with $\pi_J(c)=a$ and $\pi_K(c)=b$.
It is algebraic, even definable,
over $A$, but not in its unary closure.
Two copies of the finite unary-closed
extension $A\cup\{c\}$ over $A$ CANNOT
be strongly amalgamated: both alleged
distinct new cell vertices must map to
that same unique $c$.

The same obstruction already destroys
SAP in the POINT-GENERATED hidden class.
Choose ORIGINAL real points
$x=(r,c_0,k_0)$ and $y=(r_0,c,k_1)$
with $r\ne r_0$ and $c\ne c_0$.
Their unary closure contains the
row quotient $r$, the column quotient
$c$, and their respective ORIGINAL
cell quotients $(r,c_0)$ and $(r_0,c)$,
but NOT the CROSS cell quotient $(r,c)$.
A third original real point
$z=(r,c,k_2)$ generates precisely
this missing $M/L$ vertex. Yet that
vertex is uniquely determined by
the $J$-coordinate of $x$ and the
$K$-coordinate of $y$. Hence two
copies of the FULL point-generated
structure $\cl\{x,y,z\}$ over
$\cl\{x,y\}$ cannot be strongly
amalgamated either.

Thus \emph{naming all exact quotient sorts}
would destroy even point-generated
hidden SAP, whereas the actual terminal
MI-only hidden signature names
$M/J,M/K$ but NOT $M/L$.
The example does not contradict the
preceding no-algebraicity lemma,
whose exact signature hypothesis is
strictly narrower. Joint quotient
homogeneity by itself does not imply SAP.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Graph-coupled SAP--CCO with two incomparable MI quotients
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Graph-coupled SAP--CCO with two incomparable MI quotients]
\label{ex:typed-graph-coupled-two-mi}
A POSITIVE non-free-superposition control for the
preceding MI-only hidden algebraicity result is
the Fraisse limit of finite one-sort structures
with TWO original equivalences $R,C$ and
one undirected irreflexive graph edge relation
$G$, subject only to
\[
 \text{no $G$-triangle contained in one
 $R$-class OR one $C$-class}.
\]
Name the complete ORIGINAL diversity atom
$(\epsilon_R,\epsilon_C,\rho)\in\{0,1\}^3$
of each pair, where the first two bits
record membership in $R,C$ and
$\rho$ records $G$-adjacency.
All eight pair atoms occur.
The age is triangle-defined.
Its STRONG amalgamation is the independent
free amalgam of the two equivalence
systems together with NO new cross-factor
$G$-edges: every all-$G$ triangle
then lies in one original factor.
Thus the countable limit is homogeneous,
transitive and has SAP.

For semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO, a finite
partial old network can violate one
of the two equivalence systems only
via a coordinate-inequality edge
closed by a specified equality path,
giving a forbidden SIMPLE cycle.
If neither coordinate system is
inconsistent, assign distinct labels
to its equality-connected components
and make ALL unspecified $G$-edges
nonedges. A forbidden $G$-triangle
inside one completed equivalence
class would have all THREE graph
edges already specified as $G$.
Each of those specified atoms must
then also carry that coordinate's
EQUALITY bit, else the coordinate
system was already inconsistent.
Thus the triangle itself would be
a specified impossible 3-cycle.
Consequently the partial network
completes injectively whenever
each specified simple cycle maps,
so the source has semantic CCO.

The FULL original invariant-equivalence
lattice is
\[
                   \Id<L=R\cap C<R,C<\Top .
\]
For either $G$-colour (edge or nonedge),
its old atomic-orbital graph generates
exactly $L$, $R$, $C$ or $\Top$
according to its two equality bits.
For nonedges, a two-step path through
a fresh compatible coordinate is enough.
For graph edges, use a two-step path
unless the existing endpoint $G$-edge
would make a forbidden monochromatic
triangle, in which case a three-step
$G$-path with NONEDGE diagonals
works. Every displayed configuration
is a legal triangle-consistent finite
old structure, so exists by homogeneity.
It follows that there are no further
invariant equivalences; all strict
relative indices are infinite.
All four nonidentity equivalences
are FULL RAW exact using the
NONEDGE singleton orbitals:
their ACTUAL twofold RAW products
are respectively $L,R,C,\Top$.
The two proper meet-irreducibles
are $R,C$, with infinite common
meet class $L$.

For the ACTUAL MI-only hidden language
naming $M/R,M/C$ but NOT $M/L$,
every hidden vertex outside ANY
finite unary-closed hidden base $A$
has infinite orbit under
$\Aut(M/A)$. For an off-base REAL
point choose finite real representatives
of orphan quotient vertices of $A$
avoiding that point, then apply old
SAP to obtain infinitely many
real clones over their complete
real diagram. For a new ROW quotient
class, choose such representatives
avoiding that row; Fraisse extension
gives arbitrarily many old points
with its complete original spoke
types over the representatives but
pairwise DIFFERENT fresh row classes
and mutual $G$-NONEDGES.
Old homogeneity transports the
new row class to each of these
different quotient values while
fixing the real representative
frame, hence fixes $A$.
The column case is symmetric.
Therefore hidden
$\operatorname{acl}(A)=A$,
and \cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}
gives HEREDITARY hidden SAP
independently of the general
typed high-chromatic orbit proof.

This example genuinely couples
a triangle-free $G$-restriction
to BOTH equivalence directions;
it is NOT a free superposition of
an arbitrary graph and equivalences.
Its two MI quotient axes do,
however, still have CARTESIAN
incidence with infinite common cells.
In fact this phenomenon cannot
fail for ANY finite collection of
pairwise compatible nontrivial
ORIGINAL invariant classes in a
terminal symmetric SAP+CCO source:
the general infinite exact-class
Helly corollary
\cref{cor:rh-sap-infinite-exact-helly}
makes their COMMON real intersection
an INFINITE equivalence class.
Therefore a genuinely non-Cartesian
higher-order MI coordinate incidence,
with all pairs compatible but no
joint real point, is EXCLUDED by
the original CCO+SAP hypotheses,
not merely missing from this example.
An additional named exact but
NON-MI quotient $M/L$ would again
destroy hidden SAP by the unique
meet-coordinate obstruction of
\cref{ex:typed-exact-nonmi-hidden-sap-failure}.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Hierarchical non-Cartesian incidence of three MI quotients
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Hierarchical non-Cartesian incidence of three MI quotients]
\label{ex:typed-hierarchical-three-mi}
The terminal MI-only hidden age can have
NON-CARTESIAN quotient incidence and
nontrivial NAMED upward quotient maps,
while still having SAP.
Take ONE original real sort
\[
 M=\mathbb N_{\rm parent}\times
   \mathbb N_{\rm row}\times
   \mathbb N_{\rm col}\times
   \mathbb N_{\rm clone}.
\]
Within each parent the row/column
coordinates are local. Name the
FIVE complete symmetric diversity
old atoms $p,u,v,w,q$,
respectively: same parent/row/column
(different clones); same parent/row
but different column; same
parent/column but different row;
same parent with different row and
column; and different parents.
Real equality is logical.

Every finite complete triangle-legal
old diagram is exactly a triple of
equivalence relations $R,C\le H$,
where $R,C$ record same parent/row
and same parent/column, while
$H$ records same parent.
Independently amalgamate the
$H$-classes and then the $R,C$
class systems within each resulting
$H$-class, always retaining distinct
formal old vertices by choosing
fresh clones in their common cell.
Thus the age has SAP and is
triangle-defined; independent
parent, relative row/column and
within-cell permutations make
its countable limit homogeneous
and transitive.

Semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO follows
from the same original coordinate
constraint analysis: an incompatible
H-, R- or C-inequality is closed
by a path of corresponding
EQUALITY edges; a shortest such
path with the violating inequality
edge is a forbidden specified
SIMPLE cycle. Here $R,C\le H$
must be respected: R/C equality
edges also impose H equality.
Without any such obstruction,
assign parent labels to H
components, row/column labels
independently inside each parent,
and DISTINCT clone points to all
formal real vertices. This gives
an injective original completion.

The FULL invariant-equivalence
lattice is exactly
\[
                 \Id<L=R\cap C<R,C<H<\Top,
                 \qquad R\vee C=H.
\]
Its complete classification follows
because the connectivity relations
of the original atoms
$p,u,v,w,q$ generate respectively
$L,R,C,H,\Top$; every invariant
equivalence is a union of atoms
and hence their generated join.
Each original invariant
equivalence is ACTUAL FULL RAW
exact, with old products
\[
         p;p=L,\quad u;u=R,\quad
         v;v=C,\quad w;w=H,\quad
         q;q=\Top .
\]
All proper relative indices
are INFINITE by parent/row/column/
clone infinitude. The three
proper NONIDENTITY meet-irreducible
kernels are exactly $R,C,H$;
$L$ is exact but NON-MI.

The ACTUAL MI-only hidden language
names $M/R,M/C,M/H$ but NOT $M/L$,
with named upward maps from row
and column quotients to their
common parent quotient.
Two orphan MI classes from
$M/R$ and $M/C$ are compatible
iff their upward parent images
agree; within that parent
their common real fibre is
INFINITE. For ANY finite
unary-closed hidden base $A$,
an off-base parent quotient
vertex moves through unused
parent blocks, an off-base
row/column quotient vertex
moves through unused local
classes within a fixed parent
(or with an unfixed parent),
and an off-base ORIGINAL real
point moves among infinitely
many clones of its own cell.
These independent permutations
fix every vertex of $A$.
Thus the actual hidden
$\operatorname{acl}(A)=A$,
and the general
\cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion}
gives hereditary MI-only
hidden SAP without invoking the
original high-chromatic
orbit-infinitude argument.

Naming the additional exact
NON-MI cell quotient $M/L$
would destroy that property:
a row class and a column class
with the same parent determine
one UNIQUE $L$-class outside
their named unary closure.
This is the same multi-parameter
algebraicity obstruction as
\cref{ex:typed-exact-nonmi-hidden-sap-failure}.
The example is NON-CARTESIAN
globally, because row and column
classes from DIFFERENT parents
are incompatible, but every
PAIRWISE compatible finite
MI-class tuple still has an
infinite real fibre, by
\cref{cor:rh-sap-infinite-exact-helly}.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Graph-coupled hierarchical MI calibration
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Graph-coupled hierarchical MI calibration]
\label{rem:typed-hierarchical-graph-mi}
The parent/row/column source of
\cref{ex:typed-hierarchical-three-mi}
can be GENUINELY coupled to an
additional symmetric irreflexive
graph $G$, without losing its
SAP, semantic homomorphic CCO,
full invariant NR2 or its hidden
MI-only algebraicity-free
property. Name the TEN original
fine diversity atoms given by
one of the FIVE hierarchical
pair types and a $G$-edge/nonedge
bit. Forbid $G$-triangles entirely
within ONE row class or entirely
within ONE column class.

This remains triangle-defined.
For strong amalgamation, first
amalgamate the three old
equivalences and declare EVERY
new cross-factor $G$-edge a
NONEDGE. For semantic CCO,
inconsistency of H,R,C
coordinates gives a shortest
forbidden equality-path-plus-
inequality-edge cycle; if those
constraints are consistent, make
all missing $G$-edges nonedges.
Any remaining forbidden
within-row/column $G$-triangle
was already entirely specified
and is itself an impossible
three-cycle. Thus the old partial
network completes.

The ORIGINAL invariant-equivalence
lattice remains exactly
$\Id<L<R,C<H<\Top$:
the NONEDGE original fine
orbital graphs alone have the
same respective connectivity
equivalences $L,R,C,H,\Top$,
and the G-edge orbital graphs
generate no additional invariant
equivalence. In particular all
these equivalences are FULL RAW
exact via squares of the
nonedge singleton atoms,
and the proper MI kernels
are still $R,C,H$.
The original finite frame
selection uses fresh row/column
values with NONEDGE new
adjacencies; each off-base
MI coordinate has infinitely
many old homogeneous
realisations of its complete
fine one-point type over that
frame, choosing all mutual
new $G$-edges as NONEDGES.
Consequently the actual MI-only
hidden age still has SAP by
\cref{lem:unary-homogeneous-sap-criterion},
whereas naming exact NON-MI
cell quotient $M/L$ still
produces the algebraic
meet-coordinate obstruction.

Unlike an unrestricted free
superposition of a graph with
equivalences, the $G$-triangle
forbiddance is conditional on
TWO proper MI quotient classes;
unlike a global Cartesian
coordinate product, row and
column quotients from distinct
parent classes cannot meet.
The proof controls ACTUAL
binary triangles and all simple
specified old cycles, not just
quotient-orbit names.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: An anchored fine pair type fixes every old hidden coordinate reading
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[An anchored fine pair type fixes every old hidden coordinate reading]
\label{lem:typed-anchored-real-clone-readout}
Let \(p\) be an actual real point of original
sort \(a\), and let \(B\) be a finite
COMPLETE old visible frame not containing
\(p\). Assume that for every old proper
hidden coordinate vertex \(q\) whose
reading must be retained, \(B\) contains
one designated actual real representative
\(a_q\) of the target quotient class.
Also include representatives of all
proper quotient coordinates \(F_J(p)\)
that must be retained from \(p\).
Suppose \(p'\ne p\) is another real point
of sort \(a\) and
\[
       \col(p',z)=\col(p,z)\qquad(z\in B).
\tag{ACR}\label{eq:typed-anchor-clone-reading}
\]
Then \(p'\) has exactly the same
represented proper \(J\)-coordinates as
\(p\) for every relevant \(J\), and
the same named unary term values after
all upward maps and quotient transitions.
Every old real--proper-coordinate
semantic cylinder with first endpoint
\(p\) and second endpoint among
the retained \(q\)'s has the same
value with first endpoint \(p'\).
All relations between proper coordinates
of \(p\) and old proper coordinates
\(q\), as well as between two
old proper coordinates, are unchanged.

The conclusion is only about hidden
RELATIONS/FUNCTIONS that are canonically
defined by original fine pair orbitals
and represented quotient classes.
Higher-arity original tuple constraints
are not covered by this binary lemma.
\end{lemma}

declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed representative splitting]
\label{lem:typed-real-sort-splitting}
Let \(h:C\to H\) be a homomorphism-embedding of a finite functionally closed
transition-enriched hidden structure into a full hidden expansion of some
finite visible \(A\in\mathcal C\).  After passing to a finite visible
extension \(A'\in\mathcal C\), one may choose pairwise distinct real images
for all old real vertices of \(C\) and pairwise distinct designated real
representatives for all old proper coordinate vertices.  All specified old
relations, coordinate functions, quotient transitions and semantic-cylinder
relations are preserved.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Irreducible source supports and complete-pattern defects
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Irreducible source supports and complete-pattern defects]
\label{lem:typed-joined-source-support}
Let \(C\) be a finite functionally closed PARTIAL
hidden structure, and let \(D=\cl_C(B)\)
for at most \(k\) OLD hidden source vertices.
Assume \( |\cl_C\{b\}|\le m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) for each chosen generator
\(b\in B\), as holds when \(C\) is unary-admissible.
Suppose \(D\), with its actual induced
PARTIAL diagram, is irreducible in the
hidden language (including its unary functions).
If \(C\) has a hidden
homomorphism-embedding completion,
then the map on \(D\) is an EMBEDDING,
so \(D\) is isomorphic to a completed
induced hidden substructure. In particular,
if the full induced diagram of \(D\) is
missing a relation, inequality, or
functional identity that every actual
completed realisation of its displayed
joining datum has, then \(C\) has NO
homomorphism-embedding completion.
The defect is supported on at most
\(k m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) old vertices.

It is NOT enough that a displayed relation
joins some unary TERM VALUES from
\(\cl_C(b)\) and \(\cl_C(c)\):
the joint closure \(\cl_C\{b,c\}\)
can remain reducible. Such an
unjoined pair must NOT be subjected
to the complete two-root test merely
because a relation holds in a common
quotient-coordinate subdiagram.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: A reducible two-root control
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[A reducible two-root control]
\label{rem:typed-term-join-not-irreducible}
In the one-sort age of an equivalence
with infinitely many infinite classes,
let \(x,y\) be real vertices and let
\(u=F_E(x)\), \(v=F_E(y)\) be their
proper quotient coordinates. Take
the functionally closed partial
hidden diagram induced by the
two complete one-generated diagrams
of \(x,y\), together with the
displayed OFF-DIAGONAL quotient-cylinder
relation on \(u,v\), but with NO
original fine atomic relation on
\(x,y\) (nor arbitrary cross-cylinder
relations on \(x,v\), \(y,u\)).
This diagram is completable,
choosing \(x,y\) in distinct
\(E\)-classes. It is the free
amalgam of its restrictions
to \(\{x,u,v\}\) and
\(\{y,u,v\}\) over \(\{u,v\}\).
A relation between \(F_E(x)\) and
\(F_E(y)\) thus DOES NOT make
the full two-real-root closure
irreducible. In a guarded lift
the quotient-cylinder datum is
attached to its ACTUAL old source
endpoints \(u,v\), while the
individual projection equations
are attached to \(x,u\) and \(y,v\).
It is invalid to fill in the
previously unspecified fine
\(x,y\) relation before completion.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Exactly when a hidden term-pair orbital has no diversity preimage
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exactly when a hidden term-pair orbital has no diversity preimage]
\label{lem:typed-term-orbit-diagonal-dichotomy}
Let \(a,b\) be original
transitive named real sorts
of one homogeneous complete
typed binary SAP structure,
and let
\(\tau:a\to Q\),
\(\sigma:b\to R\)
be surjective equivariant
unary-term maps with
original real kernels
\(J=K_\tau\), \(K=K_\sigma\).
For every NONEMPTY
\(\Aut(\M)\)-orbit
\(\Theta\subseteq Q\times R\)
exactly one of the following
holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Its pullback contains
an ordered pair of
DISTINCT original real
vertices. Then its
DIVERSITY preimage is
the nonempty full
representative saturation
\(\operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t)\)
of any one old atomic
diversity pair type
\(t\) in that pullback.
\item Its pullback contains
NO distinct original
real pair. Necessarily
\(a=b\), \(J=K=\Id_a\),
both maps are injective
equivariant identifications
of their real source with
their respective output
sorts, and \(\Theta\)
is the graph pairing
\(\tau(x)\) with
\(\sigma(x)\) for the
SAME original real point
\(x\in a\).
\end{enumerate}
In case (ii), a requirement
on two distinct, irreducibly
joined OLD source vertices
to realise \(\Theta\)
is a bounded real-identity
defect, not a nonempty
STRONG diversity constraint.
For a single OLD source
real root the corresponding
term identity is tested
in its unary closure.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: CCO-free positive pullback for complete quotient-pair orbitals
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[CCO-free positive pullback for complete quotient-pair orbitals]
\label{lem:typed-complete-orbital-positive-NR2-SAP}
Let $M$ be any countable HOMOGENEOUS finite complete
binary structure with named individually transitive
original real sorts, symmetric same-sort old atoms,
and visible SAP. Assume that on EACH original
real sort there is NO strict finite-relative-index
interval in the FULL lattice of original
invariant equivalences.  Semantic CCO, exact-ball
Helly, and distributivity of the invariant
equivalence lattice are NOT assumed.

For ANY surjective $\Aut(M)$-equivariant maps
$\tau:M_a\to Q$, $\sigma:M_b\to R$
to transitive quotient $G$-sets,
each complete $G$-orbital $\Theta\subseteq Q\times R$
has exactly one of the following OLD diversity
pullbacks:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item ONE nonempty ORIGINAL strong-positive typed
word profile, equal to the full
$\ker\tau,\ker\sigma$-saturated old cylinder
of ANY of its fine atomic diversity witnesses;
\item the EMPTY diversity spectrum, possible
only if $a=b$, both kernels are TRUE real
equality, and $\Theta$ is the same-real-point
graph of $\tau,\sigma$.
\end{enumerate}
The nonempty spectra of all such orbitals partition
the ORIGINAL old diversity atomic palette.
In particular, the terminal named-term readout below obtains
positivity from old SAP plus full-lattice terminality,
without CCO. This does NOT imply hidden SAP, exact
quotient structure inheritance or any Ramsey arrow.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Complete hidden term-pair orbitals have one positive old cylinder
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Complete hidden term-pair orbitals have one positive old cylinder]
\label{lem:typed-term-pair-orbit-pullback}
Let \(\tau:a\to Q\) and
\(\sigma:b\to R\) be two
NAMED unary term functions
from original transitive
real sorts \(a,b\) into
actual hidden real or
proper represented quotient
sorts. Let \(J=K_\tau\)
and \(K=K_\sigma\) be their
OLD real kernel
equivalences from
\cref{lem:typed-coordinate-normal-form};
each is either actual
logical equality or a
nonzero represented proper
meet-irreducible.

Let \(\Theta\) denote ONE
complete named hidden
binary semantic-cylinder
orbital on the output
sort pair \(Q,R\), or a
single named quotient
transition graph orbital,
or the actual equality
diagonal on one common
hidden output sort.
Assume \(\Theta\) has at
least ONE witness
\((\tau(x_0),\sigma(y_0))\)
with DISTINCT original
real representatives
\(x_0\ne y_0\).
Put \(t_0=\col(x_0,y_0)\).
Then the exact old
DIVERSITY atomic spectrum
of this term-value
comparison is
\[
 \{t:\Theta(\tau(x),\sigma(y))
       \text{ whenever }\col(x,y)=t\}
     =\operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t_0).
\tag{TOP}\label{eq:typed-term-orbital-pullback}
\]
The right side is a
NONEMPTY POSITIVE STRONG
typed reachable profile:
interpret each nonzero
\(J,K\) as its diversity
palette \(J^\circ,K^\circ\),
omit actual identity
endpoint factors, and use
\cref{lem:typed-raw-strong-saturation}
and the terminal reachability
of these equivalence
diversity palettes.

The equality-comparison
case excluded by the
distinct-representative
hypothesis is characterised
EXACTLY by
\cref{lem:typed-term-orbit-diagonal-dichotomy}:
it has equality real
kernels at both source
endpoints and forces their
SAME original real point.
It is NOT a positive
STRONG diversity type. In an irreducibly
joined source pair of
DISTINCT OLD hidden
vertices it is a bounded
identity defect, as in
\cref{lem:typed-identity-transport-redundant}.
For two occurrences of
the SAME old source root,
the equality is instead
already tested within its
one-generated unary
closure, with NO synthetic
STRONG identity edge.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Exact diversity partition by complete hidden term-pair orbitals
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Exact diversity partition by complete hidden term-pair orbitals]
\label{cor:typed-complete-orbital-pullback-partition}
In the terminal typed source let
$\tau:a\to Q$ and $\sigma:b\to R$
be surjective equivariant NAMED unary terms
with original real kernels $J,K$,
each either logical equality or a represented
proper nonzero quotient equivalence.
For each COMPLETE $\Aut(\M)$-orbital
$\Theta\subseteq Q\times R$, put
\[
 \mathcal P_\Theta=
 \{\col(x,y):x\in a,\ y\in b,\ x\ne y,\
       (\tau(x),\sigma(y))\in\Theta\}.
\]
As $\Theta$ ranges over the complete actual hidden
pair orbitals, the NONEMPTY $\mathcal P_\Theta$
form a PARTITION of the realised old
$a$-to-$b$ DIVERSITY atomic palette.
Each part is exactly ONE original full
$J,K$-saturated cylinder
$\operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t)$ and is
a nonempty positive typed STRONG reachable profile.
There is at most ONE orbital with empty
diversity pullback; if it exists, then
$a=b$, $J=K=\Id_a$, and it is exactly
the SAME-original-real-point graph orbital
of \cref{lem:typed-term-orbit-diagonal-dichotomy}.
Thus one COMPLETE hidden orbital never pulls
back to an unverified union of distinct cylinders;
an arbitrary union of hidden orbitals is NOT
claimed to be one cylinder or one reachable profile.
\end{corollary}
