declarations.title: Mixed original sorts: quotient diagonal versus real equality
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Mixed original sorts: quotient diagonal versus real equality]
\label{ex:typed-mixed-block-orbital-diagonal}
Let $I,N_A,N_B$ be countably
infinite sets. Take two disjoint
original named real sorts
$M_A=I\times N_A$ and
$M_B=I\times N_B$.
On each sort name the complete
symmetric diversity pair atoms
$p_A,p_B$ for DISTINCT points
with the SAME $I$-coordinate
and $d_A,d_B$ for DIFFERENT
$I$-coordinates. Between
the two original sorts
name $r:A\to B$ for
SAME $I$-coordinate and
$s:A\to B$ for DIFFERENT
$I$-coordinates, with their
actual typed converses.

The combined finite-complete
binary structure is homogeneous,
has visible SAP and semantic
HOMOMORPHIC simple-cycle CCO.
Indeed finite coloured diagrams
are precisely finite systems
of equality/inequality
constraints on a COMMON block
index set $I$, with arbitrary
distinct points in each old
sort/block. Any inconsistent
specified diagram has an
inequality edge connected by
a specified equality path;
choose a SHORTEST such path
to get an uncompletable
specified simple cycle.
Otherwise assign distinct
block indices to the equality
components. Original SAP
keeps all real points distinct
using fresh $N_A,N_B$
coordinates even when
their block indices are forced
to agree. Original finite
partial isomorphisms extend
by a common block permutation
and independent
within-sort/block permutations.

The FULL same-sort invariant
lattices are
$\Id_A<E_A<\Top_A$ and
$\Id_B<E_B<\Top_B$, where
$E_A,E_B$ are the actual
same-block equivalences;
all strict relative indices
are INFINITE. The actual
RAW word $p_A;p_A$ represents
$E_A$ including genuine
real identity, and
$p_B;p_B$ represents $E_B$.
Let $Q_A=M_A/E_A$,
$Q_B=M_B/E_B$, both actual
copies of the common block
index $I$.
The cross atom $r$
induces the NAMED
bijective quotient
transport
\[
                   q_r:Q_A\longrightarrow Q_B.
\]
Its graph is ONE complete
hidden quotient-pair orbital
$\Theta_r\subseteq Q_A\times Q_B$;
the other complete orbital
$\Theta_s$ consists of
different block indices.
Their FULL old diversity
pullbacks are respectively
\[
 \mathcal P_{\Theta_r}
   =\operatorname{Cyl}_{E_A,E_B}(r)
   =p_A\starprod r\starprod p_B
   =\{r\},
\qquad
 \mathcal P_{\Theta_s}
   =\operatorname{Cyl}_{E_A,E_B}(s)
   =\{s\}.
\]
Likewise the mixed REAL/QUOTIENT
hidden orbital on
$M_A\times Q_B$
saying that the old A-point
has the SAME block as the
B-quotient point has
diversity preimage
\[
                   \{r\}\starprod p_B=\{r\}.
\]
No identification of real
A- and B-points, and no
section choosing individual
REAL block representatives,
is involved.

The subtle diagonal control
is on $Q_A\times Q_A$:
its TRUE HIDDEN quotient
diagonal $\Delta_{Q_A}$
has NONEMPTY OLD diversity
preimage
\[
     \mathcal P_{\Delta_{Q_A}}
       =\{p_A\}
       =p_A\starprod p_A\starprod p_A.
\]
Two distinct old real A-points
in one infinite $E_A$-class
therefore realise EQUALITY
of their hidden $Q_A$ outputs.
In contrast the TRUE old
real equality diagonal on
$M_A\times M_A$ has EMPTY
old diversity pullback
and is the identity-only
exception of
\cref{lem:typed-term-orbit-diagonal-dichotomy}.
Thus a HIDDEN quotient
diagonal is NOT generally
an OLD STRONG identity edge.

If $q_r$ were OMITTED
from a proposed hidden
unary signature while
the canonical mixed
binary quotient orbitals
were still named, the
unique matched $Q_B$ value
over one orphan $Q_A$ point
would be algebraic but
NOT generated by a
named unary term. This
would violate the abstract
criterion
\cref{cor:typed-abstract-relative-kernel-sap-iff},
even though the original
two-sorted visible source
still has SAP and CCO.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Hidden SAP does not force G1-positive quotient diagonals
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Hidden SAP does not force G1-positive quotient diagonals]
\label{rem:typed-hidden-sap-not-G1-positivity}
The CCO-free hereditary SAP criterion
\cref{cor:typed-abstract-relative-kernel-sap-iff}
does NOT imply the positive-orbital
G1 conclusion if the original FULL
no-finite-relative-index hypothesis
is omitted.

Indeed use the ACTUAL homogeneous
visible SAP+semantic-CCO source
\cref{ex:typed-term-visible-index-two-hidden-sap}:
\[
 M=\mathbb N_{\rm block}\times
      \mathbb F_2\times\mathbb N_{\rm clone},
 \qquad
 \Id<K<J<\Top,\quad[J:K]=2,
\]
whose original diversity
atoms are $p$ (same block,
same bit, distinct clones),
$q$ (same block, opposite
bits), and $r$ (different
blocks). Name ONLY the
coarse J-quotient sort
$Q_J=M/J$ and its projection,
with all actual canonical
hidden binary orbitals.
As proved in that example,
its entire hereditary
unary-closed hidden age
HAS SAP, although the
original invariant lattice
has an index-two interval.

The TRUE HIDDEN diagonal
orbital
$\Delta_{Q_J}\subseteq Q_J^2$
has old DISTINCT-real-pair
pullback
\[
            J^\circ=\{p,q\}.
\tag{FG1}\label{eq:typed-finite-index-G1-failure}
\]
But this menu is NOT the
STRONG endpoint profile of
ANY original positive
atomic word in the
three-letter palette
$\{p,q,r\}$. If the word
contains an $r$-letter,
choose its intermediate
block indices from the
infinite common block set
so each r-step changes
block and the final block
differs from the initial
one. The resulting fully
injective real path has
endpoint atom $r$, so
the word profile is NOT
contained in $\{p,q\}$.
If the word contains
NO r-letter, its points
all lie within ONE block,
and the parity of the
number of $q$-letters
uniquely determines the
endpoint bit difference:
for distinct endpoints
its STRONG profile is
$\{p\}$ or $\{q\}$,
never $\{p,q\}$.
The real identity output
cannot be added as a
fictitious positive atom.

The obstruction already
occurs at the equality-
inclusive RAW exact
level. A word containing
NO $r$ has FIXED endpoint
bit parity, so its RAW
relation cannot contain
BOTH original diversity
atoms $p,q$. A word
with EXACTLY one $r$
has all endpoints in
different blocks, so
cannot contain $p,q$
either. A word with
at least TWO $r$ letters
contains the old
different-block atom
$r$: use at least three
distinct block indices
along the successive
$r$-steps, leaving the
first and last blocks
different. Consequently
ANY nonempty finite
intersection of RAW
word profiles containing
BOTH $p$ and $q$
ALSO contains $r$.
The actual invariant
equivalence
$J=\Id\cup p\cup q$
is therefore NOT a
FULL RAW exact
equivalence in this
source.

Thus even the
COMPLETELY NAMED coarse
hidden quotient diagonal
has NO positive old
STRONG word-pullback
in this source, despite
the hidden hereditary SAP
given by the abstract
kernel criterion.
The actual $J$ quotient
is not covered by the
general ORIGINAL FULL
EXACT quotient lifting
theorem, although its
canonical hidden expansion
is homogeneous directly
by explicit block actions.
In the terminal G1 theorem
FULL no-relative-index
two is a substantive
RAW exactness and
positive-path hypothesis,
not an irrelevant
technical consequence
of hidden SAP.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: Typed guarded real lift
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{construction}[Typed guarded real lift]
\label{con:typed-guarded-lift}
Let \(C\) be a finite UNARY-ADMISSIBLE
(\cref{def:typed-unary-admissible-source}), functionally
closed partial transition-enriched hidden structure.
Before introducing two-root constraints, its full
one-generated induced diagrams are already actual
completed hidden diagrams by the explicit
unary-admissibility hypothesis, and have size at most
\(m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) by
\cref{lem:typed-unary-closure-bound}. Thus ALL intended
unary function, transition and functional-identity
equations hold literally in \(C\) on every
one-generated closure. An arbitrary partial source
FAILING this hypothesis is NOT covered by this
guarded-lift construction or by the uniform
bounded-CLOSED-obstruction theorem below: its
one-generated closure can be arbitrarily large.
Such sources are excluded by condition (ii) in the
eventual HN local-finiteness test, as checked explicitly
in \cref{thm:typed-direct-irreducible-unary-HN}.
After this initial gate, test all bounded
ACTUALLY joined multi-root semantic-cylinder,
old-tuple and relation patterns as below.
Since every real sort and every
represented quotient sort is transitive and all unary coordinate terms are
\(0\)-definable, every prospective representative of a valid root realises the
same one-root diagram.  In particular, a unary self-equation or a relation
entirely internal to one functional closure needs no artificial two-witness
encoding.

Perform the analogous bounded check on every ACTUAL displayed datum
joining distinct OLD hidden source vertices: take the unary-functional
closure of its complete SOURCE support, which is irreducible because
a displayed relation tuple contains all its specified joining roots,
and require the induced hidden diagram on THIS irreducible
closed source support to occur in a full typed expansion.
This is exactly the valid case of
\cref{lem:typed-joined-source-support}.
In particular a relation only between proper quotient
term values of otherwise unjoined real roots does
NOT license completion of their reducible real two-root diagram
(see \cref{rem:typed-term-join-not-irreducible}).
All constraints below are attached to their ACTUAL old
displayed source endpoint vertices, not to arbitrary pairs
of real roots whose unary terms happen to be related.  For a displayed old relation of arity \(r\), do this on the union
of the \(r\) one-generated closures of its support.  The maximum arity and
\(m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) are fixed, so every failure again has a uniform bounded
witness.  These checks include reflection: a mandatory cylinder, term
equality, or canonical old tuple type which is absent from the partial source
is a malformed local diagram just as much as a wrong positive symbol is.
In particular, if TWO DISTINCT source vertices \(b\ne c\)
belong to the SAME represented proper quotient sort
\(B_{a,J}\), a displayed relation whose actual
quotient map is the IDENTITY cannot demand
\(b\mapsto c\): such a map would force their
equality in every completed hidden structure,
contradicting injectivity of a hidden
homomorphism-embedding. This is a bounded
two-generated identity/equality defect,
not a positive strong-diversity theta constraint.
When the two occurrences denote the SAME old
hidden vertex, the identity holds inside its
already checked one-generated unary closure.
The reduction
\cref{lem:typed-identity-transport-redundant}
guarantees that all identity-containing
relational transport cases fall into these
two alternatives.

Give every old real vertex its own real witness and every old proper coordinate
vertex a designated prospective real representative in its underlying real
sort.  For displayed data whose endpoint hidden vertices are distinct, impose
on the corresponding pair of witnesses all applicable positive profiles:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item a projection equation to a \(J\)-coordinate imposes \(J\);
\item an upward quotient equation from a \(J\)-coordinate to a
      \(K\)-coordinate imposes \(K\);
\item a NONTRIVIAL named quotient-transition
      equation \(\pi_{R,J}(b)=c\) imposes
      the IDENTITY-FREE reachable graph profile
      \(J^\circ\starprod R\starprod(J^R)^\circ\) from
      \cref{lem:typed-transition-cylinder};
      identity-containing \(R\) is redundant by
      \cref{lem:typed-identity-transport-redundant}
      and is checked as a bounded unary
      functional-identity datum instead;
\item a displayed semantic cylinder imposes its named cylinder profile;
\item a specified old real atomic pair type \(t\) imposes \(\{t\}\).
\end{enumerate}
For each genuinely IRREDUCIBLE
one- or two-generated OLD
source support already joined
by a displayed relation datum,
take the WHOLE locally vetted
COMPLETE induced closed hidden
diagram, not merely the first
primitive joining relation.
Apply the complete two-root
comparison only when the
corresponding induced
\(\cl_C\{b,c\}\) is actually
irreducible; the test is
justified by
\cref{lem:typed-joined-source-support},
not by a mere cross relation
between unary term values.
Any original one-root projection
or unary term identity stays
inside its own checked closure.
For every ordered pair of
unary TERM VALUES from these
two closures, impose on the
two designated real ROOT
representatives the POSITIVE
pullback profile of its
mandated complete named
cylinder, quotient-class
equality, or original
real atomic pair type.
This is a FINITE list:
\cref{lem:typed-unary-closure-bound}
bounds the available unary
term functions and closures,
and the old named sorts/atom
palettes are finite.

Each such term-pair
preimage profile is a
NONEMPTY positive STRONG
reachable spectrum by the
direct complete-orbital
pullback theorem
\cref{lem:typed-term-pair-orbit-pullback}.
This uses that the mandatory
named comparison in the
complete OLD support is a
SINGLE actual hidden
semantic-cylinder orbital
(or a named quotient
transition graph/equality),
and that its term functions
have proper represented
real kernels.
The pullback is exactly
ONE old representative
cylinder
\(\operatorname{Cyl}_{J,K}(t_0)\),
not a complement, not an
uncontrolled union and not
an arbitrary product of
independently selected
representative types.
Its equality-containing
logical-Id exceptional case
is handled as a bounded
OLD real identity defect
or a one-root unary
equation, never by a
synthetic STRONG identity.
This is the explicit
binary positivity interface
required by the guarded
lift construction.

When the local source diagram
has only one root occurrence,
all identities are already
checked in its one-generated
unary closure. For an UNJOINED
pair of closures, do not
insert negative cross
constraints or arbitrarily
choose a completion cylinder:
homomorphism-embeddings are
not required to reflect
absent relations between
different irreducible
components.

Keep every displayed complete old higher-support factor distinguished; its
complete canonical pair shadow is therefore already among the pair constraints
above.  On each constrained OLD witness pair \((b,c)\), the bounded
complete-pattern test has already certified ONE irreducible OLD source
support \(\mathfrak S_{bc}=\cl_C\{b,c\}\), on which ALL imposed term-pair
comparisons hold together.  The direct common-survivor argument of
\cref{lem:typed-one-source-support-per-guarded-pair} (proved immediately
below WITHOUT using this exact-domain intersection) therefore produces
ONE original fine diversity atom belonging to EVERY imposed positive
profile on this pair.  In particular their total intersection is
NONEMPTY, not merely pairwise intersecting.  If the OLD complete-pattern
test fails, its bounded irreducible source support is already a
non-completable witness, so the construction stops before this stage.
Since the imposed spectra are positive typed reachable profiles,
their nonempty finite intersection \(D\) is a typed strong exact domain
by \cref{lem:typed-exact-domain-calculus}.  This common-survivor
existence step does NOT invoke typed 2-Helly; strong Helly remains
essential elsewhere for exact product algebra and theta completion.
Attach a fixed private typed theta bundle realising \(D\), and record
the full transition-closed root signature
from \cref{def:typed-transition-root-signature}.  Denote the resulting
visible guarded network, together with its distinguished higher-support
factors, by \(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\).
\end{construction}

declarations.title: A single irreducible OLD source support for each guarded pair
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[A single irreducible OLD source support for each guarded pair]
\label{lem:typed-one-source-support-per-guarded-pair}
In the BINARY terminal construction
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift},
let \((b,c)\) be a pair of
DISTINCT actual old hidden
source vertices on whose
prospective real witness pair
the construction imposes at
least one positive root
constraint. Then all profiles
imposed on this SAME witness
pair are consequences of
the ONE induced old
functionally closed diagram
\[
                   \mathfrak S_{bc}=\cl_C\{b,c\},
\]
which is irreducible in the
PARTIAL OLD hidden source
language and has at most
\(2m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) old
vertices. The construction's
complete-pattern check
therefore requires \(\mathfrak S_{bc}\)
itself to be a completed
induced hidden member.
Consequently ONE embedding
of \(\mathfrak S_{bc}\) into a full
hidden expansion, followed
by distinct real
representative selection,
provides an old fine atomic
pair \(t\) lying
SIMULTANEOUSLY in EVERY
positive profile imposed on
\((b,c)\).

This is not asserted for
an arbitrary pair of
OLD root ancestors \(b,c\)
whose descendants
\(\tau(b),\sigma(c)\) are
related in \(C\): unless
\(b,c\) themselves are
joined by displayed unary
or binary source data,
the guarded construction
issues NO forced
complete-pair spectrum on
their witness pair.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Private theta cycles have OLD source endpoints
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Private theta cycles have OLD source endpoints]
\label{lem:typed-private-theta-cycle}
Let \(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\) be the visible
network of \cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.
Every positive root-pair constraint
is issued with an ACTUAL OLD hidden
source endpoint pair and is realised
by a finite theta network whose
interior vertices are disjoint from
all old root witnesses and from
all other private interiors. The
only specified incidences of a
private interior with vertices
outside its own theta are at the
two designated OLD root witnesses.
Consequently, every specified simple
cycle of \(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\) either
is contained in one private theta,
or traverses any theta which it
meets outside its root vertices
along a COMPLETE branch from
one designated OLD root witness
to the other, without repeated
interior vertices. Upon contracting
these branches, the endpoints
and the root-signature anchors of
EVERY macro side belong to the
ORIGINAL partial hidden source.
This is independent of which
completion atom will later be
chosen on any unrecorded root pair.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Uniform size of complete typed two-root gadgets
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform size of complete typed two-root gadgets]
\label{lem:typed-two-root-uniform-size}
There is a finite integer
\(B_{\mathrm{pair}}\), depending
ONLY on the fixed finite typed
hidden language and its original
finite typed strong exact-domain
families, such that each locally
admissible TWO-generated joined
hidden diagram from
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}
has an equivalent guarded
two-real-root constraint
represented by one nonempty
exact-domain theta network
with at most \(B_{\mathrm{pair}}\)
formal vertices.
This includes ALL mandated
named pair relations between
values of unary terms in the
two root closures and
does not presume an unbounded
choice of representative
points or transition words.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Two-generated hidden reflection is an atomic-root test
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Two-generated hidden reflection is an atomic-root test]
\label{lem:typed-two-root-complete-reflection}
Work in the terminal typed hidden signature
with its FINITE family of real and
proper quotient sorts, unary projections,
upward maps, quotient transitions,
and complete named semantic cylinders.
Let \(b,c\) be TWO distinct root
positions of a finite functionally
closed PARTIAL hidden structure.
Assume their one-generated closures
and the full induced diagram on
each ACTUALLY IRREDUCIBLE
two-generated OLD source support
passed the bounded complete-pattern
test of
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift},
as warranted by
\cref{lem:typed-joined-source-support}.
Suppose some displayed datum
joins the two closures in an
IRREDUCIBLE source piece.
Let \(D_{bc}\) be the nonempty
intersection of ALL positive
typed representative-pair profiles
imposed by those data, as in
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.

Then EVERY actual old diversity
atom \(t\in D_{bc}\) on the
two chosen distinct real
representatives interprets
the same COMPLETE named
two-generated hidden diagram
on the source one-generated
closures: it preserves and
reflects all displayed unary
term equalities, projection
and quotient-transition values,
named semantic-cylinder
relations, and complete old
real pair atomic colours.
The same conclusion applies
to each binary pair inside a
distinguished higher-support
complete OLD source factor;
the support-\(\ge3\) tuples
themselves remain conditional
on the separately stated
support-normal completion
interface.

No claim is made that
an UNJOINED pair of old
hidden root closures must
have its absent binary
relations reflected:
homomorphism-embeddings
allow different irreducible
components to gain
new cross relations and,
where permitted, overlap
outside their common base.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Typed guarded root forcing and lift equivalence
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed guarded root forcing and lift equivalence]
\label{lem:typed-guarded-lift-equivalence}
Let \(C\) be as in \cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}, and suppose the
construction reaches \(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\) rather than stopping at a
pairwise profile conflict.  Every visible completion of
\(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\) canonically realises all displayed positive typed
hidden data and all transition-closed root identities.  Moreover,
\(C\) has a hidden completion if and only if
\(G_{\mathrm{typ}}(C)\) has a visible completion (with the distinguished
old higher-support factors kept fixed in the support-normal finite-arity
case).  In particular, hidden non-completion implies visible guarded-lift
non-completion.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Literal old-coordinate seams for successive macro sides
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Literal old-coordinate seams for successive macro sides]
\label{lem:typed-old-seam-telescope}
Let \(C\) be a functionally closed
PARTIAL old hidden structure,
and let \(b_0,\ldots,b_m\)
be a sequence of ACTUAL OLD
hidden source vertex occurrences
with consecutive pairs
\((b_{i-1},b_i)\) issuing
source-supported guarded macro
sides. For each side suppose
\cref{lem:typed-old-source-branch-equation}
provides a literal equation
\[
 \pi_i(\tau_{i-1}(b_{i-1}))
       =\tau_i(b_i)
\]
between NAMED OLD unary-term
values at represented quotient
coordinates \(J_{i-1},J_i\).
Here at a shared intermediate
root \(b_i\) both incident sides
must use the SAME represented
\(J_i\)-coordinate readout,
possibly written by two terms
which are IDENTICALLY the same
canonical quotient map in the
actual hidden signature.

Then their composite equation
\[
 (\pi_m\circ\cdots\circ\pi_1)
    (\tau_0(b_0))=\tau_m(b_m)
\tag{OSE}\label{eq:typed-old-seam-telescope}
\]
holds LITERALLY in \(C\),
regardless of whether the
complete irreducible OLD
supports of two successive
sides have any common REAL
vertex. Their intersection may
consist solely of proper
quotient-coordinate vertices.

The conclusion cannot be
obtained merely because two
DISTINCT OLD hidden source
vertices \(q,q'\) happen to
have EQUAL images in some
homomorphism-embedding completion.
They may be used as one seam
only if their equality is
already literal in \(C\), or
an explicitly displayed NAMED
unary transition in the OLD
source connects their required
coordinate values.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: A strong idempotent has an exact RAW equivalence envelope
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[A strong idempotent has an exact RAW equivalence envelope]
\label{lem:typed-idempotent-raw-exact}
Let \(a\) be an actual named transitive
sort of a finite complete homogeneous
symmetric binary SAP+semantic-CCO
source. Let \(e\in\Rch^{aa}\) be a
NONEMPTY strong diversity profile
of one positive typed atomic word
\(w:a\to a\), and suppose
\(e\starprod e=e\).
Then
\[
                 E_e=\Id_a\cup e
\]
is not merely an invariant
equivalence: it is an actual
FULL RAW exact equivalence,
represented by the equality-inclusive
endpoint word \(ww\).
Consequently, in the finite
distributive lattice of represented
full exact equivalences on \(a\),
\[
 E_e=\bigcap\{J:J\text{ is a represented
 meet-irreducible equivalence and }
                         J\supseteq E_e\}.
\tag{TF1}\label{eq:typed-idempotent-MI-meet}
\]
The intersection of an empty family
is the universal same-sort equivalence.
Neither a synthetic equality-labelled
diversity edge nor an unproved
exactness of EVERY invariant
equivalence is used.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Scope of the RAW exact idempotent envelope
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{remark}[Scope of the RAW exact idempotent envelope]
\label{rem:typed-idempotent-envelope-scope}
The preceding equation
\(R_w;R_w=\Id\cup e\)
uses only symmetric original
pair orbitals, source transitivity,
the STRONG endpoint identity
\(e\starprod e=e\), and SAP
injectivisation of RAW walks.
It does NOT require the
terminal no-finite-cover
hypothesis or a priori
exactness of every invariant
equivalence. Its assertion
that \(E_e\) is FULL RAW exact
comes from the literal
positive old word \(ww\).
The subsequent representation
of \(E_e\) as the meet of
represented meet-irreducibles
uses the separate FINITE
DISTRIBUTIVE exact-lattice
theorem from Part~I; this
extra deduction must not
be conflated with the direct
word identity.
\end{remark}

declarations.title: CCO-free idempotent lattice and its distributive CCO specialization
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[CCO-free idempotent lattice and its distributive CCO specialization]
\label{lem:typed-strong-idempotent-lattice-monolith}
Fix ONE original named TRANSITIVE sort $a$
of a finite-complete homogeneous
binary source whose same-sort old
atom colours are SYMMETRIC.
Assume visible SAP and FULL
original invariant-equivalence NR2
on that sort, but do NOT assume CCO.
Let $\mathscr I_a$ be the set
of all NONEMPTY same-sort
STRONG POSITIVE REACHABLE
word profiles
$e\in\Rch^{aa}$ with
$e\starprod e=e$.
Then
\[
                  e\longmapsto
                    E_e=\Id_a\cup e
\]
is an order-preserving BIJECTION
from $\mathscr I_a$ onto the
finite lattice of ALL original
invariant equivalences
on $a$ EXCLUDING $\Id_a$.
In particular $\mathscr I_a$
is a finite LATTICE with
\[
  e\wedge f=e\cap f\ne\varnothing,
  \qquad
  e\vee f=e\starprod f
             =(E_e\vee E_f)^\circ .
 \tag{IL}\label{eq:typed-strong-idempotent-lattice}
\]
It has a UNIQUE least nonzero
idempotent $e_{0,a}=L_a^\circ$,
where $L_a>\Id_a$ is the
SAP-monolith, and
\[
       e_{0,a}\subseteq e,\qquad
       e_{0,a}\starprod e
                   =e\starprod e_{0,a}=e
       \quad(e\in\mathscr I_a).
\]
If the original source ALSO has
semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO,
this finite lattice is moreover
DISTRIBUTIVE by original FULL
RAW exact-ball Helly and CRT.
Thus the BIJECTION, NONEMPTY
MEETS and common monolith
hold even in a symmetric
SAP+NR2 source which is
NOT CCO; only distributivity
uses the additional CCO input.

The element $e_{0,a}$ acts as
a unit ONLY inside the
idempotent lattice, NOT on
arbitrary reachable profiles.
This does NOT turn OLD G5
idempotent interval certificates
for the generally COARSER
$E_e$ into an unsupported
$L_a$-equality certificate.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Quotient-functional branches are visible at their hidden roots
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Quotient-functional branches are visible at their hidden roots]
\label{lem:typed-branch-root-visibility}
Let \(b,c\) be two distinct hidden root positions,
each either a real root or a proper represented quotient
root. Write \(H_b,H_c\) for the equivalence kernels
of their designated real representatives:
\(H_b=\Id\) for a real root and its original
represented proper meet-irreducible for a quotient
root; similarly for \(c\). Let \(D\) be the
nonempty exact pair menu imposed by the
complete locally valid two-root hidden pattern.
Thus
\[
              H_b;D;H_c=D .
\tag{TV1}\label{eq:typed-anchored-bisaturation}
\]
Suppose a positive typed branch profile \(P\)
in a theta presentation contains \(D\), and
\(P;P^\smile\subseteq J\) for a represented
proper meet-irreducible \(J\) at its source.
Let \(J^P\) be the transported target equivalence.
Then
\[
                  H_b\le J,\qquad
                  H_c\le J^P .
\tag{TV2}\label{eq:typed-branch-visible-kernels}
\]
Consequently the quotient transition forced by
\(P\) is an equality of named unary term values
already in the finite functionally closed
two-root hidden substructure; it does
\emph{not} require naming the \(J\)-coordinate
of an independently chosen, unconstrained
auxiliary representative.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Original-source equations for quotient-functional theta branches
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Original-source equations for quotient-functional theta branches]
\label{lem:typed-old-source-branch-equation}
Let \((b,c)\) be one ACTUAL
old hidden endpoint pair on which
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}
issues a nonempty exact visible
root menu \(D_{bc}\). Let \(H_b,H_c\)
be the original representative kernels.
Suppose \(P\in\Rch^{ab}\) is a
positive branch profile in its
private theta presentation, with
\(D_{bc}\subseteq P\), and let
\(J\) be a represented proper
meet-irreducible with
\(P;P^\smile\subseteq J\).

Then the \(J\)-coordinate of
\(b\) and the transported \(J^P\)
coordinate of \(c\) are NAMED
unary terms of the OLD source
vertices, and the equation
\[
  \pi_{P,J}(\tau_J(b))
           =\tau_{J^P}(c)
\tag{TOE}\label{eq:typed-old-source-branch-equation}
\]
already holds as a LITERAL
unary-term identity in the
original functionally closed
partial hidden structure \(C\).
Here \(\pi_{P,J}\) denotes the
existing named atomic transition
representing the quotient map
of \(P\). The conclusion remains
valid when \(D_{bc}\) is a MEET
of several original profiles,
none of which individually has
\(J\)-functional fibres.

The conclusion applies only to
the source-supported root-pair
gadgets specified in
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.
No such equation is inferred
from an arbitrarily selected
new completion type on an
UNJOINED pair of hidden roots.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Off-diagonal idempotent interval reinsertion
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Off-diagonal idempotent interval reinsertion]
\label{lem:typed-idempotent-reinsert}
Let \(w\) be a positive composable typed diversity word
whose STRONG endpoint profile is a nonempty same-sort
idempotent \(e=e\starprod e\). Let \(x,y\) be
\emph{distinct actual real vertices} of its common endpoint
sort. If \(xE_ey\), where \(E_e=\Id\cup e\) is
the actual equivalence of
\eqref{eq:typed-idempotent-equivalence}, then the
entire word \(w\) can be realised between \(x,y\)
with all path interiors new, preserving the
already completed finite old structure on its roots.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Simultaneous private word insertion over a complete old base
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous private word insertion over a complete old base]
\label{lem:typed-simultaneous-word-insertion}
Let \(A\) be a finite COMPLETE
visible member of the original
typed SAP+CCO age. Fix a finite
list of old typed diversity
atomic words \(w_i\), each
with two specified DISTINCT
endpoint vertices \(p_i,q_i\in A\)
of the required endpoint sorts.
Suppose
\[
 \col_A(p_i,q_i)\in\Prof(w_i)
\]
for every \(i\), where
\(\Prof(w_i)\) is the genuine
STRONG simple-path endpoint
profile of that particular
original atomic word.
Then a single finite complete
visible member \(B\supseteq A\)
realises ALL words \(w_i\)
between the prescribed endpoints,
with every word's interior
pairwise distinct and with
interiors of different words
disjoint from each other and
from \(A\). Every originally
specified atom on \(A\) is
preserved literally. The
endpoint pairs may overlap
with each other inside \(A\).
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: OLD boundary coordinate certificate for one deleted idempotent gap
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[OLD boundary coordinate certificate for one deleted idempotent gap]
\label{lem:typed-old-gap-boundary-certificate}
Let \(C\) be a finite
UNARY-FUNCTIONALLY CLOSED
partial terminal typed
hidden source whose
one-generated diagrams
and every ACTUALLY
joined irreducible
two-root source support
have passed the COMPLETE
bounded local test of
\cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.
Suppose
\[
 b_0 \ \xrightarrow{P_1}\
 b_1\ \xrightarrow{P_2}\
 \cdots\ \xrightarrow{P_m}\ b_m
\]
is one original
source-supported
composable macro
subpath with distinct
formal OLD root
vertices \(b_i\).
Each \(P_i\) is the
NONEMPTY positive
STRONG profile of the
ACTUAL traversed
private branch, and
the original source
exact pair menu on
\((b_{i-1},b_i)\)
is \(D_i\subseteq P_i\).
Assume
\[
       P_1\starprod
           \cdots\starprod P_m=e,
       \qquad e\ne\varnothing,
       \qquad e\starprod e=e
\]
with endpoints of the
same original sort \(a\).
Let
\(E_e=\Id_a\cup e\).

For EVERY represented
proper meet-irreducible
\(J\supseteq E_e\),
there are named unary
term functions
\(\tau_{0,J},\tau_{m,J}\)
on the OLD source
endpoints \(b_0,b_m\)
whose values are their
represented \(J\)-coordinates
and satisfy
\[
             \tau_{0,J}(b_0)
                        =\tau_{m,J}(b_m)
\tag{OGC}\label{eq:typed-old-gap-certificate}
\]
as LITERAL equality of
vertices of the ORIGINAL
partial source \(C\).
This equality survives
in the induced closed
substructure
\(\cl_C\{b_0,b_m\}\).

Consequently, for ANY
homomorphism-embedding
completion of that
retained boundary
substructure, the
chosen original real
representatives of
\(b_0,b_m\) have an
actual pair relation
in the FULL RAW exact
equivalence \(E_e\).
If the representatives
are distinct, their
original fine diversity
atom belongs to the
STRONG profile \(e\).
The same conclusion
holds when \(E_e=\Top_a\),
with the empty family
of \(J\)-equalities
interpreted as the
universal relation.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed compressed guarded macro path
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Typed compressed guarded macro path]
\label{lem:typed-factor-path}
Work in the binary terminal guarded-lift setting after the bounded
one-/two-root source tests of \cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.
Let \(P_1\cdots P_n\), with \(n\ge1\), be a source-supported positive
macro path with pairwise distinct formal OLD root vertices, as obtained from the
complementary path of a specified simple cycle. Put
\(h=3|S_{\rm typ}|\).

There is a compression in the typed hidden language with at most \(2^h\) retained original macro letters
and at most \(2^{h+1}\) OLD root vertices. Their induced unary closure
retains the complete source support of each retained letter and the
literal boundary certificates of all deleted idempotent intervals.
Every hidden completion of this retained source permits reconstruction
of the original macro path after choosing distinct real representatives
of the retained roots by \cref{lem:typed-real-sort-splitting}.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: No zero-valued composable positive typed macro interval
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[No zero-valued composable positive typed macro interval]
\label{lem:typed-composable-products-nonzero}
In an actual homogeneous
named-sorted complete binary
SAP source, let
\(P\subseteq M_a\times M_b\)
and \(Q\subseteq M_b\times M_c\)
be NONEMPTY invariant
DIVERSITY pair palettes
of the indicated types.
Then their genuine STRONG
three-distinct-vertex
product is nonempty:
\[
                    P\starprod Q\ne\varnothing .
\]
Consequently the product of
EVERY nonempty contiguous
subword of a composable
positive typed macro word
is nonzero. In the typed
semigroup
\(S_{\rm typ}=\{0\}
 \sqcup\bigsqcup_{a,b}\Rch^{ab}\),
the adjoined zero can occur
on NONCOMPOSABLE typed inputs,
but NEVER at a node of a
factorisation forest built on
one actual composable positive
macro path.
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Partition and simultaneous reconstruction of a pruned OLD cycle
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Partition and simultaneous reconstruction of a pruned OLD cycle]
\label{lem:typed-pruned-cycle-reconstruction}
Consider a SPECIFIED SIMPLE cycle
\(Z\) of a binary guarded lift which
is not confined to one private theta.
Choose one original complete atomic
theta branch as a fixed anchor;
the complementary side contracts to
a typed macro word
\(P_1\cdots P_n\) with ACTUAL OLD
source root witnesses
\(v_0,\ldots,v_n\), pairwise distinct
along the complementary path.
For each macro letter \(P_i\),
remember the ONE ORIGINAL selected
positive atomic branch word \(w_i\)
traversed by \(Z\); thus
\(\Prof(w_i)=P_i\).

Apply a factorisation forest to
\(P_1\cdots P_n\).
By
\cref{lem:typed-composable-products-nonzero},
EVERY subtree value of this
composable positive word
is NONZERO; in particular
no unbounded-arity node
can have the adjoined
zero as its idempotent.
Recursively keep
both children of every binary node,
and the first and last children of
every node with at least three
children of one idempotent value.
When middle children are discarded,
STOP recursion on those children,
and record the corresponding whole
contiguous original interval word
with its two OLD boundary roots.

Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The retained original macro
letters and the maximal recorded
deleted intervals form a DISJOINT
ordered partition of the original
complementary macro path. The two
boundary roots of every deleted
interval occur among endpoints of
the retained macro letters. No
boundary vertex is introduced
after taking an OLD source induced
substructure.
\item Every maximal deleted
interval has nonzero STRONG
idempotent product \(e\), so its
whole ORIGINAL concatenated
atomic branch word has the
strong endpoint profile \(e\).
\item Let \(A\) be ANY finite
COMPLETE old visible structure
containing pairwise distinct
representatives of ALL retained
OLD source root vertices, with
the fine atomic pair on each
retained macro side lying in its
ORIGINAL \(P_i\), and with the
boundary pair of each deleted
interval of value \(e\) lying in
\(E_e=\Id\cup e\).
ALSO assume that the fine atom
of the two anchor endpoints
belongs to the STRONG endpoint
profile of the EXACT fixed
original anchor branch word.
Then the cycle \(Z\) can be
recreated as a specified
SIMPLE positive atomic cycle
inside one finite complete old
visible extension of \(A\),
provided each root pair of \(Z\)
is represented by the same
chosen root points in \(A\).

Only the last implication uses
visible SAP; it imposes NO
condition on newly chosen fine
cross colours between interiors
of distinct inserted words.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

proofs.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure

declarations.title: Uniformly bounded ORIGINAL hidden anchor support
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Uniformly bounded ORIGINAL hidden anchor support]
\label{lem:typed-forest-old-anchor-bound}
Work in the BINARY guarded-lift
setting after the bounded
one-/two-root OLD source tests
of \cref{con:typed-guarded-lift}.
Put \(s=|S_{\rm typ}|\),
\(h=3s\), and let
\(m_{\mathrm{typ}}\) be the
one-generated hidden
unary-closure bound of
\cref{lem:typed-unary-closure-bound}.
For any specified simple
bad cycle in the guarded
visible network, choose one
original private atomic
branch as a fixed anchor
and contract the complementary
private branch traversals
to a typed macro path.
After the idempotent-node
pruning used in
\cref{lem:typed-factor-path},
there is a set \(B\) of
ACTUAL OLD hidden source
vertices such that:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(B\) contains the
two original root positions
of the fixed anchor branch,
the endpoints of every
retained macro side, and
both boundary roots of
every deleted idempotent
interval; all ORIGINAL
unary term values of
these vertices belong to
\(\cl_C(B)\).
\item Every retained
macro-side spectrum is
supported inside the
induced OLD partial
diagram on \(\cl_C(B)\),
including its complete
irreducible old pair
support. Every deleted
idempotent interval has
the same endpoint
represented-MI term
equalities already
LITERALLY in that
induced OLD diagram.
\item One may choose
\[
 \bigl|\cl_C(B)\bigr|
   \le m_{\mathrm{typ}}
               (2^{h+3}+4).
\tag{OAB}\label{eq:typed-forest-old-anchor-bound}
\]
No term-value vertex newly
created by a subsequent
visible completion is included
among these OLD anchors.
\end{enumerate}

The claim concerns this
retained OLD hidden support
and its literal partial
relations; it does NOT
assert that this partial
support is itself a
completed hidden member.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Typed bounded hidden obstructions
declarations.heading: Typed terminal transfer via quotient-transition closure
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Typed bounded hidden obstructions]
\label{cor:typed-bounded-hidden}
There is a constant \(N_{\mathrm{typ}}\), depending only on the
finite terminal typed hidden language, such that every
NON-COMPLETABLE UNARY-ADMISSIBLE
(\cref{def:typed-unary-admissible-source})
finite functionally closed PARTIAL transition-enriched
hidden structure contains a non-completable induced
functionally closed substructure on at most
\(N_{\mathrm{typ}}\) vertices.

The qualifier is ESSENTIAL: the assertion is FALSE for
arbitrary total-unary partial sources, which may contain
arbitrarily long malformed cycles of named mutually
inverse quotient-transition functions.
\end{corollary}

declarations.title: Exact real-root closure and point-generated cofinality
declarations.heading: Typed terminal Ramsey conclusion and finite-cover transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Exact real-root closure and point-generated cofinality]
\label{lem:typed-real-root-closure-cofinal}
Let $\widehat{\M}$ be the actual terminal completed
transition-enriched hidden structure, with its original real sorts
and named proper MI quotient sorts. Assume the literal unary
signature of Part~III: nonidentity real-source maps project to
proper quotients, and the remaining nonidentity maps are upward
maps or quotient transitions, with no real-valued map from a
quotient sort. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every finite set $D$ of original real points,
\[
       \cl_{\widehat{\M}}(D)\cap M_{\mathrm{real}}=D.
\tag{RCF}\label{eq:typed-real-root-closure}
\]
\item Every finite induced unary-closed completed hidden
substructure $B\subseteq\widehat{\M}$ is contained inducedly
in a finite point-generated substructure
$\cl_{\widehat{\M}}(D)$. One may take $D$ to contain the real
points of $B$ and one actual real representative of each proper
quotient vertex of $B$.
\item Every linear order on $B$ extends to a linear order on
this finite $\cl_{\widehat{\M}}(D)$.
\end{enumerate}
No automorphism section or SAP over an orphan-only base is
required. The no-real-output hypothesis is substantive: adding
a unary selector from a proper quotient back to a real point
could invalidate (i).
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Finite full-code hidden order readout on original real sorts
declarations.heading: Typed terminal Ramsey conclusion and finite-cover transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Finite full-code hidden order readout on original real sorts]
\label{lem:typed-finite-ordered-real-readout}
For each original named real sort $a$, choose a finite list
$\mathcal T_a$ representing all applicable unary term functions
in the terminal typed hidden signature, including the identity
real-root term, as supplied by
\cref{lem:typed-unary-closure-bound,lem:typed-coordinate-normal-form}.
For every ordered pair of real sorts $a,b$ and terms
$\tau\in\mathcal T_a$, $\sigma\in\mathcal T_b$, add the binary
comparison predicate
\[
 C_{\tau,\sigma}(x,y)
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \tau(x)<\sigma(y).
\tag{TOR}\label{eq:typed-ordered-real-readout}
\]
The tuples $x=y$ are included: terms with different hidden
values may give a true diagonal comparison, so these added
binary predicates need not be irreflexive.

The resulting finite relational expansion satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every finite original real $A$, its point-generated
hidden closure $\widehat A$ is determined up to unique
isomorphism over $A$ by the original atomic unary, pair and
equality types. These determine all hidden term equalities,
unary-function values and complete named semantic-cylinder
relations.
\item A linear order on $\widehat A$ is determined exactly by
its comparison predicates. More precisely, put
\[
 T_A=\{(x,\tau):x\in A,\ \tau\in\mathcal T_{\operatorname{sort}(x)}\},
 \qquad Q_A=T_A/{\equiv_A},
\]
where $(x,\tau)\equiv_A(y,\sigma)$ means equality of their
hidden term values, determined by the old atomic types.
A comparison list is compatible precisely when
\[
 [(x,\tau)]<[(y,\sigma)]
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C_{\tau,\sigma}(x,y)
\]
defines a strict linear order on $Q_A$, including the tuples
$x=y$. Every embedding of real readout expansions
$f:A^*\to B^*$ extends uniquely to an ordered hidden embedding
$\widehat f:\widehat A\to\widehat B$, and conversely every
such hidden embedding restricts to a real readout embedding.
\item The expansion is precompact and reasonable: there are
finitely many expansions of each finite $A$, and along every
old embedding $A\hookrightarrow B$ every order on $\widehat A$
extends to an order on $\widehat B$.
\item If the hereditary ordered hidden envelope is Ramsey,
then the finite real readout class is Ramsey.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Diagonal term-order comparisons are already necessary with one MI
declarations.heading: Typed terminal Ramsey conclusion and finite-cover transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{example}[Diagonal term-order comparisons are already necessary with one MI]
\label{ex:typed-diagonal-term-order-necessary}
Let $M$ be the countable
homogeneous one-sort
structure with ONE
nontrivial equivalence E,
infinitely many infinite
E-classes, and the COMPLETE
symmetric binary old
diversity colours
$p$ (distinct same-class
pairs) and $q$
(different-class pairs).
This original source has
SAP, triangle-defined age
and semantic homomorphic
CCO, with FULL original
NR2.

Its actual MI-only hidden
signature has one original
REAL sort M and the
proper quotient sort
$Q=M/E$, with the
named unary projection
$F_E:M\to Q$. For the
SINGLE original real
point $A=\{x\}$,
the point-generated
hidden closure contains
the TWO DISTINCT
hidden vertices
\[
                       x,\qquad F_E(x).
\]
There are two possible
strict linear orders
on this hidden closure:
$x<F_E(x)$ and
$F_E(x)<x$. They give
the SAME old real
one-point diagram and
there are NO pairs of
DISTINCT original real
vertices on which an
off-diagonal term-order
readout could distinguish
the two orders. But
\[
   C_{\operatorname{id},F_E}(x,x)
       \Longleftrightarrow x<F_E(x)
\]
distinguishes them
immediately. Therefore
one cannot delete
diagonal comparisons
$x=y$ from
\eqref{eq:typed-ordered-real-readout},
even with ONE original
real sort, ONE proper
MI quotient and NO
mixed original-sort
transports.
\end{example}

declarations.title: Actual terminal hidden orbit completeness gives irreducibility
declarations.heading: Typed terminal Ramsey conclusion and finite-cover transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Actual terminal hidden orbit completeness gives irreducibility]
\label{lem:typed-terminal-hidden-irreducible}
In the ACTUAL finite
terminal MI-only hidden
signature, take ALL old
original real sorts,
proper represented
MI quotient sorts,
named unary projections,
upward maps and quotient
transitions, all named
old fine atomic
real-pair predicates,
and the FULL named
semantic-cylinder
binary orbital partition
on every ordered
sort-pair containing
at least one proper
quotient sort, as in
\cref{lem:typed-cylinder-realisation}.
Then EVERY finite induced
UNARY-CLOSED completed
hidden substructure is
IRREDUCIBLE in its
ORIGINAL hidden language,
without adjoining
a universal $E_*$ edge.

This statement concerns
ACTUAL complete hidden
orbitals and named unary
graphs, not an arbitrary
reduct retaining only
selected cylinders.
\end{lemma}

declarations.title: Terminal typed Ramsey expansion
declarations.heading: Typed terminal Ramsey conclusion and finite-cover transfer
declarations.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Terminal typed Ramsey expansion]
\label{thm:internal-ramsey-terminal}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite-sorted homogeneous complete binary
triangle-constrained class with SAP and semantic homomorphic CCO, such that
every proper same-sort invariant-equivalence cover has infinite relative
index. Then $\mathcal C$ admits a finite relational precompact Ramsey
expansion. Its added comparison predicates record a linear order on the
point-generated transition-enriched hidden coordinate system.
\end{theorem}
